auto-778976f3f4af.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin set for rare three-way meeting in Shenzhen
auto-778976f3f4af.summary:
The White House says the leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, later next week. Officials said nuclear arms reduction would be on the agenda, with Iran possibly raised too, but Ukraine would be avoided. Russia has confirmed the meeting, while Beijing has not yet publicly confirmed it. A senior US official said no agreement was expected.

The talks follow the expiry of the New START nuclear treaty between Washington and Moscow in February, leaving the largest arsenals without binding limits. Analysts note that Beijing is wary of being tied to Russia's war in Ukraine and of the 'new Yalta' comparison.

Gains a major diplomatic platform alongside the US and China
Seeks nuclear arms talks but faces criticism over softening toward Moscow

impact_points: China, as host, faces awkward optics and possible strain with the EU if Ukraine is discussed without Europeans present.
Russia gains a diplomatic showcase alongside the US and China, while Ukraine's Zelenskyy has voiced concern about being sidelined.

auto-33d06d12e622.headline: ASEAN opens Manila summit amid Myanmar talks and wider regional agenda
auto-33d06d12e622.summary: Southeast Asian leaders opened their 49th annual summit in Manila, the Philippine capital, on Sunday, with the meetings running through November 17. Discussions cover energy and food security, trade and conflict, including the war in Iran. Leaders agreed to keep Myanmar's military-backed government out of full political representation for now, while signalling that gradual readmission could follow progress on the five-point consensus. Timor-Leste's admission was marked with an updated bloc emblem, and a digital economy framework agreement was handed over to the secretary-general.

Donald Trump expected in Manila, engaging with the region on conflict and trade

impact_points: Myanmar's military government faces a possible gradual return to ASEAN ties if it makes concrete progress on peace steps.
Member states such as Thailand gain room for bilateral engagement with Myanmar, easing pressure on the bloc's ban.

auto-f6bb7a503ce6.headline: Iran says it struck US radar in Bahrain as Hormuz standoff deepens
auto-f6bb7a503ce6.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday they fired six drones at a US air defence radar facility at Riffa Air Base in Bahrain, the second such claim in three days. Bahrain said its air defences intercepted the attack before it could reach its targets, and its interior ministry sounded alerts and urged residents to seek shelter.

The US military has not commented on Sunday's claim, though it earlier denied that a radar was destroyed on Friday and said it had downed two Iranian drones. The episode comes amid a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran insists on control and attacks what it calls unauthorised shipping.

Drone strikes and Hormuz closure face US retaliation and mounting pressure
Iranian drone attacks on US assets, while US air defences shot them down

impact_points: Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, faces repeated drone attacks and has condemned Iran's actions.
Gulf states and shipping firms face disruption as tanker traffic through Hormuz remains restricted and vessels hit mines.

auto-7d1bdfdf60db.headline: Estonia to shut Russian border crossings over alleged sabotage plot
auto-7d1bdfdf60db.summary:
Estonia says it will close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 December, blaming Russia's military intelligence service, the GRU, for an attempted arson attack on a drone manufacturer. Intruders tried to break into Threod Systems, a drone maker in Viimsi near Tallinn, early on Saturday, aiming to set the building on fire and cause an explosion. Security staff stopped them before significant damage occurred.

Eight suspects, all residents of Latvia, were detained and five remain in custody. Estonia's security service KAPO says its intelligence links the plot to the GRU, and officials warn Russia is increasingly targeting European defence firms that supply Ukraine. Russia has been asked for comment; the investigation continues.

Accused of ordering the sabotage; border closure and pressure follow

impact_points: Russia faces a closed Estonian land border and sharper diplomatic pressure after Tallinn's sabotage accusation.
Estonia's defence industry and Ukraine-bound drone supply chains face ongoing sabotage threats from Russian-linked operatives.

auto-358054ba5943.headline: Russia reportedly seeks NATO pullback and bilateral pacts; Kremlin denies agreeing to European role
auto-358054ba5943.summary: Following US-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, Russia's demands reportedly include NATO withdrawing troops from Central and Eastern Europe and a ban on further expansion, according to leaked documents. Moscow also reportedly wants nonaggression pacts with individual European states, which critics say could undermine NATO's collective defence. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff said Putin agreed to European participation in the next round, but a Kremlin aide said on Monday that Russia has not agreed to this and that the date is not set.

actors.why: Stalled talks and continued drone strikes leave Ukraine under heavy pressure
Demands for NATO pullback and bilateral pacts are seen as leverage

Excluded from talks so far, with its security architecture at stake

auto-8c623564469c.headline: Houthi advance on Aden raises fears for Red Sea shipping and oil markets
auto-8c623564469c.summary:
Iran-backed Houthi rebels have pushed the Yemeni army out of the Red Sea coast and now control the Bab al-Mandab Strait area, a route that normally carries about 12% of global trade. Government forces are reportedly withdrawing to defend the interim capital, Aden, while Houthi forces were said to be around 60 kilometres from the city, according to military sources cited by AFP. The Houthis have also attacked Saudi Arabia, damaging an oil pipeline.

Analysts quoted in the reporting warn that a fall of Aden could escalate the regional conflict and add pressure to a global economy already strained by the US-Iran war. Others say a costly urban offensive is unlikely, and that the Houthis may seek a negotiated outcome. The Houthis also released 600 government detainees, which they called a humanitarian step.

Houthi attacks and loss of Red Sea oil route pressure Saudi exports and security
Iran-backed Houthis gain strategic coastline and smuggling routes
Regional escalation adds pressure amid the wider US-Iran conflict

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces renewed attacks and risks to its oil exports through the Red Sea.
Global shipping and oil markets could face fresh disruption if the Bab al-Mandab Strait is threatened further.

auto-62c2072317c4.headline: Tankers hit mines in Hormuz on route Iran deems unauthorised
auto-62c2072317c4.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says several oil tankers have struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz while using a route Tehran considers unauthorised. The IRGC Navy said two tankers caught fire and exploded in the southern part of the strait after switching off their tracking systems. One supertanker was reported to carry more than two million barrels of crude and may have sunk. Other tankers reportedly turned back after receiving warnings from the Guard's traffic control centre. Several explosions have been reported in the waterway over the past week, and the claims could not be independently verified.

Global oil shipping is disrupted through a critical chokepoint, with risks to traffic and prices

impact_points: Shipping operators using the southern Hormuz route face fire, sinking and cargo losses from mine strikes.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard is asserting control over passage through the strait, with tankers forced to heed its warnings or turn back.

auto-858917c08b11.headline: Third US carrier reaches Middle East as tensions with Iran persist
auto-858917c08b11.summary:
The USS Theodore Roosevelt reached the western Indian Ocean and is heading to join two other American carriers in the Middle East, the first time the Pentagon has moved three carriers to the region since the Iraq war. The deployment comes amid US pressure on Iran and reported Iranian attacks on US-linked sites in Bahrain, which Iran's Revolutionary Guards have claimed. Iran faces gas shortages and damage to its infrastructure from US strikes, with officials reportedly worried about public unrest.

The Roosevelt was originally meant to replace the USS George H.W. Bush, but that carrier's deployment has been extended through the holidays. Separately, Yemen's Houthis, backed by Iran, have advanced toward Aden, and Saudi Arabia removed its coalition commander.

Under blockade and strikes, facing gas shortages and public unrest risk

impact_points: The United States is strengthening its military presence in the region as pressure on Iran continues.
Iran faces fuel shortages and economic strain that could deepen unrest and hamper its war effort.

auto-6f5476309fb2.headline: Burnham says Brexit has failed, plans EU reset deal
auto-6f5476309fb2.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said Brexit has not worked and that the country has lost more than it gained. Speaking ahead of a summit with European leaders, he said he would sign a new agreement with the EU if it fits Labour's manifesto and government red lines and improves the existing deal. He says the agreements could raise GDP by 0.4%, about £17bn, covering food and farming, emissions trading and youth mobility. The EU relations minister, Hamish Falconer, said the UK could have a voice in the room but no vote on EU food policy, and that an exit clause may be included. Boris Johnson argued Brexit should not be a political priority for Labour.

actors.why: Seeks a reset deal the government says could lift GDP and ease business barriers

impact_points: The UK would seek a closer trading and regulatory relationship with the EU, with a claimed economic gain of about £17bn.
The EU is reportedly concerned a future UK government could reverse the deal, so an exit clause is under discussion.

auto-f15bf95dc8b3.headline: China and Canada widen tariff cuts as Ottawa weighs US trade strains
auto-f15bf95dc8b3.summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit and agreed to further tariff reductions. China will offer extra tariff relief on about 400 million Canadian dollars of exports, including frozen pork, fish and seafood, while Canada extends exemptions on some Chinese steel and aluminum for two years. The talks followed Carney's remark that Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if negotiations with the United States over an integrated North American auto industry fail.

Carney said he wants US talks to remain the priority, and Canada is reportedly making progress with Washington, though differences remain. Any Chinese auto investment, he said, would need substantial local manufacturing rather than simple assembly. Ontario's premier has criticised the earlier January deal on Chinese electric vehicles.

impact_points: Canada faces pressure on its auto sector, with Chinese investment offered as an alternative to US-linked production.
China gains expanded market access for its exports and stronger ties with Ottawa, while Washington's trade relations with Canada are strained.

auto-7739faaca616.headline: Oman and Iran discuss Hormuz shipping safety amid rising tanker attacks
auto-7739faaca616.summary:
Iran and Oman held talks on Tuesday, November 17, about protecting maritime corridors and keeping global shipping and trade flowing, Oman's foreign ministry said. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi visited Oman, which borders the southern side of the Strait of Hormuz and has acted as a mediator since the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28.

Shipping through the strait remains disrupted, with attacks on tankers increasing while Iran restricts traffic and Washington maintains a naval blockade on Iran. Sources said Iran attacked navigation systems on an Omani island in the strait last week, though the damage could not be independently confirmed. The strait is still a key obstacle in stalled negotiations to end the nine-month-old war.

Talks on shipping safety, but disrupting traffic and facing a US naval blockade

auto-4a3420b303e0.headline: Trump arrives in Manila for Quad talks before China trip
auto-4a3420b303e0.summary:
US President Donald Trump is flying into the Philippines at the close of an ASEAN summit, where protests against his visit are possible. It will be his first Quad meeting with Japan, Australia and India, the first gathering of that group in two years. The trip also includes APEC in Shenzhen and a planned trilateral meeting with China and Russia, which comes after his party's midterm defeat and spy allegations that could strain a fragile US-China trade truce.

China's Premier Li Qiang, speaking at the ASEAN summit, stressed free trade and unity against outside interference. Trump is set to meet Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, with a trade agreement under negotiation with Thailand.

auto-ca6f6aab0d6f.headline: Ghalibaf warns Iran would mirror US logic on dams and bases
auto-ca6f6aab0d6f.summary: Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, responded on X to a New York Times report that appeared to justify US strikes on Iranian water infrastructure. He argued that such reasoning could be used to target civilian facilities, and said that under the same logic any dam, port or power plant near a US or Israeli military base could be treated as dual-purpose. Ghalibaf said Iran would apply this reasoning without change. Earlier, US officials had said they were preparing to attack Iran's vital infrastructure, particularly its dams, in a new round of strikes.

auto-0ec96eb542dd.headline: Riyadh names new commander for Yemen coalition after territorial reversals
auto-0ec96eb542dd.summary:
Saudi Arabia has replaced the head of the military coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Houthis. The royal decree moved General Fahd bin Hamad bin Abdulaziz al-Salman to an advisory post at the Defence Ministry, with Chief of the General Staff Fayyad al-Ruwaili taking over. The change follows reports that Riyadh's Yemeni allies had been forced to pull back from parts of their territory.

Yemen's armed forces, speaking through spokesman Yahya Saree, separately claimed missile strikes on King Khalid Airport and a financial centre in Riyadh, along with attacks on forces in Lahj province. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed these claims, and they could not be independently verified. Yemeni media also alleged a high volume of Saudi air strikes on several provinces.

auto-6539e431c896.headline: Israeli military reportedly moved 3.5 million Palestinian photos to Amazon cloud
auto-6539e431c896.summary: Reporting by The Guardian, based on leaked documents and military sources, says the Israeli military uploaded about 3.5 million photographs of Palestinians to Amazon Web Services in early 2024. The images were moved to an Amazon data centre near Tel Aviv by a military department that maintains databases on Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank, to be analysed with Amazon's Rekognition facial recognition tool. Amazon said it has no visibility into customers' cloud workloads and denied that Israeli soldiers worked from its Tel Aviv offices. The Israeli military declined to comment on contracts.

auto-3be7816ec807.headline: Report says French military personnel are secretly working inside Ukraine
auto-3be7816ec807.summary:
Radio France Internationale reported that French military personnel have been in Ukraine since at least summer 2026 under a confidential mission codenamed Volia, led by a French general. Their tasks reportedly include training Ukrainian troops and helping maintain French-supplied equipment, using short-term deployments. The number of personnel was not disclosed, and French lawmakers were reportedly not formally informed. A source told AFP the personnel have no combat role, and the French General Staff did not comment.

The mission is said to be linked to Gerfaut, a French detachment in Poland under an EU military assistance mission for Ukraine. The reporting could not be independently verified.

auto-63ed9b3dd59c.headline: EU prepares 22nd Russia sanctions package as Kallas rejects Moscow's demands
auto-63ed9b3dd59c.summary:
The European Union is preparing a new sanctions package against Russia, its 22nd since February 2022, targeting banks, crypto channels and the shadow fleet used to avoid the oil price cap. The Commission has begun consulting member states, and the proposal is due before the end of the month, with conclusion expected in December.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called Russia's peace demands absurd, including Ukrainian withdrawal from Donbas and NATO pullbacks, and said a ceasefire must come first. Some officials also questioned whether Kallas would join the EU's negotiating team, which leaders set up without her.

auto-5b31c06a19a8.headline: Britain sanctions eight Israeli firms over West Bank settlement building
auto-5b31c06a19a8.summary: Britain has imposed sanctions on eight Israeli construction and property development firms it says are helping plan and build settlements in the occupied West Bank. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband urged Israeli companies not to bid on or profit from the projects, which the UK says threaten the two-state solution. The Foreign Office also sanctioned the activist group Tzav 9 for obstructing aid into Gaza, where it says Israeli authorities are holding large stocks of tents and tarpaulins and blocking timber. The measures freeze assets and disqualify directors.

auto-4063ba089bf2.headline: Iran rejects US reports of alleged dirty bomb plot in Washington
auto-4063ba089bf2.summary:
US intelligence reportedly indicates Iran is drawing up plans that could involve a radiological or chemical attack on senior Trump administration officials in Washington, according to CNN, which cited unnamed officials. The officials said the planning appears aimed at giving Tehran extra options rather than signalling an imminent strike, and that it was unclear whether operatives were in place. Iran's foreign ministry called the allegations baseless, and the White House said there were no credible threats to the homeland at this time.

President Trump said the US was looking into the matter and warned that Iran would pay a heavy price if an attack occurred. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman also said the reports were propaganda meant to justify strikes on Iranian infrastructure, pointing to water facilities hit in recent US-Israeli attacks.

auto-ed45520f135c.headline: Saudi-led coalition downs Houthi drone; Houthis claim missile strikes on Riyadh
auto-ed45520f135c.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone aimed at the Riyadh Region, a day after Saudi defenses downed two drones sent toward Makkah and Riyadh, which the coalition called an attempt to target holy sites. Separately, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group fired ballistic missiles at Riyadh's financial district and King Khalid International Airport, and at Saudi troops in Yemen's Lahij governorate; Saudi Arabia had not responded and the missile claims could not be independently confirmed. Reports also described explosions in Aden.

In a separate development, Saudi Arabia condemned repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain as a violation of international law, while Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian aerial attacks and urged citizens to seek shelter.

auto-fbcb202fd28d.headline: US tightens AI chip export licensing, drawing Chinese condemnation and threats of retaliation
auto-fbcb202fd28d.summary:
Washington has introduced new limits on exports of advanced AI chips. Under the rules, data centres anywhere in the world must obtain a US licence to supply large volumes of computing power from these chips to firms headquartered in China, Macau, or other countries under US arms embargoes. Licences are also required for shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which the US Commerce Department says face a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.

China's foreign ministry called the curbs an overreach of national security and said Beijing would take necessary measures to protect its interests. The commerce ministry expressed firm opposition, urged Washington to resolve differences through talks, and warned of countermeasures.

auto-865fc748b5e1.headline: US assesses Iran retains 1,500 to 2,500 ballistic missiles despite strikes
auto-865fc748b5e1.summary:
US intelligence estimates Iran still holds between 1,500 and 2,500 ballistic missiles, a figure officials rate as low confidence because exact counts are hard to verify. Israeli officials put the number above 1,500. Iran is reportedly producing around 50 missiles a month, about half its prewar rate, and has reopened some underground sites damaged in strikes.

The estimates have fed debate in Washington over whether to resume strikes, while Iran's Revolutionary Guard has said the 2,000-kilometre range limit no longer applies. Reports also describe heavy use of US Patriot interceptors and attacks on Gulf bases.

auto-4a7557e51073.headline: Iraq sets Friday deadline for Iran-backed militia to leave southern town
auto-4a7557e51073.summary: Iraq's prime minister, Ali al-Zaidi, has ordered the armed forces into Jurf al-Sakher, south of Baghdad, a town controlled by the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah group. The government says an investigation found oil smuggling and pipeline tampering in the area and has set a deadline of Friday for the militia to withdraw. Kataib Hezbollah rejects the smuggling claims as fabricated and says it will not give up its stronghold, though its commander said the group does not seek a clash with Iraqi forces. The move follows heavy US and Gulf pressure on Baghdad to curb Iran's influence.

auto-9727480265f5.headline: Moldova shuts its airspace after Russian drones enter over Chișinău
auto-9727480265f5.summary:
Moldovan authorities closed the country's entire airspace on Tuesday after a Russian Shahed-type drone was detected heading toward the capital, Chișinău. Officials said the drone crossed from Ukraine during a Russian attack on Ukraine, and several other drones also entered Moldovan airspace. Air traffic was diverted, with at least one passenger flight rerouted toward Romania, and the central sector reopened at 17:03. Five drones reportedly crashed in villages across the country, with no casualties reported.

President Maia Sandu and Foreign Minister Mihai Popșoi condemned the incursions as a breach of sovereignty, with Sandu saying Moldova lacks the defence capabilities to counter the drones.

auto-ef808193c0c0.headline: Israeli-settled West Bank village sees fatal shooting of elderly Palestinian woman
auto-ef808193c0c0.summary:
A 72-year-old Palestinian woman, Fadda al-Fahidat, was shot dead in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, a village near Jericho in the occupied West Bank, and several others were wounded, according to the Palestinian health ministry. Local residents blame Israeli settlers who had recently moved into eight houses there, while the Israeli army describes a car-ramming attack and rock-throwing that prompted its troops to open fire, without mentioning the woman's death. Israeli police said they had opened an investigation, and the accounts remain in conflict.

The incident follows months of tension in the village, where rights groups report settler intimidation and land seizures. Settlements are illegal under international law.

auto-bf4ac1bfc507.headline: US Navy acting chief admits Iran war strains fleet during Senate hearing
auto-bf4ac1bfc507.summary:
At his Senate confirmation hearing, Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao acknowledged that the war with Iran, now in its ninth month, is straining the navy. Senators from both parties pressed him on long ship deployments, dwindling weapons stocks, low crew morale and the handling of officer removals, including the leadership of the submarine USS South Dakota. Cao said the navy's joint efforts had set China back, while noting the war's cost.

Separately, US Vice President JD Vance told Fox News the United States does not intend to stay in a long-term commitment with Iran, rejecting a ten-to-fifteen-year or even two-year conflict. He said Washington's nuclear concerns about Iran remain but that the US would withdraw with good results. Trump has said further strikes are unlikely, though forces remain ready.

auto-6131c6e2c605.headline: Saudi Arabia replaces Yemen coalition commander as Houthis press toward Aden
auto-6131c6e2c605.summary:
Saudi Arabia dismissed Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad al-Salman as commander of the coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, replacing him with Chief of Staff General Fayyad al-Ruwaili, according to a royal decree. The move follows a run of setbacks for Yemeni government forces as the Iran-backed Houthis seized coastal territory and advanced toward Aden, the interim seat of government. The government said it was pulling back from areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on defending Aden.

US commentator Tucker Carlson claimed the Houthis are occupying parts of Saudi Arabia, but that assertion could not be independently verified. Analysts doubt the leadership change alone will reverse the battlefield trend.

actors.why: Commander replaced amid Houthi attacks and pressure on its border and infrastructure
Houthis advancing toward Aden while government forces retreat and fragment
Houthi gains enhance Iran's position in the wider regional conflict

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces mounting pressure as Houthi attacks on its territory and infrastructure continue.
Yemen's internationally recognised government risks losing Aden, its provisional capital, to the Houthis.

auto-a3bf6edfe85c.headline: US pushes Ukraine peace deal as Europe debates its role
auto-a3bf6edfe85c.summary:
The United States is pressing Russia and Ukraine to consider wide-ranging proposals covering NATO rules, military assets and troop placements across Europe, according to people familiar with the talks. Reports say Washington has even asked Kyiv whether it would cede the Donbas region to Russia in exchange for NATO membership, a idea that clashes with the European view that fighting must stop before security talks begin.

The European Union is divided over how to take part. European leaders agreed on a seven-member team, including France, Germany, the UK, Italy, Poland, the EU institutions and NATO, but some officials say the debate over who represents Europe distracts from the war itself. Three-way talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November produced only a prisoner swap, and Russia has intensified attacks on Ukrainian cities.

actors.why: Pressed to consider ceding Donbas to Russia for NATO membership
US talks may advance Russian demands on Ukraine and NATO security arrangements
Leads a push for a sweeping deal and sets the terms of negotiations
Divided over strategy and seeks a say in US-brokered negotiations
Part of the European seven-member team seeking a role in talks
Part of the European seven-member team seeking a role in talks

impact_points: Ukraine faces pressure to consider ceding Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, a prospect it has not accepted.
European states risk being sidelined from talks on their own security arrangements unless they secure a unified seat at the table.

auto-0775ce617eaa.headline: Serbian air force jet crashes near Belgrade, pilot dies
auto-0775ce617eaa.summary: A Serbian military MiG-29 fighter jet crashed on Tuesday morning near Stara Pazova, northwest of Belgrade, killing its pilot. The defence ministry identified him as Major Goran Bulajić, 53, who had served in the Serbian military since 1996 and leaves two children. The crash happened at about 8:45 am local time, and video circulating online shows the aircraft burning in a field. The ministry has set up a commission to examine the circumstances and any possible responsibility, and an air force expert panel will determine the cause.

actors.why: Loses an experienced pilot and faces an investigation into the crash

impact_points: Serbia loses an experienced pilot and faces a formal investigation into its MiG-29 fleet's safety.
Bulajić's family, including his two children, is left without him, and the air force must review the incident.

auto-7dc3857d6bc6.headline: US federal charges filed against Irish man over damage to Air Guard plane
auto-7dc3857d6bc6.summary:
US prosecutors have charged Daithi O'Corrain, 48, with destroying US government property after an April attack on a US Air National Guard C-130 Hercules parked at Shannon airport in Ireland. The indictment, unsealed in Manhattan, alleges he cut hydraulic lines, smashed cockpit instruments and put ball bearings into fuel tanks, leaving the aircraft unable to fly again. Irish police arrested him at the scene, where he faces local charges of criminal damage and trespass. He is not in US custody, and no US court date has been set.

Prosecutors allege the attack was planned for months. Supporters describe O'Corrain as a peace activist who was protesting US military action against Iran and Israel's war in Gaza. If convicted in the US, he faces up to 10 years in prison.

actors.why: Loses a $60m aircraft and prosecutors frame the attack as a security threat.
Attack occurred on Irish soil; local police arrested the suspect, creating diplomatic and security scrutiny.

impact_points: The United States loses a roughly $60 million transport aircraft and faces a national security embarrassment at an allied airport.
Ireland must manage a US federal case against one of its own citizens while handling its own criminal proceedings.

auto-655dc09d56ab.headline: Knesset elects Eisenkot-allied Kahana speaker, a setback for Netanyahu's camp
auto-655dc09d56ab.summary:
Israel's parliament, the Knesset, elected Matan Kahana as its speaker on Tuesday by 66 votes out of 120, defeating Likud's candidate Ofir Katz, who received 52. Kahana, a former special forces soldier and ally of Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to begin reversing parts of the outgoing agenda of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as early as Wednesday. Eisenkot has until next month to form a government, and neither bloc holds a majority after the October 27 elections.

The speaker sets parliamentary timetables, so the post can speed up or delay legislation. Both Arab-majority slates backed Kahana, while Likud criticised the result, and an investigation into alleged vote fraud found no evidence of bribes affecting the outcome, the central elections committee said.

actors.why: Parliamentary power shifts from Netanyahu's camp toward Eisenkot's opposition bloc.

impact_points: Netanyahu's Likud and his legislative agenda, including judicial reforms, face a serious setback from the new speaker.
Eisenkot's bloc gains leverage to repeal judicial changes and push a state inquiry into the October 7 attack.

auto-63693e15a5cb.headline: Haitians rally in Port-au-Prince backing El Salvador's troops against gangs
auto-63693e15a5cb.summary: Thousands of people gathered in Haiti's capital to show support for Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele and for Salvadoran soldiers working to counter armed gangs that control large parts of the city. Demonstrators framed the foreign security presence as a welcome response to a worsening crisis. The rally came ahead of planned talks between Haitian authorities and Bukele, though the reporting available did not confirm the agenda or outcomes of those discussions.

actors.why: Public backing for foreign troops against gangs, with talks with Bukele pending
Bukele's government gains regional prominence and a security partnership role

impact_points: Haiti's government and security forces gain visible public backing for seeking outside help against gang violence.
El Salvador's leadership strengthens its regional profile by being welcomed as a security partner in Haiti.

auto-7c5acdd61d5c.headline: Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing everyone aboard
auto-7c5acdd61d5c.summary: A Russian military An-12 transport plane went down in the Kemerovo region of Siberia, near the village of Yagunovo, killing all 19 people on board, according to the defence ministry as relayed by state media. The ministry said the aircraft was on a scheduled flight over an uninhabited area and preliminarily blamed a technical malfunction. Regional governor Ilya Seredyuk said emergency crews quickly put out a fire and police sealed off the site. Early reports from other outlets gave differing casualty figures, and CCTV footage showing the crash was verified by Reuters and the BBC.

actors.why: Military loses a transport aircraft and all 19 aboard; technical fault under investigation

impact_points: Russia's military faces a fatal aviation loss, with an investigation into the cause now under way.
Local authorities in Kemerovo must support the probe and manage the site, while families of those aboard await confirmation.

auto-a790032dad10.headline: Kremlin officials tell Russian MPs to prepare for a post-war return of fighters
auto-a790032dad10.summary: Representatives of the Russian presidential administration reportedly told United Russia lawmakers to get ready for the end of the war in Ukraine, when soldiers return home. The remarks were made at a November 13-14 seminar near Moscow, attended by Sergei Kiriyenko, first deputy chief of staff. According to a source cited by the business daily Vedomosti, officials said everyone should be prepared for "victory". The report did not explain how lawmakers should prepare. The seminar also reportedly covered the 2030 presidential and 2031 Duma elections, and Kiriyenko urged MPs to be closer to ordinary people.

actors.why: Kremlin preparing lawmakers for post-war return of fighters and elections
Russian officials signal the war's end, though no outcome is confirmed

impact_points: Russia's ruling establishment is signalling planning for a post-war period and returning combatants.
Russian lawmakers face pressure to rebuild their public image and connect with ordinary citizens ahead of elections.

auto-ca25be16730b.headline: Drones cause most verified civilian deaths in Sudan's war, UN finds
auto-ca25be16730b.summary:
The UN human rights office says drone strikes caused more than 1,630 of the 2,230 civilian deaths it verified in Sudan between January and the end of October. The war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, which began in April 2023, has seen both sides rely increasingly on long-range drones. UN rights chief Volker Turk said the violations may amount to war crimes. The UN also flagged a series of drone strikes on power stations and fuel depots that caused blackouts and shortages far from the front lines.

The UN says true casualty figures are likely higher. Sudanese women journalists have condemned the drone attacks and called for a halt to strikes on populated areas, along with an extended arms embargo.

actors.why: Civilians suffer deadly drone strikes and loss of power, water and fuel.
UN calls for pressure and arms embargo expansion, implicating outside suppliers.

impact_points: Sudanese civilians face mounting losses from drone strikes on homes, markets, power and water facilities.
Regional and international backers supplying the warring parties are criticised by the UN for sustaining the fighting.

auto-b8ceae6248d9.headline: French public sector workers strike again over pay and budget deadlock
auto-b8ceae6248d9.summary:
Public sector workers across France staged a one-day nationwide strike on Tuesday, demanding pay rises, with high school and university students and some private sector workers joining cost-of-living protests. The interior ministry counted about 146,000 demonstrators nationally, far fewer than at the previous unified protest day on November 5, while unions said turnout was larger. The government has ruled out a general pay rise in its draft 2027 budget, though it offered extra index points for the lowest-paid staff and an earlier minimum wage increase. Police were deployed in large numbers, and the protests were largely peaceful apart from isolated violence.

The unrest comes as France races to pass its budget ahead of next year's presidential election, with the far right seen as a contender. Unions say public servants have lost 16 percent of purchasing power since 2017. Russia's foreign minister separately accused France of 'direct participation' in the Ukraine war over a small French training deployment, which Paris rejected.

actors.why: Government faces strikes, protests and stalled budget talks before a presidential election.
Lavrov publicly accused France of direct involvement in the Ukraine war, raising tensions.
French trainers in Ukraine are a focus of Russian claims, though the deployment is described as limited.
Belgian students protested school conditions and tuition fees in a similar wave inspired by France.

impact_points: France's government faces mounting pressure from unions and students while trying to pass a deficit-cutting 2027 budget.
Public sector staff, including low-paid workers near the minimum wage, face continued loss of purchasing power and unresolved pay talks.

auto-e5365dde9092.headline: ASEAN and China miss deadline for South China Sea code of conduct
auto-e5365dde9092.summary:
ASEAN and China failed to finish negotiations on a code of conduct for the South China Sea by the end of 2026, the Philippines' foreign minister Theresa Lazaro said in Manila. Provisional agreement exists on about 80 percent of the draft text, but key issues remain open, including whether the code would be legally binding, its geographic scope, and how terms would be defined. Talks are expected to continue when Singapore takes over the ASEAN chair in 2027.

At the same summit, ASEAN and Chinese Premier Li Qiang were expected to pledge restraint in actions that could escalate disputes, according to a draft statement seen by the AP, which could not be independently confirmed as final. ASEAN also extended its ban on Myanmar's leader attending summits over the country's failure to follow a 2021 peace plan.

actors.why: Chair failed to meet its deadline; ongoing Chinese maritime confrontations continue
Pledges restraint but code remains unfinished and its position is contested
Will take over the chair and inherit the unfinished talks in 2027
Remains a claimant whose maritime disputes stay unresolved without the code
Remains a claimant whose maritime disputes stay unresolved without the code
Faces continued ASEAN rebuke and extended ban on its leader attending summits

impact_points: China and Southeast Asian states, including the Philippines, Vietnam and Malaysia, face continued uncertainty over maritime rules and disputes.
The Philippines, as chair, takes a setback in its goal of finalising the code this year, though talks advance under Singapore.

auto-6d2fd6035c8c.headline: France and Malaysia deepen ties with rare earths and defence deals
auto-6d2fd6035c8c.summary:
France and Malaysia upgraded their relationship to a strategic partnership during Emmanuel Macron's two-day visit to Kuala Lumpur, his first since 2017. Macron and Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim signed agreements covering critical minerals, energy, semiconductors and defence. Malaysia agreed to relax its export ban on raw rare earths for France, tied to a joint mining and processing venture between Carester and Malaco in Perak state, expected to begin operating in early 2027.

On defence, the two countries plan a regional centre to counter hybrid threats such as cyberattacks and disinformation, and Airbus will supply helicopters to Malaysia's air force. No financial terms were disclosed. The visit comes as Malaysia reviews its reliance on foreign arms suppliers after Norway revoked a missile export licence.

actors.why: Gains processing investment and partnership, though it bends its raw export ban.
Secures rare earths supply and reduces dependence on China.
Faces reduced reliance by France on Chinese rare earths supply.
Revoked a missile export licence, prompting Malaysia to question its reliability.

impact_points: Malaysia gains French investment and technology in rare earths processing while easing its raw export ban.
France reduces its reliance on China for rare earths and secures supply for its industrial value chain.

auto-437699730a63.headline: Gaza truce at risk as Board of Peace urges UN action
auto-437699730a63.summary: The US-backed Board of Peace told the UN Security Council in a report that the year-old Gaza truce between Israel and Hamas could collapse without urgent steps to carry out the 2025 ceasefire deal. The board said both sides have fallen well short of their commitments, and it criticised Israeli restrictions on aid and supplies, ongoing air strikes, and Israel's blocking of the interim civil administration meant to run Gaza. It also said Israel has not decided on the conditions for returning civilian police to the territory. The board asked the Council to press both parties and said any outcome must keep a credible path toward Palestinian statehood.

actors.why: Civilians face aid shortages, winter exposure and a possible return to war.
Faces pressure over blocked aid, air strikes and stalled ceasefire commitments.
Its Board of Peace warns the flagship Gaza plan is at risk of failing.

impact_points: Palestinians in Gaza face another winter in tents and rubble, with aid blocked and reconstruction stalled.
Israel and Hamas risk losing the ceasefire framework, and with it any road map for withdrawal and rebuilding.

auto-6f51d716aa6f.headline: Irish man charged over axe attack that disabled US military aircraft in Ireland
auto-6f51d716aa6f.summary:
A 48-year-old Irish man, Daithi O'Corrain, has been indicted in New York for allegedly damaging a US Air National Guard C-130 Hercules at Shannon Airport in April. Prosecutors say he breached security, cut hydraulic lines, smashed cockpit gauges and poured ball bearings into the fuel tanks, leaving the roughly $60 million aircraft unable to fly again. He faces up to 10 years in prison if convicted of destroying government property.

Irish police arrested him at the scene and charged him with criminal damage and trespass. Supporters say he acted in protest against the US-Israel war on Iran and US support for Israel's war in Gaza; prosecutors say he planned the attack for months.

actors.why: Loses a $60 million military aircraft and pursues charges over attack
Security breaches at Shannon Airport and protest tensions over US military presence

impact_points: Ireland faces renewed scrutiny of US military use of Shannon Airport amid repeated security breaches.
The United States loses a costly aircraft and must pursue O'Corrain, who is not in US custody.

auto-0a0bdab86651.headline: Second merchant ship sinks off Bulgaria after suspected drone attacks in Black Sea
auto-0a0bdab86651.summary:
A Liberia-flagged gas tanker, the GAS HUSKY, sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea, about 50 nautical miles offshore, after reportedly being struck by drones. All 19 Filipino crew were rescued by a Bulgarian Cougar helicopter, and two were treated for minor injuries. The incident came a day after a Somali-flagged cargo ship, the BETUL 8, capsized nearby after a suspected sea drone attack; its 12 crew were also saved.

The tanker's master said four drones hit the ship, which would make it the seventh merchant vessel struck in Bulgaria's zone since October. Investigators have not confirmed the cause, and officials have not said whether drones were involved. Analysts and political leaders widely blame Russia, though Moscow's role remains unverified.

actors.why: Vessels sinking in its exclusive economic zone; rescues and security burden rising
Tanker was bound for Romanian port of Midia; regional shipping disrupted
Shipping attacks threaten Ukraine's Black Sea trade routes and grain exports
Widely blamed for drone strikes on commercial shipping, though unconfirmed
Pledged funds for a Black Sea maritime security hub to counter threats

impact_points: Bulgaria and Romania face repeated losses of merchant vessels and growing pressure on Black Sea shipping routes.
Global grain and energy supply chains risk disruption, with Ukraine warning food prices could rise sharply if routes are hit.

auto-79d01ea79e38.headline: Iraq restarts crude exports through long-shut Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey
auto-79d01ea79e38.summary:
Iraq has restarted pumping crude oil for export through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey, initially at 120,000 barrels per day, with plans to raise flows to 500,000 bpd. Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair announced the restart, saying it followed maintenance, rehabilitation and testing. The 960-km line had been offline since 2014, when repeated attacks by Daesh militants shut it down.

The reopening gives Iraq a northern export route that reduces dependence on its southern terminals, which have been hit by the Iran war and the disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Officials say northern exports can be sold at market prices without discounts. How much the pipeline adds to total exports depends on available supply.

actors.why: Regains an export outlet and diversifies away from disrupted southern routes
Receives Iraqi crude transiting its territory via the pipeline
Iraq's shift away from Hormuz lessens the leverage of Iran's disruption of the strait

impact_points: Iraq gains an alternative export route, reducing reliance on southern terminals and the disrupted Strait of Hormuz.
Turkey becomes a transit route for Iraqi crude, which could raise its role in regional energy flows.

auto-104c40371853.headline: US takes custody of Army colonel suspected of spying for Russia after UK arrest
auto-104c40371853.summary: A US Army lieutenant colonel arrested by British counter-terrorism police near Gloucester on 10 November on suspicion of spying for Russia has been transferred to US military custody, UK police said. The 41-year-old, identified as Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, was based at Imjin Barracks, the headquarters of NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. The case was handed to American authorities under existing international protocols after a joint investigation with MI5 and the FBI, meaning he will not face trial in the UK. The Kremlin has denied any involvement.

actors.why: Takes custody of accused officer and gains a counterespionage win
Arrest and investigation handed over, with an espionage breach at a NATO site
Accused of espionage, though Moscow denies any link to the case

impact_points: The United States gains custody of the accused officer, who will be tried under US military law rather than in Britain.
NATO and the UK face scrutiny over a suspected Russian espionage breach at a key alliance headquarters near Gloucester.

auto-56a9c3e5b20c.headline: Kim Jong Un's foreign travel history and possible Trump meeting in China
auto-56a9c3e5b20c.summary:
The headline story concerns North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's travel abroad, set against reporting that President Trump may seek a meeting with him during an Asia trip. Trump is attending an ASEAN summit in the Philippines before heading to China for APEC, where he is expected to hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Reports say Trump has signalled interest in meeting Kim, with Xi's involvement described as a possibility, though no meeting is confirmed. Coverage also notes a planned three-way discussion among the US, China and Russia on nuclear arms control, scheduled for November 19, without a pre-agreed agenda.

actors.why: Possible talks with Trump could bring diplomatic opening, though none is confirmed
Hosts APEC and may broker a Kim meeting, boosting its diplomatic role
Trump seeks direct leader talks with Kim and nuclear arms discussion
Putin joins trilateral talks, with Ukraine on the agenda

impact_points: North Korea would face renewed attention and possible diplomatic opening if a meeting with Trump materialises, though nothing is confirmed.
China would gain a central mediating role, as reports suggest any Kim meeting could be arranged with Xi's involvement.

auto-6681dd5dfa00.headline: Multiple tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Guards report
auto-6681dd5dfa00.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say several oil tankers have struck naval mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz via a southern route Tehran considers unauthorised. The Guards said two vessels were hit in one statement, and six tankers caught fire in similar incidents over Sunday and Monday. Explosions lit up the waterway for hours, according to the Guards, who warned shipping owners against trusting American military assurances about the route.

A separate report described a gas tanker whose crew abandoned ship off Oman after being hit by a projectile, and Oman evacuated 24 crew from another tanker after a fire nearby. These claims were reported by Iranian and regional media and were not independently verified in the coverage.

actors.why: Claims its Guards are defending the strait against an unauthorised route, drawing scrutiny.
Crews evacuated and a gas tanker hit by projectile off its coast.
Its military route guidance is being publicly rejected and blamed by Tehran.

impact_points: Oil shipping through the Strait of Hormuz faces serious danger, with tankers burning and mines reported on the southern route.
Oman and regional crews face evacuation risks, while shipowners are warned against using routes backed by US military guidance.

auto-4ed2b452e1db.headline: Russian city of Kursk installs monument honouring North Korean troops
auto-4ed2b452e1db.summary:
A monument to North Korean soldiers who fought alongside Russian forces in Kursk Oblast has been put up on Internatsionalnaya Street in the city of Kursk. Local outlet Drug dlya Druga reported that the sculpture, made by the Grekov Studio of Military Artists in Moscow, is currently wrapped in protective plastic. Russian President Vladimir Putin said on November 16 that it would be unveiled by the end of 2026.

North Korean units took part in the fighting in Kursk from late 2024, after Ukrainian forces had occupied part of the region. Western intelligence estimates cited by the Wall Street Journal say North Korea lost roughly 5,000 troops, about a third of them killed, though these figures could not be independently confirmed.

actors.why: Publicly honours the North Korean role in its Kursk fighting, showing a strengthened alliance.
Receives official Russian recognition of its troops' sacrifice, though losses were heavy.
Faces a symbolic reminder of foreign troops fighting on Russia's side in its war.

impact_points: North Korea is publicly honoured by Russia for its combat role, strengthening the two countries' military ties.
Ukraine faces a visible sign of Pyongyang's support for Moscow's war, which Kyiv is likely to see as deepening the conflict's international dimension.

auto-bd3a283c9d16.headline: Xi, Putin and Trump set for Shenzhen summit amid Iran and Ukraine deadlock
auto-bd3a283c9d16.summary: Leaders of China, Russia and the United States are expected to meet in Shenzhen on 18 and 19 November on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Commentators have compared the gathering to the 1945 Yalta Conference, though analysts cautioned that breakthroughs on Iran, Ukraine or trade are unlikely. Nuclear arms control is expected to feature, after the New START treaty expired earlier this year, leaving the US and Russia with over 5,000 warheads each. A Tehran-linked opinion piece urged the leaders to revive the spirit of the 1986 Reagan-Gorbachev talks.

actors.why: Hosts summit and faces Hormuz oil disruption and weaker exports
Gains a leadership platform and possible role mediating Iran talks
Seeks a diplomatic win but faces trade tensions and stalled Iran talks
Remains in conflict with the US, hoping Russia and China can help
Stakes tied to the Iran conflict Israel joined with the US

impact_points: China, the Strait of Hormuz's major oil buyer, is pressured by closure disruptions and weaker exports.
Iran and the United States remain deadlocked, with Russia and China seen as possible mediators.

auto-613f80415186.headline: South Korea's Lee arrives in Shenzhen ahead of APEC summit and US-China-Russia talks
auto-613f80415186.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung arrived in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. His schedule through Thursday includes a CEO summit, a dinner hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping, and the main session. The gathering is expected to coincide with a meeting among Xi, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump, where nuclear arms reduction may be discussed. Seoul says its views should be sufficiently reflected on issues touching the Korean Peninsula, and whether Trump will meet North Korea's Kim Jong-un remains a key question.

actors.why: Seoul seeks its interests reflected in peninsula talks, with its influence uncertain
Hosts APEC and a high-profile leaders' meeting, strengthening its diplomatic stage
Trump's possible talks with Xi, Putin and Kim could advance denuclearization diplomacy
Putin joins a trilateral meeting on nuclear arms reduction with China and the US
Possible Trump meeting with Kim Jong-un could raise its diplomatic standing

impact_points: South Korea must press its interests on the Korean Peninsula while larger powers discuss arms control and North Korea.
China, Russia and the United States could reshape regional security arrangements, affecting Seoul's diplomatic position in Asia.

auto-1ee0aeb083ea.headline: Six hurt, including a teenager, in drone strike on Dnipro
auto-1ee0aeb083ea.summary:
Six people were injured after Russian drones attacked two districts of Dnipro, according to Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk Oblast Military Administration. He said an apartment block, a house, student accommodation, a recreation park and infrastructure were damaged. A 37-year-old woman was reported in serious condition, while a 15-year-old boy, two men and another woman were in moderate condition. Hanzha gave no details on the consequences of a separate strike on the Pokrovske hromada in the Nikopol district.

The report comes from Ukrainian officials and has not been independently verified.

actors.why: Civilians injured and buildings damaged in Dnipro by Russian drones
Russian forces carried out drone strikes on Ukrainian civilian areas

impact_points: Ukraine's Dnipro residents face injuries and damage to homes, student housing and public infrastructure from drone strikes.
Ukrainian regional authorities must respond to ongoing Russian drone attacks on civilian areas in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast.

auto-2e240e3015f2.headline: Ukraine reports nearly 2,000 Russian casualties in one day, plus equipment losses
auto-2e240e3015f2.summary:
Ukraine's General Staff reported that Russia suffered 1,970 killed and wounded over the past day, bringing its cumulative personnel losses since February 2022 to about 1.63 million. The figures are Ukrainian military claims and have not been independently verified. Separately, Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 1,336 Ukrainian drones, which would be the largest such claim since the full-scale invasion began. Ukrainian officials also described Russian strikes on civilian areas, and an entire section of the Crimean Bridge was reported to have collapsed.

The reports also cover Western support for Kyiv. Norway pledged about $300 million and Sweden about $71 million toward US weapons purchases for Ukraine through NATO's PURL mechanism.

actors.why: Reported heavy personnel losses, drone interceptions claimed, and Crimean Bridge section collapsed
Ukraine reports inflicting losses while facing ongoing Russian strikes on civilian areas
Pledged about $300 million toward US weapons for Ukraine via NATO
Pledged about 720 million Swedish krona toward Ukrainian weapons initiatives
Pledged $300 million for Ukraine weapons, a stance its defence minister defended

impact_points: Russia faces heavy reported personnel and equipment losses, with its war effort under sustained pressure.
Ukraine and its allies face continued drone and missile strikes, while Western funding for Kyiv's weapons grows.

auto-10a49bb68975.headline: US officials say recent tech outages show no sign of hacking
auto-10a49bb68975.summary: A series of technical failures hit the United States in recent days, disrupting Microsoft tools, major banks, air traffic operations and a National Security Agency classified network. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking while travelling with President Trump in the Philippines, said there was no evidence linking the incidents to hackers, criminals or any foreign state. Officials attributed the problems to software bugs, a network upgrade and a router upgrade, and Senate intelligence chair Mark Warner echoed that view. Trump dismissed concerns, while a former White House press secretary urged more transparency.

actors.why: Widespread outages disrupted flights, banking and classified communications, drawing public criticism.
Rubio's trip to Shenzhen for the APEC summit places China in the wider diplomatic picture.

impact_points: The United States faces public frustration over grounded flights, disrupted banking and government communications during the outages.
Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase and United Airlines users were hit, with officials saying the causes were internal maintenance or upgrades.

auto-3d19758bfcb8.headline: Iran warns of response as US reports link dams to missile sites
auto-3d19758bfcb8.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei rejected a New York Times report that suggested Iranian dams overlap with suspected underground missile sites, calling the claims baseless propaganda meant to justify attacks on civilian infrastructure. He said Iran would answer any aggression with a forceful response. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf argued that, by the same logic, any dam, port or power plant near a US or Israeli base could be called dual-use. Iranians interviewed said they fear more civilian infrastructure could be struck in any renewed conflict. The report itself acknowledged its link was speculative.

actors.why: Faces threatened strikes on dams and power, with leaders vowing retaliation
Criticised for reports and threats targeting Iranian civilian infrastructure
Named alongside the US as a party accused of aggression against infrastructure

impact_points: Iran faces fears of renewed strikes on water, power and dams, with civilians bearing the disruption.
The US and Israel face Iranian warnings of a forceful response, and criticism over legitimising attacks on civilian sites.

auto-5ea0423d068b.headline: Israeli strikes on Hamas commanders continue as Gaza deaths and arms financing draw scrutiny
auto-5ea0423d068b.summary: The Israeli military says its Southern Command has carried out a series of targeted strikes on Hamas brigade commanders in Gaza, aiming to stop the group rebuilding its capabilities. An IDF officer rejected accusations of deliberately harming civilians and said Hamas exploits civilians and hospitals. Separately, medical sources cited by Reuters and Al Jazeera reported at least four Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in one day, including a six-year-old boy in Deir el-Balah. A Dawn investigation also reported that Deutsche Bank backed a deal financing gearbox parts for Israel's Merkava tanks, which have been used in incidents that killed civilians.

actors.why: Pursuing targeted strikes on Hamas, but facing criticism over civilian harm and arms supply
Civilians and medics killed in Israeli attacks, including a six-year-old boy
Deutsche Bank's financing of Merkava tank parts draws reputational and ethical scrutiny

impact_points: Israel faces international scrutiny over civilian casualties and its military conduct in Gaza.
Palestinian civilians in Gaza face continued deaths, and Hamas's leadership faces repeated targeted killings.

auto-e6cab8531ccc.headline: Trump begins Asia tour with Philippines stop ahead of China nuclear talks
auto-e6cab8531ccc.summary:
US President Donald Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday to start a multi-day Asia trip. He is set to meet Quad leaders, sign a trade deal with Thailand, and join an ASEAN summit where South China Sea disputes and Myanmar are on the agenda. Protesters rallied against his visit in Manila.

Later in the week, Trump is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on November 19. auto-2945c5593bf5.headline: Ukrainian strikes badly damage Kerch bridge, cutting Crimea's road link to Russia
auto-2945c5593bf5.summary: Ukraine has badly damaged the Kerch bridge, which links the Russian-annexed Crimean peninsula with Russia, in an overnight missile and drone attack that Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as unprecedented. Ukrainian officials said a road arch and span collapsed, severing the road link, while the rail arch was damaged but the line stayed open. Russian-installed Crimean governor Sergey Aksyonov confirmed road traffic was suspended, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would be repaired. Separately, Moscow's defence ministry said it intercepted 1,336 Ukrainian drones.

auto-6df3ceea9f82.headline: Jordanian Black Hawk helicopter crashes during military training, injuring five
auto-6df3ceea9f82.summary: A Black Hawk helicopter belonging to the Jordanian Armed Forces crashed on Wednesday while taking part in a military training exercise, according to the army's General Command. Specialised teams were dispatched to the scene and the army said protecting its personnel was its top priority. Initial reports gave no details of the aircraft's damage, and one of those hurt was reported to have serious injuries, though the figure of five injured was not confirmed by all sources. The army promised further updates as the situation develops.

auto-da201d906e18.headline: Oil slips as US stockpiles rise amid US-Iran strikes and Hormuz shipping risks
auto-da201d906e18.summary:
Oil prices edged lower on Wednesday after data showed US crude and fuel inventories rising last week, though ongoing US-Iran hostilities and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited the decline. Brent fell to roughly $92 a barrel and US West Texas Intermediate dropped to about $84.

Bahrain's defence force said it intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, a day after Iranian drones hit a US military radar system there and the US struck a missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island. A tanker was also struck near Oman, and Yemen's Houthis said they launched drones at Saudi pumping stations on an East-West pipeline used to bypass Hormuz. Talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar continued.

auto-075afea7b7d5.headline: EU expands Russia sanctions to banks, refiners and shadow fleet operators
auto-075afea7b7d5.summary:
The Council of the European Union has approved new sanctions against 12 Russian citizens and 101 entities, accused of financing Russia's war against Ukraine. The list includes 49 Russian banks and financial institutions, major oil refineries, online marketplaces and firms running tankers in Russia's shadow fleet. Individuals on the list face asset freezes and an EU entry ban.

A separate package adopted on the same day targets 2 entities and 30 people tied to Russian disinformation and cyberwarfare, including the Kremlin-linked Social Design Agency and the NoName057(16) hacker group. EU officials warn Moscow may try to influence upcoming elections in several member states.

auto-86cc053c42d1.headline: US probes Singapore firm Megaspeed over alleged Nvidia chip diversion to China
auto-86cc053c42d1.summary:
The US Justice and Commerce departments confirmed they are investigating Singapore-based Megaspeed, suspected of helping send Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China in breach of US export rules. The probe began in 2024, and in June 2025 Nvidia placed the company on a no-sell list after federal agents inspected its premises and interviewed then-chief executive Alice Huang.

The case followed revelations about Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's personal affairs, including one reportedly with Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. China denies the spying allegation. Washington has since tightened chip curbs, and Singapore says it is seeking trusted access to advanced chips.

auto-4bd7a4a3547d.headline: Ukraine damages Crimean Bridge as Russia faces strikes and Putin prepares summit
auto-4bd7a4a3547d.summary:
Ukraine says it severely damaged the Crimean Bridge, the road and rail link between Russia and occupied Crimea, using cruise missiles and drones in an overnight operation. Images show a large arch section collapsed into the water, while the rail section was reportedly still standing. Russia's Kremlin said the bridge would be rebuilt and be better than before, and opened a terrorism case. The strike came just before Vladimir Putin was due to meet Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China.

Separately, Russian missile and drone attacks hit Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro River, causing traffic closures, water and heating disruptions, and deaths in several Ukrainian cities.

auto-6d17eabff16e.headline: Ukrainian drones reportedly hit two Russian refineries in Krasnodar Krai overnight
auto-6d17eabff16e.summary: Two oil refineries in Russia's southern Krasnodar Krai were reportedly struck by drones overnight on November 17–18, 2026. Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channels said the Ilsky and Afipsky plants were hit, but the Kyiv Independent could not verify the strikes or the damage. The reported attacks are part of a wider Ukrainian campaign against Russian oil infrastructure, aimed at disrupting fuel supplies to Moscow's military and cutting revenue for the war. Ukraine's General Staff had earlier said it struck the Ilsky refinery on November 16, and Ukrainian military officials did not immediately confirm the latest strikes.

auto-8f96bfcc13f6.headline: Ukrainian drones linked to repeated flight halts at Russian airports
auto-8f96bfcc13f6.summary:
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said in early September that Russian airspace was becoming unsafe because of drones, while stressing Ukraine was not targeting civilian aircraft. An analysis of Russian aviation agency announcements from 1 August to 4 November 2026 found restrictions at Russian airports almost every day, peaking at 30 airports on 16 October. Frequency was highest at Domodedovo, Vnukovo and Sochi, and Moscow's four main airports were restricted together 14 times. Russia's Defence Ministry reported the number of drones each night, and airport restrictions generally rose with the reported drone count. Russian authorities cite only flight safety as the reason.

The analysis, conducted by a Ukrainian open-source intelligence group, did not explain every individual case, and it could not independently confirm drone activity beyond the ministry's own figures. Media reports and airport notices broadly matched in timing.

auto-21df8b101161.headline: NYT report linking Iranian dams to missile sites draws sharp criticism
auto-21df8b101161.summary: The New York Times published a story suggesting some of Iran's dams and water projects may have been built to support its underground missile programme, citing overlaps between water infrastructure and sites hit in US-Israeli airstrikes. The paper described the connection as speculative. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei called the report baseless and propaganda meant to justify attacks on vital infrastructure, while Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned that any US or Israeli base-adjacent dam or power plant could be treated as dual-use. auto-be568e94701c.headline: Canada and China expand tariff relief as Ottawa seeks trade beyond the US
auto-be568e94701c.summary:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen and agreed to cut tariffs on more goods. China will offer relief on about 400 million Canadian dollars of exports, including frozen pork and seafood, while Canada extends exemptions on certain Chinese steel and aluminium products for two more years. The move builds on a January deal and comes as Carney looks to reduce dependence on the United States amid tariffs and stalled North American trade talks.

Carney said the relationship now offers greater predictability and that Canada is ahead of schedule on its goal of raising exports to China by 50 percent by decade's end. The announcement drew a sharp reaction from a White House trade adviser, who criticised Carney's remarks about possibly turning to Chinese automakers.

auto-69f9577493ef.headline: Houthi advance nears Aden as Saudi-backed Yemeni forces pull back
auto-69f9577493ef.summary: Houthi rebels have pushed toward Aden, the temporary seat of Yemen's internationally recognized government, after taking districts and a coastal area roughly 60 to 100 kilometres away. Saudi Arabia replaced its Joint Forces commander, and Houthi drones were reported over Saudi provinces, including Riyadh and Mecca. auto-91d83bcecd86.headline: EU proposes €45 billion loan for Ukraine, repayable from future Russian reparations
auto-91d83bcecd86.summary: The European Commission has proposed a €45 billion loan to Ukraine for 2027, covering about two-thirds of an expected €70 billion financing gap. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Ukraine would repay the loan only once Russia pays reparations for war damage. She said the arrangement would give Kyiv stronger leverage in future negotiations and that other partners should cover the remainder. The proposal needs approval from EU member states and follows a separate €90 billion EU loan agreed late last year for 2026 and 2027.

auto-927edcf25564.headline: Irish man charged over attack that disabled US military plane at Shannon
auto-927edcf25564.summary:
A 48-year-old Irish man, Daithi O'Corrain, has been indicted in New York for damaging a US Air National Guard C-130 Hercules at Shannon Airport in Ireland on 11 April. US prosecutors say he breached security, cut wiring and hydraulic lines, smashed cockpit instruments, struck the exterior with an axe and put ball bearings into the fuel tanks, leaving the roughly $60 million aircraft unable to fly again. He was arrested in Ireland at the time and charged there with criminal damage and trespass. Supporters say the act protested US military activity linked to the wars involving Iran and Gaza; officials have not given an official motive.

If convicted of destroying government property, O'Corrain faces up to 10 years in prison. He is not in US custody and no arraignment date has been set.

auto-a430480344bf.headline: Moldova summons Russian envoy after drones breach its airspace
auto-a430480344bf.summary:
Moldova's foreign ministry called in the Kremlin's ambassador-designate in Chișinău, Oleg Ozerov, after seven drones entered Moldovan airspace during a Russian attack on Ukraine. One drone was spotted over the capital, and at least five crashed on Moldovan territory in several villages, with no casualties reported. Moldova briefly closed its airspace, and a passenger flight was diverted toward Romania. Officials called the incursions a serious breach of sovereignty and a threat to regional security.

President Maia Sandu said Moldova lacks the defence capabilities needed to counter such drones and called for sanctions against Russia. Incursions have become more frequent, and Moldova expelled a Russian embassy member in October after an earlier drone fell near homes.

auto-0ec0a71bcfd4.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea reportedly massing troops at border, raising war concerns
auto-0ec0a71bcfd4.summary:
Ethiopian and Eritrean forces have reportedly gathered along their shared border, bringing the two armies close to each other, according to conflict monitors and people linked to militias in Tigray. Monitors reported artillery fire and armed clashes near the border town of Badme, though Reuters could not independently confirm them and Eritrea and Ethiopia did not fully address the reports.

The tensions follow fighting between Ethiopia's federal government and Tigrayan rebels, and earlier reports that Eritrean troops crossed into Tigray. auto-ca1b97dfd68e.summary:
Israel's Knesset elected Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, as speaker on Tuesday, with 66 of 120 votes, against 52 for Likud's candidate Ofir Katz. The post controls the parliamentary timetable, and Eisenkot's camp is now using it to advance bills that would undo judicial and media measures passed under Benjamin Netanyahu, who remains caretaker prime minister.

Bills to repeal those measures passed preliminary readings after Eisenkot's bloc walked out of votes on Netanyahu-camp bills, which also passed. Eisenkot has until next month to form a government, and the two Arab-majority lists backed Kahana.

auto-474924e4f3bc.headline: Trump arrives in Shenzhen for talks with Xi and a planned trilateral with Putin

Trump is due to hold bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday, then join Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a first-ever three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Agenda items include nuclear arms control, after the last US-Russia treaty expired in February, and the Iran war. US officials described the trilateral as an opening conversation with low expectations for a deal, while a Kremlin aide said Ukraine would likely come up.

Trump had earlier spent time in Manila, where he met Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and announced a new trade deal with the Philippines.

auto-c9d4b3e7672e.headline: Iraq restarts Kirkuk-Ceyhan oil pipeline to Turkey, easing Hormuz export dependence
auto-c9d4b3e7672e.summary:
Iraq has restarted crude exports through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey, shut since 2014 after Islamic State attacks. The Oil Ministry in Baghdad said pumping resumed after technical tests, with an initial flow of 120,000 barrels per day, to rise gradually to 500,000. The line gives Iraq a northern route that reduces reliance on southern terminals and the Strait of Hormuz, disrupted by the Iran war.

Iraq and Turkey agreed in August on a one-year shipping arrangement while talks on a longer deal continue. Iraq's cabinet also approved a plan to rehabilitate the pipeline, though no scope of work was given. How much the flows add to total exports remains unclear.

Beijing's foreign ministry accused Washington of overstretching national security and pledged necessary measures to protect China's interests. The commerce ministry voiced firm opposition, warned the curbs threaten global semiconductor supply chains, and threatened countermeasures.

auto-75a371bb0eef.summary:
Leaders closed the 49th ASEAN Summit and related meetings at a ceremony in Pasay City, near Manila, on November 17. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said the region's challenges, including energy, maritime security, technology and climate, are increasingly linked, and urged closer institutional ties. The Philippines formally passed the bloc's chairmanship for 2027 to Singapore. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong set the theme "Deeper Integration, Wider Partnerships" for 2027, when ASEAN marks its 60th anniversary, pledging a more unified single market and continued outreach to outside partners.

auto-e42561e28950.headline: US and Iran settle into limited clashes without full war
auto-e42561e28950.summary:
Iran and the United States have largely avoided all-out war since July, when a June memorandum of understanding collapsed, instead trading intermittent attacks and using economic pressure. Iran says it struck US military sites in Bahrain and Kuwait, and the US carried out an air strike on Qeshm island. Ukrainian forces launched two precision attacks on the Kerch bridge, the only road and rail link between southern Russia and Crimea, using drones and cruise missiles. One arch collapsed into the Kerch Strait, blocking road traffic, limiting rail to a single track, and heavily damaging roughly 200 metres of the roadway. Zelenskyy said the strikes used Ukrainian-made weapons, while a Dutch company said its cruise missiles took part. The Kremlin called the damage insignificant and said the bridge would be restored.

The bridge is a major symbol of Moscow's hold on Crimea, and its loss of use could disrupt grain and steel shipments from southern Russia. Analysts differ on the military value of the strike, with some arguing it was counterproductive.

auto-fbab7fe39b3f.headline: EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine's 2027 funding gap

auto-b6c2b925262b.headline: UN watchdog reports new North Korean enrichment building at Yongbyon

Chinese President Xi Jinping has held bilateral meetings on the sidelines, including with Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney, with both sides agreeing to ease trade barriers.
