auto-835cbaf6db83.headline: EU creates sanctions office to enforce Russia measures, names new envoy
auto-835cbaf6db83.summary:
The European Commission has formally set up a dedicated sanctions office in Brussels and named Swedish diplomat Lars Danielsson as its head, taking over from David O'Sullivan on February 6, 2027. The office is meant to shift focus from listing new targets toward enforcing existing Russia sanctions and closing loopholes, with staffing expected to rise from about 45 to 50-60. It will also take on the EU's other regimes, including those against Iran and North Korea.

The EU's finance commissioner, Maria Luis Albuquerque, said the bloc would work with member states and partners to prevent circumvention. Officials hope the centralised structure will give the envoy more weight when persuading third countries such as those in Central Asia and the Middle East to enforce sanctions.

actors.why: Tighter EU enforcement and closed loopholes add pressure on Russia's sanctions evasion
Expanded EU sanctions office brings Iran regime under closer enforcement scrutiny
North Korea sanctions now fall under the expanded EU office's remit
Centralised sanctions office strengthens the bloc's enforcement capacity and envoy's leverage

impact_points: Russia faces tighter enforcement of EU measures, including scrutiny of carve-outs and sanctions evasion routes.
Iran and North Korea come under the expanded office's remit, while third countries in Central Asia and the Middle East face more pressure to comply.

auto-e96feef20bfa.headline: French troops reportedly in Ukraine on training mission; Russia calls it direct participation
auto-e96feef20bfa.summary:
Radio France Internationale reported that French military personnel have been in Ukraine since at least summer 2026 under a confidential mission called Volia, training Ukrainian troops and maintaining equipment. Sources told AFP the personnel have no combat role, and the French military detachment in Poland serves as a gateway for them. The number of troops has not been disclosed.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Tuesday that the deployment amounted to direct participation in the war and that Moscow had conveyed its concern to Paris. France's deputy defence minister called the deployment very limited and said the claim of intent to fight was absurd.

actors.why: Accused by Russia of direct participation; France denies combat role
Gains French training and equipment maintenance support for its forces
Uses the deployment to press its warnings against European involvement
Hosts the French military detachment that serves as the gateway into Ukraine
The mission operates within the EU's military assistance framework for Ukraine

impact_points: France faces Russian accusations of direct involvement in the war, while insisting its personnel are non-combat trainers.
Ukraine gains French training and equipment support, but Russia's warnings raise the risk of wider escalation involving Europe.

auto-9b0a75331f21.headline: European officials doubt Russia's readiness for peace talks as Trump pushes ahead
auto-9b0a75331f21.summary: European diplomats and officials privately and publicly doubt that Vladimir Putin is ready to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine, despite renewed US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. The talks produced only a promised prisoner swap whose details remain unfinalised, and no date has been set for the next round. Russia has intensified strikes on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure, while Ukraine has struck deep inside Russia, drawing US criticism. European governments, including the UK, Germany and France, remain engaged mainly to avoid being sidelined by Washington.

actors.why: Facing intensified strikes on civilian infrastructure with no clear ceasefire in sight
Accused of rejecting ceasefires and continuing attacks, though it seeks to revise European security structures
Pushing for a deal and criticising Ukraine's deep strikes, but talks have stalled
Among European states preparing to join talks while doubting Moscow's intentions
Diplomats doubt Russia's sincerity while preparing to join negotiations
President Macron says Putin is betting on forcing Ukraine into submission

impact_points: Ukraine faces intensified Russian strikes on energy, water and civilian infrastructure while peace prospects remain uncertain.
European states and the EU risk being sidelined if Washington strikes a separate deal with Moscow, prompting them to stay in the talks.

auto-931f712de3e9.headline: Israeli forces push into central Gaza, displacing residents despite truce
auto-931f712de3e9.summary:
Israel's military launched a ground operation on Wednesday in central Gaza, with tanks advancing toward the Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps. The army says it is targeting Hamas infrastructure and a threat to its troops, and has closed the Salah al-Din road in the area. Residents reported artillery fire, airstrikes and drone-dropped explosives, and at least two people were wounded, with many families fleeing. Hamas called the operation a serious breach of the October 2025 ceasefire, and more than 1,600 Palestinians have reportedly been killed since that truce began.

The Israeli military says it controls over 60 percent of Gaza behind the so-called Yellow Line. Aid organisations were told by COGAT to avoid the affected zones.

actors.why: Residents forced to flee under fire; civilians killed and wounded in the assault.
Military gains ground and controls more territory, though ceasefire tensions rise.
Accused by Hamas of responsibility for the operation as ceasefire mediator.

impact_points: Palestinian civilians in central Gaza face renewed displacement and danger from the ground assault and bombardment.
The October 2025 ceasefire is under strain, with Hamas and the US-mediated deal at risk of collapse.

auto-1981c689dc1c.headline: Drone attacks hit Iranian Kurdish opposition bases in Iraq's Kurdistan region
auto-1981c689dc1c.summary: Two explosives-laden drones struck bases of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups in Sulaymaniyah, in Iraq's autonomous Kurdistan region, security sources told Reuters. Iran has repeatedly hit such groups on Iraqi soil, accusing them of carrying out attacks inside Iran. A separate report said a drone also targeted a base in the Dokan area, though it gave no details on who was responsible or on casualties. Separately, an alert system was triggered after a drone flew over the Khor Mor gas field in the same region. The reporting did not confirm the attackers.

actors.why: Drone strikes on its Kurdistan region territory and a gas field alert threaten its sovereignty and security
Accused by reports of repeatedly striking opposition groups on Iraqi soil

impact_points: Iraq's Kurdistan region faces repeated strikes on its territory, raising security concerns for its authorities and residents.
Iranian Kurdish opposition groups are pressured by the attacks, which Tehran links to alleged operations inside Iran.

auto-2c9f94ec0888.headline: Israeli settlers' gunfire kills Palestinian woman in West Bank village near Jericho
auto-2c9f94ec0888.summary:
A 72 or 73-year-old Palestinian woman, reported under varying names, was shot dead outside her home in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, a village west of Jericho in the occupied West Bank. Residents say armed settlers fired after a confrontation, and several relatives, including her son, were wounded. The settlers had recently taken over eight homes in the village after moving in earlier this month.

The Israeli military gave a different account, saying Palestinians rammed an Israeli vehicle and rocks were thrown, prompting troops to fire. A military source later said the woman was shot by an Israeli civilian, and police opened an investigation. Accounts of the events could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Resident killed and relatives wounded; farmland access lost after settler takeover
Settler shooting under police investigation; international criticism over settlements and violence

impact_points: Palestinian residents of al-Duyuk al-Tahta face killings, injuries, lost farmland and fear of further settler attacks.
Israel faces international scrutiny over settler violence, settlement expansion, and its police investigation into the shooting.

auto-06af0717576f.headline: Taiwan watches US-China-Russia summit talks as Russian aircraft approach
auto-06af0717576f.summary:
Taiwan says it is in close contact with Washington ahead of a planned three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Taipei said it welcomes efforts that help manage the risks of authoritarian expansion, while reiterating its aim to strengthen self-defense and preserve the status quo. Taiwan's envoy, Stan Shih, is attending the summit, the first time he has represented Taiwan there since 2007.

Taiwan also reported two Russian military aircraft entering its air defence identification zone from the northeast, and Japan said two Russian aircraft briefly entered its airspace northwest of Fukuoka. China has also been carrying out large, unannounced military drills around Taiwan, which Taipei describes as silent intimidation.

actors.why: Faces military pressure and uncertainty over US support during summit diplomacy
Hosts a leader-level meeting with China and Russia, but holds back Taiwan arms sale
Gains a unprecedented three-way meeting while keeping military pressure on Taiwan
Joins a high-profile meeting while sending military aircraft near Taiwan and Japan
Monitors Russian aircraft entering its airspace near Fukuoka

impact_points: Taiwan faces rising Chinese military pressure and uncertainty over US backing, including a paused arms sale.
Japan and Taiwan both face Russian military flights near their airspace, adding to regional security concerns.

auto-86ac7e96aeea.headline: Houthis advance near Aden as Yemeni government forces mount counteroffensive
auto-86ac7e96aeea.summary:
Houthi rebels have pushed to about 60 kilometres from Aden, the southern port serving as Yemen's interim government capital, after seizing the western coast and positions near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Analysts say the rebels may prefer to encircle or besiege the city rather than storm it, using pressure to force talks. The Saudi-led coalition carried out air strikes on rebel areas, which the Houthis said killed at least 17 people.

Yemen's army said it had carried out 661 attacks on Houthi positions in Taiz, Marib, al-Jawf and southern fronts under its "Dawn of Yemen" offensive, claiming 173 fighters were killed or wounded. Parliament also approved a bill designating the Houthis a terrorist organisation, which awaits enactment by the Presidential Leadership Council. The army's casualty claims could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Government could lose Aden, its last major stronghold, while Houthis gain ground
Houthi blockade and missile threats against oil facilities after ceasefire collapse
Iran-backed Houthis gain territory and leverage over Red Sea shipping routes
UAE-backed separatists are needed by Saudi Arabia to help defend Aden

impact_points: Yemen's internationally recognised government faces losing its last major stronghold, Aden, and its remaining influence.
Saudi Arabia faces renewed Houthi pressure, including a naval blockade and missile strikes on its oil facilities since the ceasefire collapsed.

auto-c4e3048fab10.headline: US officials reject links between a string of tech outages
auto-c4e3048fab10.summary:
Over the past week, a run of technology failures hit the United States, including a Microsoft email outage, a nationwide halt to air travel, disruptions at JPMorgan Chase and United Airlines, an Apple services outage, and a brief loss of a National Security Agency network. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told a House committee the incidents were separate maintenance and upgrade problems rather than a coordinated or state-sponsored attack, while noting that threats from Iran had risen. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was zero evidence linking them to hostile actors, as criticism of the administration's handling mounted.

Cybersecurity researchers said the outages showed how fragile ageing infrastructure has become under pressure from AI-driven change, and flagged a separate Java vulnerability. Companies and agencies involved have said the causes were internal, not cyberattacks.

actors.why: Faces criticism over its response, though officials deny any hostile cause.
Clayton says threats from Iran have increased, though not linked to the outages.

impact_points: The US government faces growing public and congressional pressure over how it handled the disruptions and communicated about them.
Airlines, banks and tech firms must now shore up legacy systems, as upgrades have triggered failures and raised security concerns.

auto-18de0f96a13d.headline: US officials push back on long Iran war as Navy chief faces criticism
auto-18de0f96a13d.summary:
US Vice President JD Vance said in a Fox News interview that Washington does not intend to keep fighting Iran for years, rejecting talk of a decade-long or even two-year commitment. He acknowledged the war's political cost, including its effect on fuel and energy prices, and blamed neoconservatives for pushing toward an open-ended conflict.

In a Senate hearing, Democrats accused acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, who is seeking confirmation, of being too deferential to the Trump administration over the Iran war and of downplaying the strain on sailors' mental health. The naval blockade of Iran and the stalemate around the Strait of Hormuz also came under scrutiny.

actors.why: Under US naval blockade and strikes, with conventional forces heavily damaged
Faces political costs, energy price pressure and scrutiny over an open-ended war
Regional ally whose security interests align with US pressure on Iran

impact_points: Iran faces a US naval blockade and strikes, with its conventional military heavily damaged, according to US officials.
US sailors and Navy leadership face scrutiny over mental health strain and the war's costs, while American energy prices rise.

auto-b23aeca3b505.headline: Israeli spy chief pushed for joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, sources say
auto-b23aeca3b505.summary:
Mossad director Roman Gofman reportedly urged US officials in Washington last week to join Israel in strikes on Iran, according to two people briefed on the visit. He also met envoy Steve Witkoff in Miami and briefed officials on Israeli intelligence, reportedly including on Iran's nuclear programme. Separately, US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper met Israeli military leaders in Tel Aviv on Wednesday for a joint regional security assessment focused on Iran. The Israeli military described the talks as routine, and Trump has reportedly held off on new strikes.

The contacts come amid a fragile ceasefire in a war that began in late February, with recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran affecting Gulf states including Kuwait and Bahrain. A US blockade on Iranian oil exports was reimposed in July, and the US is tightening enforcement at sea. Sources said Israel's military assesses Iran poses no imminent threat.

actors.why: Israel seeks to push Washington toward joint strikes on Iran
Washington weighs strikes while pressing blockade and reviewing options
Iran faces blockade pressure and threat of renewed US-Israeli strikes
Kuwait was targeted by Iranian aerial attacks, raising security risks
Bahrain repelled Iranian aerial attacks, facing ongoing regional threat

impact_points: Iran faces renewed pressure from US sanctions, blockades and possible Israeli-backed military escalation.
Gulf states such as Kuwait and Bahrain risk further Iranian retaliation if US-Israeli strikes resume.

auto-8f459b95f58b.headline: Iraq's prime minister moves against Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah militia over oil smuggling
auto-8f459b95f58b.summary:
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered security forces to prepare to confront Kataib Hezbollah, the most powerful Iran-aligned armed group in the country. Officials accuse the group of running an oil smuggling ring that diverted hundreds of millions of dollars in state oil, a charge Kataib Hezbollah rejects. Zaidi also told forces to deploy around Jurf al-Nasr and block tankers from leaving the area, and a senior Iraqi official reportedly gave the group until Friday to leave the town.

The Quds Force commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, Esmail Qaani, has arrived in Iraq to seek a settlement, meeting Zaidi and Coordination Framework parties. Some Iraqi leaders oppose armed clashes before a political deal is reached, and a Kataib Hezbollah commander vowed the group will not withdraw.

actors.why: Prime minister moves to confront militia over oil smuggling, risking armed clashes
Its Revolutionary Guards' Quds Force commander intervenes to protect proxy Kataib Hezbollah

impact_points: Iraq faces a possible direct confrontation between government troops and a heavily armed militia that holds state-salaried positions.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards and its proxy network face the loss of a key financial and military ally in Iraq.

auto-26a5128d499f.headline: EU to hold off on UK long-term ties talks until Burnham clarifies Brexit direction
auto-26a5128d499f.summary: EU diplomats say Brussels will not open talks with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Britain's longer-term relationship with the bloc until London decides whether it wants to reverse Brexit. They describe the piecemeal reset approach as reaching its limits, and want clarity before further negotiation. A UK-EU summit on Friday is expected to produce a joint statement signalling future talks on energy markets, migration and defence. Burnham said the options for ties would take time and be decided in the next parliament.

actors.why: Burnham delays options, facing EU pause and pressure within his own party
Brussels gains leverage by pausing talks until London offers clarity

impact_points: The European Union faces delays in shaping its future relationship with Britain until London sets a clear course.
The UK government must decide between options such as the status quo, customs union, single market or full rejoining.

auto-04fcff4381a9.headline: Ukrainian and Russian troops fight underground in a Soviet-era gas pipeline
auto-04fcff4381a9.summary:
For seven months, Ukrainian forces have been fighting Russian troops inside an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region, where the narrow tunnel offers shelter from the drones dominating the front line. The BBC, the first international broadcaster allowed into the pipeline, reported from near Kupyansk with a Ukrainian brigade. The account describes a subterranean battle in cramped conditions where crawling is the only movement possible.

The story is a ground-level view of a war that has stalled above the surface, as drones make advances nearly impossible for either side.

actors.why: Troops hold ground in the pipeline despite a stalled front line
Advances are blocked by drones and the underground fighting continues

impact_points: Ukraine's forces are holding positions underground, using the pipeline to avoid drone attacks that block advances above ground.
Russia faces the same stalemate, as drone warfare makes it difficult to push forward on the Kharkiv front.

auto-1305a83350b7.headline: Russian drone strike on Kharkiv Oblast market wounds eleven, including a child
auto-1305a83350b7.summary: A Russian drone attack hit a market in Zlatopil, in Kharkiv Oblast, on 18 November, setting market stalls alight across roughly 500 square metres. Regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said at least 11 people were hurt, including an 11-year-old boy, and that one woman was in serious condition while the rest had moderate injuries. Local officials said shops, homes, industrial premises and cars were also damaged, and that an energy facility was reportedly struck. Emergency crews were still working at the site amid concern about repeat attacks.

actors.why: Civilians injured and local market, shops and energy facility damaged by drone strike.
Russian drones struck a civilian market, drawing criticism for targeting non-military sites.

impact_points: Ukraine's civilians in Kharkiv Oblast face renewed danger, with a child among those wounded in a market.
Local energy and commercial infrastructure in Zlatopil suffered damage, adding pressure on Ukrainian recovery efforts.

auto-6957726febe5.headline: Ukrainian strike collapses Crimean Bridge arch; Russia pledges rebuild
auto-6957726febe5.summary:
Ukrainian forces struck the Crimean Bridge over two days, bringing down a key road arch into the Kerch Strait on 17 November. Officials in Kyiv said the attack was carried out in stages, destroying air defences and radars before long-range missiles and drones hit the structure. An unnamed Ukrainian officer told The Times the operation ran without Starlink, using Ukraine's own communications. Russia's spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would be rebuilt stronger, though engineers quoted by the BBC described the damage as severe and repairs as lengthy.

The strike came just before a planned meeting between Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump. Crimea's road link is now largely closed, leaving ferries and a land corridor as the main routes. Russia also reported record drone attacks on its territory and strikes on Kyiv's bridges.

actors.why: Key Crimea link collapsed, forcing reliance on ferries and a land corridor.
Strike demonstrates long-range reach and disrupts Russia's Crimea logistics.

impact_points: Russia loses a key transport link to Crimea, relying on ferries and a land corridor.
Ukraine demonstrates it can reach heavily defended Russian infrastructure, raising pressure on Moscow's military and symbolic standing.

auto-2d22d9469e5a.headline: US and Venezuela move to restore military ties during Hegseth visit
auto-2d22d9469e5a.summary:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited Venezuela and said the two countries had agreed to re-establish military relations. He met the country's interim leaders during the trip, and the reporting describes the agreement as a step toward expanded defence cooperation. The coverage summarised here gives no further details of the terms, timeline or specific programmes involved.

The visit marks a notable shift in ties between Washington and Caracas, which had been strained for years. The sources reviewed do not indicate how the arrangement would be implemented.

actors.why: Restores military ties with the US, gaining international backing for interim leadership
Expands defence influence and cooperation in Latin America through renewed Venezuelan ties

impact_points: Venezuela's interim leadership gains a closer security partnership with Washington, potentially strengthening its international standing.
The United States expands its military footprint and influence in Latin America, a region it has long treated as a strategic priority.

auto-fb29d8ec9e39.headline: Ukraine and Western allies hold talks on ending the war with Russia
auto-fb29d8ec9e39.summary: Ukraine held online discussions with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and European representatives on ending the war with Russia. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the talks not easy but said participants agreed to meet in Berlin with the Coalition of the Willing, a group of Ukraine's supporters. Russia disputed that European representatives would join future rounds, saying no date had been set for the next round. Meanwhile, strikes were reported on bridges in Kyiv and Ukraine launched large drone attacks on Russian targets.

actors.why: Seeks peace talks and support while facing strikes on Kyiv bridges
Faces new EU sanctions and Ukrainian drone strikes on its territory
Envoys push progress talks, though Russia rejected expanded European role
Adds 113 sanctions on Russia and pushes Ukraine's path to membership

impact_points: Ukraine faces continued Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges while seeking a negotiated end to the war.
Russia is under 113 new EU sanctions, while Moscow insists on a lasting peace rather than a temporary ceasefire.

auto-0204f7d545ec.headline: Russian strikes across Ukraine kill several people and cut power in regions
auto-0204f7d545ec.summary:
Russian air and drone attacks across Ukraine killed at least five people over a single day, according to local authorities, with four of the deaths in the southern city of Odesa, where officials said strikes hit the historic centre and a UNESCO-protected area. Ukrainian officials also reported strikes on energy infrastructure, leaving settlements in several regions without power. The attacks followed a Ukrainian strike on Russia's Kerch Bridge that killed two people, while Ukraine's Energy Ministry says Russia has launched over 1,000 attacks on energy sites since September.

At the same time, the European Commission proposed a 45 billion euro loan to help Ukraine cover a funding gap for next year, repayable only once Russia pays reparations. Talks involving the US, Ukraine and European leaders were also set to take place in Berlin.

actors.why: Deaths, blackouts and damaged energy grid, plus new EU loan support
Kerch Bridge damaged and collapsed after Ukrainian strike
Proposed 45 billion euro loan to Ukraine, repayable after Russian reparations

impact_points: Ukraine faces deadly strikes and widespread blackouts, with its energy grid under repeated attack ahead of winter.
Russia faces damage to the Kerch Bridge, a key road and rail link to occupied Crimea, after the Ukrainian strike.

auto-a360bbf330bf.headline: US court voids rule capping stays for foreign students and reporters
auto-a360bbf330bf.summary: A federal judge in Massachusetts has vacated a Department of Homeland Security rule that would have capped how long foreign students and visiting journalists could remain in the United States. Judge Dennis Saylor found the policy arbitrary and unlawful, saying the government had not shown widespread visa fraud or a national security basis for it. Under the rule, students would have been limited to four years and journalists to about eight months, replacing the open-ended duration-of-status stamp. The administration may still appeal, and a higher court is already being asked to review the temporary block issued in September.

actors.why: Court blocks DHS rule; administration can still appeal the ruling
Chinese journalists would have received only 90-day stays; the rule is blocked

impact_points: The United States government and DHS lose the stricter visa limits they had planned for students and journalists.
Foreign students, reporters and universities keep the current flexible stay arrangements, while campuses and press groups see the ruling as a win.

auto-ebfe974925a3.headline: Ecuadorian fishers sue US over March drone strike on their boat
auto-ebfe974925a3.summary:
A group of Ecuadorian fishermen has filed a lawsuit in a Pennsylvania federal court against the Trump administration over a drone strike in March that sank their vessel, La Negra Francisca Duarte II, and injured crew members. The complaint seeks financial compensation and asks the court to halt the US campaign of strikes on alleged drug boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific.

The US government has not claimed responsibility for this or two other Ecuadorian vessels sunk recently, though a Washington Post report in August suggested the CIA was involved. The wider campaign since September 2025 has reportedly killed at least 244 people, and families of victims have also taken legal action.

actors.why: Ecuadorian fishermen lost their boat and were injured; Quito has offered little help.
Faces a lawsuit and criticism over lethal strikes and lack of transparency.
Families of Trinidad and Tobago workers killed in similar strikes have also sued in US court.
Family of a missing Colombian fisherman filed a rights complaint over the strikes.

impact_points: Ecuador's fishing community faces lost livelihoods and injuries, with the captain saying little help has come from Ecuador.
The United States faces legal challenges and scrutiny over transparency and the legality of its lethal boat strike campaign.

auto-4bdd173562ee.headline: Irishman charged in US over alleged axe attack on military transport plane
auto-4bdd173562ee.summary: A 48-year-old Irishman, Daithi O'Corrain, has been indicted in New York on charges of destroying US government property after an alleged attack on a US Air National Guard C-130 Hercules at Shannon Airport in Ireland on 11 April. Prosecutors say he breached the perimeter, cut wiring and hydraulic lines, smashed cockpit gauges, poured ball bearings into fuel tanks and struck the exterior with an axe, leaving the roughly $60 million aircraft unable to fly again. He was arrested at the scene by Irish police, who charged him with criminal damage. He is not in US custody, and the charge carries up to 10 years in prison. Supporters describe him as an anti-war activist.

actors.why: Loses a $60 million aircraft and faces a claimed threat to military security
Shannon Airport security breached; local police made the arrest and charge

impact_points: The United States loses a roughly $60 million military transport aircraft that will not return to flight.
Ireland faces renewed scrutiny of security at Shannon Airport, a key hub for US military personnel and a frequent site of protest.

auto-910b06a8a1f4.headline: Hegseth visits Caracas, pledges renewed military ties and a drug crackdown
auto-910b06a8a1f4.summary:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, the highest-level American trip since Nicolás Maduro was seized by US forces in January. Hegseth said defence cooperation between the two militaries would be restored and expanded, and he met Venezuela's interim leader Delcy Rodríguez, who has governed with Washington's backing. He also praised the seizure of Maduro, who faces trial in New York, and promised to pursue drug traffickers in the region.

The trip continued to Colombia, where Hegseth also pledged action against drug networks. Critics in Venezuela say the visit underlines Washington's influence, while the country's pro-democracy opposition remains concerned about political prisoners and the lack of an election date.

actors.why: Gains US backing and renewed military ties, but faces criticism over sovereignty.
Restores influence in Venezuela, secures oil deal and expands regional military reach.
Deepens US military cooperation against drug-running guerrillas and traffickers.

impact_points: Venezuela's interim government under Delcy Rodríguez gains US backing and renewed military ties, though critics see loss of sovereignty.
Colombia gains expanded US anti-drug cooperation, while regional armed groups and drug traffickers face heightened US pressure.

auto-af97680afe18.headline: US charges Russian man with spying on Silicon Valley defence firm aiding Ukraine
auto-af97680afe18.summary: US prosecutors have charged Igor D'iu, a Russian national, with acting as an agent of a foreign government. He is accused of running a Russia-directed surveillance operation against employees of a Palo Alto technology and defence company that supplies software to Ukraine. The firm is not named in the charging documents, though CBS News reported it as Palantir Technologies, which did not respond to a request for comment. Prosecutors say he was recruited via Telegram, entered the US unlawfully from Mexico, and faces fraud, stalking and espionage-related charges. He has been held since 2 November.

actors.why: Accused of directing a spy operation against a US firm aiding Ukraine
Arrest shows enforcement against foreign intelligence on its soil
Firm's software supporting Ukraine was the alleged target of the spying

impact_points: Russia faces a US espionage case alleging Moscow targeted a firm helping Ukraine against it.
Palo Alto-area defence technology employees and their families face alleged surveillance, stalking and intimidation by a state-directed agent.

auto-330f1e4a51ca.headline: Settler gunfire kills elderly Palestinian woman near Jericho in West Bank
auto-330f1e4a51ca.summary: A 72-year-old Palestinian woman was shot dead and several relatives were wounded in the village of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho, in the occupied West Bank. Local residents and witnesses say armed Israeli settlers opened fire outside her home, days after a group moved into eight houses there. The Israeli military gave a different account, describing a Palestinian car-ramming and rock-throwing before troops fired, and later said the woman was shot by an Israeli civilian. Israeli police said they had opened an investigation, and the accounts could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Resident killed and relatives wounded; farmland access lost in the village
Settler violence and conflicting military account draw criticism and a police probe

impact_points: Palestinian residents of al-Duyuk al-Tahta face mounting danger and loss of farmland since settlers moved in.
Israel faces scrutiny over settler violence and its military's conflicting account, which the EU and other critics say undermines accountability.

auto-1d8d698944cd.headline: China hosts APEC summit in Shenzhen amid US-China trade tensions
auto-1d8d698944cd.summary:
China is hosting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, using the tech-focused city to showcase its economic rise and its view of multilateral trade. Leaders are holding bilateral meetings, and Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney and Xi Jinping agreed to reduce trade barriers, including tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood. The most closely watched encounter is a planned trilateral meeting with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, while the US has moved to further restrict Chinese access to advanced AI chips, a step that could strain the fragile tariff truce.

Analysts quoted in coverage described the trade truce as fragile, with few expecting a further extension at the summit. Reporting also said Beijing has tightly controlled the format, with some diplomats complaining it limits open discussion.

actors.why: Hosts summit, showcases economic rise and courts leaders amid US trade pressure
New AI chip restrictions risk straining the tariff truce with China
Secures tariff relief on pork, fish and seafood exports to China
Expected to join a high-profile trilateral meeting with Xi and Trump
Leader aligns with Beijing by closing Taiwan's office in the country

impact_points: China gains a platform to promote its trade and multilateral stance while confronting US trade measures.
Canada secures tariff relief on pork, fish and seafood exports in exchange for steel and aluminium exemptions extended to China.

auto-3acc714842a0.headline: Saudi-led coalition strikes dozens of Houthi sites as Yemen fighting intensifies
auto-3acc714842a0.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition says it carried out a precision operation against roughly 60 Houthi military targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah, Amran and Saada, including tunnels used to store and build ballistic missiles. The strikes came as Houthi forces advanced toward Aden, the temporary seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government, prompting government troops to pull back from areas near the Bab al-Mandeb strait. Fierce fighting was also reported in Taiz and Lahij, where local authorities accuse the Houthis of shelling civilians and restricting medical supplies.

Saudi Arabia said it intercepted Houthi cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh, while the Houthis claimed attacks on oil and radar sites in the kingdom. Saudi authorities had not confirmed those claims. The coalition's figures and the Houthi claims could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Facing Houthi missile and drone attacks on Riyadh and oil infrastructure, while leading strikes
Houthi advances toward Aden and fighting in Taiz cause civilian harm and territorial losses

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces repeated Houthi missile and drone strikes on cities, oil and military infrastructure.
Yemen's government and civilians in Taiz face advancing Houthi forces, sieges and worsening access to medicine.

auto-84722dd8f6b3.headline: Drone strikes hit two Russian oil refineries in Krasnodar Krai, four injured
auto-84722dd8f6b3.summary:
Drones struck Krasnodar Krai in southern Russia on the morning of November 18, injuring four people in the Seversky district, according to the regional operational headquarters. Fires broke out at two facilities after drone debris fell, though authorities did not name the sites. Fragments also landed at nine addresses, including private yards and streets.

The district hosts the Afipsky and Ilsky oil refineries, which local Ukrainian-monitoring Telegram channels and an independent outlet said were the likely targets, based on reports of fires, flashes and explosions. These refineries have been hit repeatedly by Ukrainian drones. The reporting could not independently confirm which plants were struck.

actors.why: Refineries set on fire, four injured, debris scattered across residential areas.
Drone strikes reportedly hit Russian energy infrastructure, continuing its campaign against refineries.

impact_points: Russia faces damage to its refining capacity and injuries to civilians in Krasnodar Krai.
Russia's energy sector and local residents in the Seversky district face disruption from the fires and debris.

auto-df8c3e566358.headline: EU weighs entry ban on Russian war veterans; Moscow threatens Kallas
auto-df8c3e566358.summary: The European Union is still discussing a ban on entry for Russians who have fought in the war in Ukraine. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said at a Brussels press conference that Russia keeps detailed records of such personnel, so obtaining their data would likely be straightforward. She did not explain the technical methods in detail, pointing to intelligence services. Russia's State Duma speaker, Vyacheslav Volodin, responded that Kallas had announced an intention to steal personal data and claimed she could face up to about 20 years in prison. Separately, the EU expanded its Russia sanctions list, targeting refineries, petrochemical plants and dozens of banks, and is preparing a 22nd package.

actors.why: Faces expanded EU sanctions and a proposed entry ban on its war veterans
Pursuing a veterans entry ban and new sanctions, though the ban remains under discussion

impact_points: Russia faces possible EU entry restrictions on its veterans and expanded sanctions on energy and banking firms.
Russian officials, including Volodin, accuse Kallas and the EU of unlawful data gathering, escalating the diplomatic dispute.

auto-9f46dff3c535.headline: US probes Singapore firm Megaspeed over alleged Nvidia chip diversion to China
auto-9f46dff3c535.summary:
The US Justice and Commerce departments confirmed a criminal investigation into Singapore-based Megaspeed, suspected of helping send Nvidia AI chips to China in breach of export controls. The probe began in 2024, and Nvidia placed Megaspeed on a no-sell list in June 2025 after an on-site check with Singaporean police. The inquiry has surfaced alongside a scandal that led Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang to step down as chief executive, following reports of an affair with a former Megaspeed executive whom US officials suspect of spying for Beijing, which denies this.

Washington has also tightened rules, requiring licences for data centres worldwide that supply large computing power to Chinese firms and for chip shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. Singapore said it is studying the measure and seeking trusted access for its companies.

actors.why: Tightened export curbs and a criminal probe reinforce its tech-competition strategy against China
Firm under investigation and new US licence requirements threaten its reputation and business access
Loses easier access to rented AI computing power and faces spying allegations it denies

impact_points: Singapore faces reputational damage as a rules-based business hub, and its firms now need US licences for advanced chips.
China loses easier access to advanced AI chips through overseas data centres, while Nvidia and Megaspeed face legal and commercial fallout.

auto-64b1d1dad1d1.headline: US charges Russian man with spying on Silicon Valley firm aiding Ukraine
auto-64b1d1dad1d1.summary:
A Russian national, Igor D'iu, has been arrested in California and charged with acting as an agent of a foreign government, stalking and fraud. US prosecutors say he was recruited and funded by Russia to watch employees of an unnamed Palo Alto technology and defence company that supplies Ukraine. Officials allege he used surveillance, tracking devices and fake identities, and took instructions over Telegram. FBI agents seized cash and fake and Russian passports in an October raid. He is due in federal court on November 24.

If convicted on all counts, D'iu could face up to 21 years in prison. US officials described the alleged plot as a violation of American sovereignty.

actors.why: Accused of directing a state-funded spying operation on US soil against a Ukraine-supporting firm.
Prosecutors charged a Russian agent and pledged to stop foreign intelligence bases in Silicon Valley.
The targeted firm supplies Ukraine's war effort, so the alleged plot aimed at weakening that support.
Alleged route used by the suspect to reach the United States, drawing scrutiny over border security.

impact_points: Russia faces US accusations of state-directed intelligence operations on American soil targeting a firm aiding Ukraine.
Ukraine's defence supply chain is exposed, as the firm's employees were allegedly targeted for their support to Kyiv.

auto-d974045a4d2d.headline: Iran and US trade strikes near Gulf bases as Hormuz tensions persist
auto-d974045a4d2d.summary:
Iranian forces have struck military sites in Bahrain and Kuwait, while US forces hit military and radar installations in southern Iran after attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The exchanges followed US strikes on the port of Sirik and Qeshm Island. Analysts say the current standoff is unstable and could escalate into full-scale war again, with Israel possibly rejoining. Iran says the US naval blockade and sanctions are hurting its trade. Mediators including Qatar and Pakistan are trying to break a stalemate over Hormuz access and sanctions relief.

Separately, US Vice President JD Vance told Fox News the Trump administration will not let the Iran conflict become a prolonged 'forever war', while acknowledging higher energy prices as a political cost.

Faces political costs from energy prices while pressing its blockade and sanctions
Targeted by Iranian drones at Riffa Air Base after hosting US forces
Reported incoming drones aimed at US equipment at Ali Al Salem Air Base

Could rejoin strikes on Iran if fighting escalates into full-scale war

impact_points: Bahrain and Kuwait, which host US forces, face renewed Iranian drone attacks on their bases.
Gulf shipping and the UAE, whose vessels were hit in Hormuz, face continued risk to oil exports.

auto-52356b076395.headline: EU weighs tough or flexible terms for Ukraine talks as Russia rejects European seats
auto-52356b076395.summary: EU leaders have picked a negotiating team for Ukraine talks, including France, Germany, Italy, Poland, the UK, and top NATO and EU officials. They now disagree on what that team should demand. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas wants maximal demands first, while Austria proposes confidence-building steps such as partial ceasefires and a monitoring forum. Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said there is no question of European participation in negotiating rounds, responding to new EU sanctions. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov accused European leaders of seeking strategic defeat of Russia.

actors.why: Rejects European role and frames EU as seeking to defeat Russia strategically
Its future security depends on European backing, which is now divided and sidelined
Struggles to agree on red lines and is excluded by Moscow from talks

Outside the negotiating team but pushing ideas to lower tensions with Russia

impact_points: Ukraine faces an unresolved fight in Europe over what terms its backers will press for in talks.
Russia is rejecting a European role, leaving the EU with little influence over any negotiated settlement.

auto-b4c1564ff4f5.headline: Myanmar's leader signals rethink of ASEAN ties while keeping talks open
auto-b4c1564ff4f5.summary:
Myanmar's president, Min Aung Hlaing, said on Wednesday that he is reconsidering the country's relationship with the Southeast Asian bloc ASEAN, though he will keep talking with its member states. Speaking to parliament, the former junta chief, who took power in a 2021 coup that sparked a nationwide civil war, also announced a peace conference planned for February, aimed at ending the fighting during his five-year term.

Min Aung Hlaing has pushed for re-engagement with the 11-member bloc, which has kept Myanmar's leadership out of its summits since the coup. ASEAN leaders said on Sunday they could gradually restore Myanmar's full political representation if progress is made on a longstanding plan to resolve the crisis.

actors.why: Leader may distance the country from ASEAN; peace conference planned to end fighting
Neighbour and ASEAN member hosting Myanmar's leader in recent diplomacy

impact_points: Myanmar risks further diplomatic isolation from ASEAN if its review leads to a breakdown in ties.
ASEAN members such as Malaysia face a dilemma over engaging a leadership they have kept out of summits.

auto-f5f01ddad7d7.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea face growing risk of direct war along border
auto-f5f01ddad7d7.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea have reportedly massed troops along their shared frontier, and monitors say the two armies are now within striking distance of each other. Conflict observers and sources linked to armed groups in Tigray describe skirmishes, artillery fire and drone strikes near the border town of Badme, though some of these reports could not be independently confirmed and one source disputed them. Eritrean forces are said to have entered Tigray in support of rebels fighting Ethiopia's federal government, while Eritrea denies any incursion and accuses Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade.

Accused of backing rebels and facing a possible invasion from Ethiopia

impact_points: Ethiopia faces the risk of a new war with Eritrea while still fighting Tigrayan rebels at home.
Eritrea, its smaller neighbour, could be drawn deeper into the Tigray conflict, raising the threat of wider regional instability.

auto-b3b52d5506b6.headline: Iran says it downed a drone over the Strait of Hormuz
auto-b3b52d5506b6.summary: Iran's Army Air Defence said it shot down a drone over the Strait of Hormuz on a Tuesday evening, in a statement issued by the army's public relations office. The army described the aircraft as a Lucas drone and said it was destroyed by domestically built air defence systems under the country's integrated air defence network. Separately, an analysis by the Atlantic Council's Elisabeth Braw notes that US navy escorts cannot protect every vessel crossing the strait, and that incidents there have risen sharply, with the most recorded in October. The drone claim could not be independently verified in the reporting provided.

Neighbouring state on the strait, exposed to rising regional tension

impact_points: Iran is pressing its claim of control over the strait, a key route for global oil shipments.
Shipping companies and vessels transiting Hormuz face rising risk as US escort coverage remains limited.

auto-6e9317402204.headline: World court set to rule on Rohingya genocide claims against Myanmar
auto-6e9317402204.summary: The International Court of Justice in The Hague will deliver its judgment on Thursday in The Gambia's case accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. The Gambia says Myanmar's 2017 military offensive in Rakhine State was meant to destroy the group, which drove at least 730,000 people into Bangladesh. Myanmar denies genocidal intent, calling its operations a counterinsurgency response. The ruling is final and cannot be appealed, though the court has limited means to enforce it, and it could be the first time the court finds a state guilty of genocide.

actors.why: Faces a possible genocide finding and orders to prosecute, compensate and allow returns.
Hosts about 1.2 million Rohingya refugees who may await any return arrangements.
Brought the case with OIC backing, gaining a major legal victory if the court rules in its favour.

impact_points: Myanmar faces a possible first-ever ICJ finding that a state committed genocide, with lasting diplomatic and legal consequences.
Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh and those remaining in Myanmar could see justice, reparations or safe-return measures shaped by the ruling.

auto-7028011f0916.headline: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi sites as Yemen fighting and Saudi missile threats grow
auto-7028011f0916.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition says it carried out a precision operation against 60 Houthi military targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah, Amran and Saada, destroying tunnels used for missile storage and workshops. The strikes came as the Houthis advanced toward Aden, the temporary seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government, which has pulled back from parts of the Taiz coast. Fighting also resumed in Lahij, and Taiz authorities accused the Houthis of shelling civilians and blocking medical supplies.

The coalition said it intercepted Houthi cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh, while Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed attacks on Saudi oil pumping stations and a radar site. Saudi authorities had not confirmed those claims, and alerts sounded in several southern Saudi cities.

actors.why: Houthi missiles and drones target Riyadh, oil sites and southern cities, though interceptions continue
Houthi advance toward Aden and coalition airstrikes deepen fighting and civilian suffering

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces repeated Houthi missile and drone attacks on its cities, military sites and oil infrastructure.
Yemen's internationally recognised government is under pressure as Houthi forces push toward its temporary capital, Aden.

auto-a77b0b376fd2.headline: Israeli parliament picks Eisenkot ally as speaker, opening path to reverse Netanyahu policies
auto-a77b0b376fd2.summary:
Israel's Knesset elected Matan Kahana, an ally of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, as its new speaker, with 66 of 120 lawmakers voting for him. Likud's candidate, Ofir Katz, received 52 votes. The speaker controls the parliamentary timetable, so Kahana's election gives the anti-Netanyahu bloc leverage to fast-track bills.

Eisenkot, who has until next month to form a government, wants to repeal judicial reforms pushed through under Netanyahu and set up a state inquiry into the security failures before the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. Netanyahu, who is caretaker prime minister, has rejected an independent probe. Neither bloc won a majority in the October election.

actors.why: Parliament shifts toward reversing judicial reforms and planning a security inquiry

impact_points: Israel's judiciary and media rules could be rolled back, weakening the Netanyahu-era political control over courts and media.
Netanyahu faces a setback to his legislative agenda and ongoing corruption case pressures, while Eisenkot's camp gains momentum.

auto-978d0793186b.headline: Myanmar's leader signals rethink of ASEAN ties after summit snub
auto-978d0793186b.summary: Myanmar's president Min Aung Hlaing told parliament his administration is reviewing its relationship with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, accusing the bloc of singling his country out. The comments followed an ASEAN summit in Manila where the ten other members kept Myanmar barred from summits and foreign ministers' meetings, while agreeing to a more flexible engagement approach and bilateral outreach. Min Aung Hlaing said Myanmar would keep talking with member states and plans a peace conference in February 2028. Some analysts see a possible withdrawal threat as more of a propaganda signal than a realistic option.

ASEAN must balance its demand for progress on the Five-Point Consensus against gradual normalisation with Myanmar.

auto-46dee26d4dc5.headline: Israeli spy chief pushed Washington for joint strikes on Iran, sources say
auto-46dee26d4dc5.summary: Sources briefed on the trip say Mossad chief Roman Gofman urged US officials in Washington and Miami last week to join Israel in strikes on Iran, sharing Israeli intelligence on Tehran's nuclear programme. Separately, US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper visited Israel and met IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir and Gofman for a security assessment focused on Iran. The Israeli military described the visit as routine, while a White House official said economic pressure was working and major combat was not needed.

auto-bfda2483905c.headline: Takaichi and Putin hold brief talks on sidelines of Shenzhen summit
auto-bfda2483905c.summary:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, on November 18, according to a Japanese foreign ministry official. It was their first face-to-face talks since Takaichi took office last year, at a time when relations between Tokyo and Moscow have deteriorated.

The official said Takaichi raised Japan's positions on a Japanese journalist detained in Russia on spying allegations and the recent seizure of Japan Tobacco assets. The two leaders reportedly spoke for about 30 minutes and agreed to keep communicating at various levels. The talks followed a Japanese protest over suspected Russian aircraft entering its airspace.

auto-c733c7147c94.headline: UK sanctions eight Israeli firms over West Bank settlements
auto-c733c7147c94.summary:
Britain has imposed sanctions on eight Israeli construction and property firms building settlements in the occupied West Bank, along with the activist group Tzav 9, which the UK says has blocked aid trucks bound for Gaza. The measures freeze assets held in the UK and bar company officials from serving as directors of British firms. The move came just before the deadline for tenders on the contested E1 settlement project in East Jerusalem, which Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said should not go ahead.

Israel's foreign minister Gideon Saar condemned the sanctions as hostile and said Israel would respond with countermeasures, while experts questioned their practical impact given the limited British ties of the targeted firms. Israel's attorney general later postponed the E1 tender until a new government is formed.

Israel faces growing diplomatic isolation from Britain, and Israel's foreign minister has promised countermeasures against London.

auto-f52f55db82ad.headline: Trump reportedly irritated by Vance's Iran war criticism, praises Rubio
auto-f52f55db82ad.summary: According to The New York Times, President Donald Trump has grown frustrated with Vice President JD Vance over his public criticism of the Iran war, reportedly wanting Vance to affirm that launching the conflict was the right decision. Vance has said there is no real rift between him and Trump, and has argued that the war and US ties to Israel contributed to Republican losses in the midterms. Trump has reportedly praised Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has defended the war as necessary for US security. Both men are seen as possible 2028 Republican contenders, though neither has launched a campaign. The White House did not comment on the report.

impact_points: Iran faces an ongoing US war and naval blockade, with the Strait of Hormuz at the centre of the stalemate.
US Republicans face divisions over the war, with the conflict's political costs weighing on their 2028 prospects.

auto-49345eae54cc.headline: Energy watchdog says Hormuz disruption is worst energy security threat on record
auto-49345eae54cc.summary:
The International Energy Agency said on Thursday that the Middle East crisis, which began in February after US and Israeli strikes on Iran, is the gravest threat to energy security it has recorded. Iran has been blockading the Strait of Hormuz and targeting tankers, and Gulf producers have struggled to export oil, despite US efforts to escort vessels through the waterway.

In its annual World Energy Outlook, the agency said consumers are increasingly bearing the costs as other buffers run out, and it warned the crisis will leave lasting effects. Its executive director, Fatih Birol, said the energy world will not return to its previous state, and that China has cut its purchases from international markets.

auto-c68b68ae2c93.summary: European leaders are set to meet in Berlin, hosted by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz with French and British leaders, to agree on funding for Ukraine's defence and to press for a European role in peace talks. auto-86afe6ad483c.headline: Houthi missile debris reportedly damages Riyadh financial district tower
auto-86afe6ad483c.summary:
Saudi Arabia's Houthi conflict widened on Thursday as the Saudi-led coalition said it had dealt with a missile launched by Yemen's Houthi movement towards Riyadh. Debris fell and caused material damage, though the extent was still being assessed. Reports said the Public Investment Fund tower in the capital's King Abdullah Financial District was hit, and casualties were not immediately known.

Earlier, Saudi civil defence authorities lifted threat alerts for the southern cities of Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait, after the Houthis claimed missile and drone attacks on sites there. The attacks follow the group's recent advances on Yemen's Red Sea coast.

auto-6f7cb8436139.headline: China and South Korea nearly finish upgrading their bilateral free trade deal
auto-6f7cb8436139.summary: China's Commerce Ministry said Beijing and Seoul have substantially concluded the second phase of talks to upgrade their free trade agreement. The ministry presented the move as a step against unilateralism and protectionism. Bilateral trade reached $331.24 billion in 2025 and $440.9 billion in the first ten months of 2026, up 63.7 percent year on year.

auto-a1505098a5af.headline: Ukrainian drones hit two Russian refineries in Krasnodar Krai overnight
auto-a1505098a5af.summary: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck two oil refineries in Russia's Krasnodar Krai overnight on November 17 to 18, damaging oil tanks at the Ilsky refinery and a processing plant at the Afip refinery. auto-90888b4540ea.headline: Lee urges peace push with North Korea at APEC summit in China
auto-90888b4540ea.summary:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung used an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, to press for renewed dialogue with North Korea. He called peace on the Korean Peninsula a prerequisite for regional prosperity and said he hoped talks could lead to formally ending the 1950-53 war, which ended only in an armistice. The appeal came as Seoul and Washington try to reopen channels with Pyongyang amid its nuclear advances. Speculation about a possible Trump-Kim meeting at the summit remains unconfirmed, according to a presidential official.

Lee also told Chinese President Xi Jinping that Beijing would play a constructive role, and met Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to discuss energy supply chains. auto-61e10505c4c0.headline: Ukrainian strike hits Crimean Bridge again, halting rail traffic
auto-61e10505c4c0.summary: Ukraine has struck the Crimean Bridge for a third time in a week, according to the Moscow-installed governor of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, who said traffic was temporarily suspended. Russia's transport ministry said a nighttime drone attack halted train services on the rail section, and that no one was hurt. Earlier strikes had reportedly damaged the road span, which appears to have collapsed into the Kerch Strait, though the full extent of damage has not been officially confirmed. Russia has also struck bridges and infrastructure in Kyiv and energy facilities elsewhere in Ukraine.

auto-732b96d0b0aa.headline: Third US carrier joins Middle East deployment as Iran strikes Bahrain base
auto-732b96d0b0aa.summary: The US Central Command said a third American aircraft carrier has reached the Middle East, a visible show of military strength as President Trump weighs next steps in the conflict with Iran. The move came after Tehran said its forces carried out a drone attack on a US radar system at a helicopter base in Bahrain, a Gulf kingdom. auto-745e20ad20aa.headline: BAE Systems to cut about 1,070 UK jobs amid Typhoon order uncertainty
auto-745e20ad20aa.summary: BAE Systems has announced plans to cut roughly 1,070 jobs at its UK head office and air business, about 2% of its 50,000-strong British workforce. A source linked the move to uncertainty over the Eurofighter Typhoon programme rather than cost-cutting. Unions and a Conservative MP have urged the government to place more orders for British-built Typhoons and collaborative combat aircraft, while the Ministry of Defence cited a £8bn Turkey Typhoon contract that it says sustains 6,000 jobs.

auto-91025a0014a0.headline: US sanctions Lebanese charity and money network accused of funding Hezbollah
auto-91025a0014a0.summary:
The US Treasury on Wednesday blacklisted Wa Ta'awanu Association, a Lebanon-based charity that provides emergency aid in southern Lebanon, along with its founder. Officials say the group channels donations to Hezbollah and offers cover for its militant activity in areas meant to be cleared under a June agreement between Lebanon and Israel.

The Treasury also sanctioned brothers Hassan and Ibrahim Khechen and companies in a gold and cash smuggling network based in Lebanon and Turkey, which it says moved Iranian Quds Force money to Hezbollah. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington would keep trying to cut Iran's funding of its regional proxies.

US accuses Iran's Quds Force of funding Hezbollah; new pressure on its proxies
Turkey-based companies in the smuggling network blacklisted

Pursuing its pressure campaign against Iran and its proxies through financial sanctions

impact_points: Lebanon faces pressure as US sanctions target groups seen as obstructing the army's disarmament of Hezbollah.
Hezbollah's financing networks, including Turkey-based companies, face new restrictions, complicating its fundraising and operations.

auto-edb12aa82da9.headline: Ukrainian drone strikes halve Russian refinery output since late October
auto-edb12aa82da9.summary: Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced the volume of crude oil processed by Russian refineries by roughly 45% since late October, according to two industry sources who spoke to Reuters. Daily throughput reportedly fell from above 700,000 metric tons to about 400,000, with 15 of Russia's 35 largest refineries disrupted or halted. Some Russian regions have reinstated limits on gasoline sales as strikes intensify. Separately, Russia launched a combined overnight attack on Ukraine with missiles and drones, and Ukrainian air defences said they downed or jammed many of them.

actors.why: Refinery output nearly halved, forcing fuel rationing in some regions
Long-range drone strikes are degrading Russia's fuel industry and military logistics

impact_points: Russia is losing a large share of its refining capacity, which pressures domestic fuel supply and prices.
Ukraine gains leverage as its long-range strikes disrupt Russia's energy income and fuel availability.

auto-3ff98dfa7e1c.headline: US charges Russian man over surveillance of Silicon Valley defence firm staff
auto-3ff98dfa7e1c.summary:
US prosecutors have charged Igor D'iu, a Russian national, with conspiring to act as an agent of a foreign government, stalking and document fraud. He was allegedly recruited and funded by Russia to watch employees of an unnamed Palo Alto, California, technology and defence company that supplies Ukraine. Officials say he was directed through Telegram, followed staff and photographed laptop screens, and was found with cash and fake identification during an October FBI raid. He is due in federal court on 24 November.

US officials called the alleged operation an intimidation attempt tied to the firm's support for Ukraine. Moscow's role has not been independently confirmed beyond the charges themselves.

actors.why: Prosecutors pursue a foreign spy case, strengthening enforcement against state-backed intelligence threats
Accused of directing a covert surveillance operation against a US firm, drawing international condemnation
The targeted firm supplies Ukraine, so the alleged plot points to pressure linked to Ukrainian support

impact_points: Russia faces US accusations of running a state-directed intelligence operation on American soil.
The targeted Silicon Valley defence firm and its staff face intimidation and security risks tied to their Ukraine support.

auto-3275b21ee5bb.headline: IEA warns Hormuz disruption could permanently reshape global oil and gas demand
auto-3275b21ee5bb.summary:
The International Energy Agency said the Middle East conflict has caused the largest disruption ever to global oil and gas trade, with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz curbed this year. The agency estimates cumulative losses of 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic meters of gas from the Gulf. Its new World Energy Outlook 2026 models a response case in which energy-security concerns accelerate electrification and efficiency, cutting global oil demand in 2035 by about 4.4 million barrels per day compared with current policies.

IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said the energy world will not return to its former state after the Iran war. The agency noted that electrification is becoming cost-competitive, though weak grids and charging networks could slow it. Cooling demand in buildings has now overtaken heating demand for the first time.

actors.why: Conflict and Hormuz disruption are central to the shock, drawing international pressure on Iran
Vessels near Musandam show Oman sits beside the disrupted Hormuz shipping route
Gulf exports curbed by Hormuz disruption, with lasting demand loss ahead
Major importers pursue energy-security measures and electrification to cut fossil fuel dependence
Large oil importers face incentives to electrify transport and reduce reliance on Gulf supplies

impact_points: Gulf oil and gas exporters face lasting loss of demand as importers shift away from fossil fuels.
Importing countries are being pushed toward domestic electrification to reduce dependence on energy shipped through Hormuz.

auto-14dc8ed5726f.headline: Israeli settlers kill Palestinian woman in West Bank village near Jericho
auto-14dc8ed5726f.summary:
A 72-year-old Palestinian woman, Fadha Wadha, was shot dead in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, a village near Jericho in the occupied West Bank, where Israeli settlers had recently moved into several homes. Palestinian residents and the Palestinian health ministry say settlers fired towards houses, and several Palestinians, including her son, were wounded. The Israeli military gave a different account, saying Palestinians rammed an Israeli vehicle and rocks were thrown before troops opened fire. Israeli police said they had opened an investigation, and the competing accounts could not be independently verified.

The incident follows a sharp rise in settler attacks and land seizures in the West Bank, which most UN bodies and countries consider illegal under international law. Israel disputes that status.

actors.why: Palestinian woman killed, several wounded, and farmland access lost in the village
Settler violence and contested killing draw criticism and a police investigation

impact_points: Palestinian residents in al-Duyuk al-Tahta face killings, injuries and loss of farmland access after the settler takeover.
Israel faces mounting international criticism over settler violence and its contested account of the killing, with a police probe under way.

auto-c06e27afc2e7.headline: South Korea's Lee returns home after ASEAN and APEC summit trip
auto-c06e27afc2e7.summary:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung left Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, ending a four-day regional tour that began with the ASEAN summit in the Philippines. He then joined the two-day APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen, where he pressed for regional backing of his initiative to build peace with North Korea. In Shenzhen he held talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and both sides reaffirmed their commitment to easing tensions on the Korean Peninsula.

At APEC, Xi called for stronger cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade, amid trade tensions with the United States and new US chip export restrictions. A meeting between Xi and US President Donald Trump was expected during the summit. Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum also attended, promoting investment at the APEC CEO Summit.

actors.why: Lee secured regional support and reaffirmed peace efforts with North Korea
Hosted APEC and pressed trade cooperation amid US chip restrictions
Putin reaffirmed commitment to easing Korean Peninsula tensions in talks
Faces tougher chip export controls and an expiring trade truce with China
Faces renewed regional diplomacy on peace efforts with South Korea
Sheinbaum pitched Plan México to global investors at the APEC CEO Summit

impact_points: South Korea gains diplomatic backing for its North Korea peace initiative from China and Russia.
China and the United States face trade strain, with a tenuous truce set to expire in January.

auto-aab9c0a57a8d.headline: Ukrainian drone strike on Kursk wounds 11, damaging homes and public buildings
auto-aab9c0a57a8d.summary:
Ukrainian drones struck the Russian city of Kursk on the morning of November 19, injuring 11 people, according to regional governor Alexander Khinshtein. A 12-year-old was pulled from rubble in the northwest of the city, and two visitors to a private clinic were hurt by shrapnel. Blast effects from falling debris damaged residential buildings, a court building, a central library and a medical college in the city centre. Khinshtein said all victims had minor injuries and denied that any military facilities were near the sites. Ukraine has not been cited as commenting on the strike.

The attack came as Kyiv was reported to have stepped up strikes on Russian energy and transport infrastructure, with Russia's Defence Ministry saying it intercepted 53 drones overnight. A separate drone attack on an oil facility in Tatarstan was also reported the same day.

actors.why: Civilians injured and public buildings damaged in Kursk; authorities say resolve is strengthening
Accused of attacking civilian areas, though strikes on Russian energy infrastructure continue

impact_points: Russia faces civilian injuries and damage to public buildings in Kursk, which borders Ukraine and is frequently attacked.
Ukraine is accused by Moscow of intimidating civilians, while Russia's energy and transport networks face mounting pressure from drone strikes.

auto-782622293004.headline: US and Iran edge toward renewed war as stalemate persists
auto-782622293004.summary:
Tensions between the United States and Iran are rising as both sides hold back from full-scale fighting while still exchanging limited strikes. Iranian military leaders say their forces are preparing for a possible new US attack and warn that any response would be harsher. Reports say Israel's Mossad has urged Washington to carry out joint strikes, though the US has signalled mixed intentions.

Washington continues a naval blockade of Iranian ports and economic pressure, while Iran insists it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz or resume talks until those measures end. Mediators from Oman and Qatar are involved, and officials say the situation could slide back into fighting.

Blockade and sanctions pressure Iran, yet midterm losses and fuel prices strain Washington

impact_points: Iran faces a possible renewed US and Israeli strike campaign, with its leaders warning of a harsher response.

auto-b97a8ead3fc8.headline: Trump claims major Philippines trade deal, but Manila confirms no agreement
auto-b97a8ead3fc8.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday in Manila that Washington had just concluded a very large trade deal with the Philippines, calling it fair to both sides, though he gave no details. The Philippine presidential office later said only that both sides had reached an understanding on economic cooperation, and its ambassador in Washington said nothing had been signed. Trump also pledged expanded defense cooperation with Manila, while the Philippines seeks firmer assurances over the South China Sea. The claims could not be verified.

auto-f4ff419461bd.headline: Putin claims economic strength and offers tech sharing at APEC in Shenzhen
auto-f4ff419461bd.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin, speaking at the APEC business summit in Shenzhen, China, said Western sanctions had pushed Russia to modernize its industry and that its economy had grown more than 10% over three years. Putin also offered to share Russian digital and technology expertise with friendly countries. Official Russian forecasts, however, put growth at just 0.4% this year, and Russia's share of global invention patents fell to 0.8% in 2025.

In Shenzhen, Putin also pointed to expanding Russia-China education links, saying more than 100,000 Russians are learning Chinese. Meanwhile, the APEC meetings drew attention to a planned three-way meeting involving US President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Putin, while Trump said North Korean leader Kim Jong-un 'would like to' attend.

Trump's possible meetings with Xi and Putin hold uncertain outcomes for Washington
Kim's possible attendance at APEC is raised by Trump but remains unconfirmed

impact_points: Russia faces a weak growth outlook despite official claims, with forecasts of only 0.4% this year.
China gains closer ties with Moscow as Russia turns east after strained relations with European countries.

auto-803c5d6abee4.headline: Denmark's parliament ratifies Arctic security pact with US and Greenland
auto-803c5d6abee4.summary: Denmark's parliament has unanimously approved a new Arctic security agreement between Greenland, Denmark and the United States. The vote was 109 to none, with no debate. The pact, signed in September by President Trump and the leaders of Greenland and Denmark, updates a 1951 defence deal. It gives the US underwater access and permission to build a missile defence system, and recognises Greenland as an equal partner. Greenland's own parliament approved it earlier in November. Danish foreign minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said it removes uncertainty over the territory, but acknowledged that trust in Washington must be rebuilt. He also said the US had not yet informed Denmark of plans for new bases.

The agreement aims to keep China and Russia from expanding influence in Greenland, including through investment.

auto-3c7e10daaaeb.headline: US defence official criticises Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russia; allies push back
auto-3c7e10daaaeb.summary:
At a Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting in Brussels, senior US Pentagon official Elbridge Colby said Ukraine's long-range strikes deep inside Russia have not been effective in ending the war or slowing Russian advances, and may have hardened Russian public and Kremlin resolve. Germany's defence minister Boris Pistorius and Britain's defence secretary Wes Streeting rejected the criticism, arguing the strikes degrade Russia's war machine. Colby also urged continued funding for the NATO-backed PURL weapons scheme, which allies supported with new pledges.

Zelenskyy, speaking by video, asked allies, especially the United States, to speed up delivery of Patriot and IRIS-T interceptors and said Ukraine needs 40 more F-16 jets. The comments came ahead of expected fresh US-led peace talks.

impact_points: Ukraine faces a rebuke from its US backer over strikes it says pressure Russia and strengthen its negotiating position.

auto-42971c03493b.headline: EU and UK set to advance post-Brexit deals at Brussels summit
auto-42971c03493b.summary:
The UK and European Union are holding a summit in Brussels to set the long-term shape of their relationship after Brexit. Prime Minister Andy Burnham, European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen and European Council president António Costa are attending; the meeting was delayed from July after Keir Starmer resigned. Three agreements are expected: easing trade in meat, cheese, wine and flowers, linking emissions trading systems, and a youth mobility scheme for 18- to 30-year-olds. Tuition fees and visa numbers remain unresolved, and the EU is tying all three deals together.

The UK has not been included in the EU's Made in Europe industrial plan, as that law is not expected to be finalised until spring 2027, with France and the European Parliament taking a stricter line.

Secures alignment and leverage, with tuition and visa terms still disputed

impact_points: The UK would align with EU food standards, affecting trade in animal and plant products from 2028.

auto-6fc37e5ea4a3.headline: Third strike in four days halts rail traffic on Kerch Bridge
auto-6fc37e5ea4a3.summary: A third Ukrainian strike in four days has disrupted rail traffic on the Kerch Bridge, the link between Russia and occupied Crimea. Separately, Russian strikes hit two bridges in Kyiv, with the city's mayor reporting damage to critical infrastructure and disruption to heating and water supplies overnight. Ukraine's president said the Crimean Bridge strike was an operation weeks in the making. Meanwhile, US, Russian and Ukrainian officials are preparing further peace talks, with European leaders meeting in Berlin to discuss funding and security guarantees for Kyiv.

auto-a332d5b1a8a4.headline: Ukrainian drones reportedly hit Russian oil pumping station in Tatarstan
auto-a332d5b1a8a4.summary: Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the Kaleykino oil pumping station in Russia's Tatarstan Republic overnight on November 19, 2026, setting the site ablaze, according to Ukrainian monitoring channels. The facility sits near Almetyevsk, roughly 380 kilometers from the Russian-Kazakh border. Ukraine says it is targeting Russian fuel production and military supply chains, pointing to recent strikes on refineries in Krasnodar Krai and the Crimean Bridge. Reuters, citing industry sources, reported that Ukrainian attacks have disrupted or halted operations at 15 of Russia's 35 major refineries over 20 days.

auto-df0dce8fa620.headline: Ukrainian strikes bring down part of Crimea's Kerch Bridge to Russia
auto-df0dce8fa620.summary: Ukraine carried out a series of drone and cruise missile strikes on the Kerch Strait Bridge, which links Russia to the annexed Crimean Peninsula, damaging and collapsing a section of the road span. Reporting says one arch fell into the strait, the rail line has been limited to a single track, and the attacks came after weeks of strikes on Russian air defences and radars. Zelenskyy said the operation was planned in stages and framed it as a response to Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would be rebuilt. The strikes came as Putin was due to attend an Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen.
