auto-35ac2a8fbbab.headline: Trump alleges Iranian chemical and biological weapons work without public evidence
auto-35ac2a8fbbab.summary:
US President Donald Trump has accused Iran of exploring chemical and biological weapons, citing no evidence, as concern grows over a reported Iranian plot against US officials in Washington. A CNN report citing US intelligence said Tehran may be planning a dirty bomb or chemical attack on senior administration figures. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Homeland Security officials said there was no imminent threat, while Trump said the US was looking into the matter and would retaliate if an attack occurred. Iran's foreign ministry called the allegations baseless.

Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera say Iran has the industrial capacity for such weapons but that its intentions remain unclear, and that US administrations have previously made unfounded weapons claims about Middle Eastern countries.

auto-3d99f39f1abe.headline: Iraq sets up joint command in Jurf al-Sakhar amid standoff with Kataib Hezbollah
auto-3d99f39f1abe.summary: Iraq's government announced a joint military headquarters in Jurf al-Sakhar, Babil province, to take over security in an area Kataib Hezbollah has controlled since 2014. Units from the army, Federal Police, Popular Mobilization Forces and an energy police regiment will fall under the command, due to start operating on Friday. It is unclear whether the Iran-aligned faction will hand over its positions. Reports say Iran's Quds Force commander, Esmail Qaani, has arrived in Iraq to broker a settlement, while officials have reportedly considered a security cordon if talks fail. The dispute follows an investigation into alleged oil smuggling in the town.

auto-942a4b86b9e7.headline: Berlin meeting of Ukraine's backers discusses security guarantees and possible troop deployment
auto-942a4b86b9e7.summary:
Leaders from more than 30 countries in the Coalition of the Willing are meeting in Berlin to discuss post-war security guarantees for Ukraine. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul called it the largest such gathering so far and said it signalled to Moscow that talks must be taken seriously. Planned elements include supporting Ukraine's armed forces, deploying a multinational force, and firm legal and political guarantees. Exercises in Poland involving about 2,800 personnel are meant to show how quickly such a force could deploy.

Wadephul also welcomed renewed US-led peace efforts, though Germany is preparing for talks to fail and for winter support to Ukraine. Putin has invited Europeans to Moscow to discuss how future talks could be structured.

auto-ae89bf494808.headline: UK and EU still divided on food rules and student fees before summit
auto-ae89bf494808.summary: Britain and the European Union remain at odds days before a planned summit in Brussels, where Prime Minister Andy Burnham is due on Friday. An EU diplomat said the talks would be decided at the last minute, and that Britain needed to move if it wanted a deal. The main disputes concern how much say the UK would have over future EU food and farming standards, and whether EU students would pay domestic or international tuition fees in Britain. Officials said EU ambassadors would keep negotiating late into the night, and a deal, if reached, would be followed by UK legislation in Parliament next week.

auto-ba9f642f45e5.headline: Russian military aircraft detected near Taiwan and Japan; Siberian crash kills 19
auto-ba9f642f45e5.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense said two Russian Tu-95 long-range bombers entered its air defense identification zone from the south, flew east of the island and exited northeast of Keelung, and released a surveillance image. Japan separately protested to Moscow after two aircraft believed to be Russian entered its airspace off Fukuoka Prefecture. auto-00e2836fedb6.headline: Russian bombers deployed across East Asia ahead of regional summits
auto-00e2836fedb6.summary:
Russia has deployed two Tu-95 strategic bombers and two refuelling tankers to Da Nang in Vietnam, the largest Russian air deployment in the region in possibly over a decade. The flights came after Russian aircraft alarmed the air forces of Taiwan and Japan on Tuesday as they moved south from Russia's Far East.

The timing coincided with Vladimir Putin's trip to Shenzhen for APEC and a gathering of leaders, including Donald Trump, in Manila. Analysts said the move aims to show Moscow can still project power in Southeast Asia despite its war in Ukraine, and possibly to signal strong ties with China. auto-9e0789b6a6e6.headline: Somalia expels UAE envoy and recalls its own ambassador from Abu Dhabi
auto-9e0789b6a6e6.summary: Somalia has ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador to leave the country within 72 hours and withdrawn its own envoy from Abu Dhabi. Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud announced the move on state media on Thursday, November 19, accusing the Emirates of unspecified violations of Somali sovereignty amounting to an open invasion. He did not say what actions the UAE had taken, and warned that anyone cooperating with the Emirates would face measures. There was no immediate response from the UAE foreign ministry. auto-48acad7680a0.headline: Vessels hit in Strait of Hormuz, leaving crew wounded and missing
auto-48acad7680a0.summary: Two commercial vessels were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz in the days before the reports. India's foreign ministry separately condemned the strike on the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT Tara Gas on 16 November. auto-81eb143e9fcb.headline: IEA says Hormuz disruption is worst energy security threat on record
auto-81eb143e9fcb.summary:
The International Energy Agency has warned that the crisis in the Middle East, which began in February after US and Israeli strikes on Iran, is the greatest threat to energy security in history. In its annual World Energy Outlook, the agency said consumers are increasingly bearing the cost as buffers run out. Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on tankers have severely disrupted oil exports from Gulf producers, despite US efforts to escort vessels through the channel.

IEA chief Fatih Birol said governments have tried to shield households, but face higher prices and some supply shortfalls. The agency warned the damage will be lasting and that a return to pre-crisis conditions is unlikely while the conflict continues.

auto-689cb644618e.headline: US Army to detonate degraded lead azide, prompting lead dust warnings in Iowa
auto-689cb644618e.summary:
The US Army plans to detonate about five tons of unusable bomb-making chemicals at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, scheduled for Friday. Officials say the blast could release a plume carrying lead-containing particles, and they advise some Middletown residents to leave their homes that morning or stay indoors with windows and doors shut.

The degraded material is lead azide, which had dried out in storage and become more sensitive to shock and friction. The EPA approved an emergency permit for the detonation, and schools in the path of the plume, including Danville, have closed. Residents and local officials say they lack clear information about the risks.

auto-0984d257abec.headline: US Centcom chief meets Saudi leaders amid renewed Houthi conflict
auto-0984d257abec.summary:
US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman in Riyadh, Saudi state media reported. The talks covered military affairs, defence cooperation and regional security. It was Cooper's third publicly reported visit to the kingdom since fighting with the Iran-aligned Houthis resumed in July. Separately, Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan met the Mecca Defence Alliance secretary-general to discuss joint defence coordination.

Reuters reported that Riyadh has sought US help against the Houthis, who have increased attacks on Saudi cities and energy sites and advanced toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Washington reportedly declined to join strikes but agreed to provide intelligence and targeting support.

auto-3fee4502e66c.headline: Arab and Muslim states back UK and Australian sanctions on West Bank settlements
auto-3fee4502e66c.summary:
Foreign ministers from 15 or 16 Arab and Muslim countries, including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Egypt, have welcomed sanctions imposed by the UK and Australia over Israeli settlement activity in the occupied West Bank. The UK sanctioned eight Israeli construction firms, property developers and a far-right group, while Australia broadened its own measures against settlement activity.

The ministers condemned Israel's settlement policies, especially the E1 plan east of East Jerusalem, and urged full implementation of the Gaza peace plan and a two-state solution. Some analysts told The New Arab the UK measures are mainly symbolic and unlikely to curb settlement growth.

auto-68e6998d3616.headline: US Senate rejects bid to force Trump to halt Iran war
auto-68e6998d3616.summary: The US Senate voted 51 to 48, largely along party lines, to defeat a war powers resolution that would have required President Trump to end the conflict with Iran or secure congressional approval to continue it. The measure had already passed the House. Only Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul joined Democrats in support, while Democrat John Fetterman opposed it. Democratic Senator Tim Kaine said the war's unpopularity was clear from the November 3 midterm results, which saw Democratic gains tied partly to rising prices. Separately, Representative Yassamin Ansari urged Congress to block funding for offensive operations against Iran ahead of a December 11 deadline.

US voters and Congress face ongoing debate over war funding, oversight and higher prices linked to the conflict.

auto-8b375adf89fd.headline: UK sanctions on settlement firms show early effects as Israel delays E1 tenders
auto-8b375adf89fd.summary:
Britain has imposed its first set of sanctions on eight Israeli construction, property and architectural businesses linked to West Bank settlements, with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband saying the measures aim to protect the two-state solution. Early signs of impact are emerging: one targeted firm, Har Hevron Development Company, reportedly had foreign trade accounts frozen by two banks, and Israel's largest bank chief said settlement builders are struggling to get foreign financing.

Israel postponed issuing tenders for the E1 settlement plan, which would sit between Jerusalem and Maale Adumim and could split the West Bank. Israel's attorney general said the decision belongs to the next government, and Israeli diplomats denied a link to the British measures, while UK sources said the sanctions played a role. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions hostile and promised countermeasures.

European states including France and Canada imposed similar settlement sanctions, reinforcing a shared stance.

impact_points: Israel faces financing pressure and a delayed E1 plan, though it denies the British measures caused the delay.
Palestinians in the West Bank may benefit if E1 is stalled, since the plan threatens a viable Palestinian state.

auto-069c8dab8042.headline: Mogadishu orders UAE envoy out within 72 hours amid escalating dispute
auto-069c8dab8042.summary:
Somalia has ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador to leave within 72 hours and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi. Officials, after a cabinet meeting, accused the UAE of interfering in Somali affairs and of an "open invasion" of its sovereignty, though they gave few specifics on what prompted the move.

The UAE foreign ministry condemned the decision as harmful to bilateral ties. The step follows earlier friction, including Somalia's January cancellation of all agreements with the Emirates over its support for Israel's recognition of Somaliland. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has also accused Abu Dhabi of backing regional administrations against the federal government.

auto-d06413cf7e70.headline: Xi opens APEC summit in Shenzhen, urging AI cooperation and free trade
auto-d06413cf7e70.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping formally opened the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, calling for deeper international cooperation on artificial intelligence, digital economy ties and free trade. He pledged to lower tariffs and widen market access for foreign firms. Xi is expected to meet US President Donald Trump on Thursday, with trade tensions and new American restrictions on advanced chip exports to China likely to dominate. A trade truce agreed last year is set to expire in January, and Washington says its tighter rules target smuggling and grey-market computing access.

Japan's prime minister reportedly faces a cool reception and sidelined support at the summit

impact_points: China faces pressure over trade barriers while promoting itself as a champion of open markets and AI cooperation.

auto-5a137e6b3ecc.headline: Bahrain jails dozens of Shiite clerics amid renewed Iranian strikes
auto-5a137e6b3ecc.summary:
Bahraini criminal court sentenced 64 defendants to life imprisonment and five others to 15 years over alleged collaboration with Iran, a trial rights groups say involved torture claims and forced confessions. The verdicts came as Iran resumed attacks on Gulf states hosting US forces. Kuwait and Bahrain said they intercepted Iranian drones and missiles, after US jets struck a missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran's army said it targeted Ali Al Salem Airbase in Kuwait, which hosts US forces, and Gulf and Arab leaders condemned the strikes. Qatar, which has mediated stalled US-Iran talks, warned the escalation could derail diplomacy. A tanker owned by the UAE's ADNOC was also hit in the strait, with one sailor missing.

Launched strikes on Gulf states after US retaliation; faces US strikes
Drone attack on airbase condemned as sovereignty violation

impact_points: Bahrain faces both domestic prosecutions of Shiite clerics and renewed Iranian strikes on its territory.

auto-2e4c3a24500a.headline: IEA says Iran war will permanently reshape global energy markets
auto-2e4c3a24500a.summary:
The International Energy Agency says the US-Israeli war on Iran will leave lasting marks on the global energy sector. Its executive director, Fatih Birol, warned that the longer the crisis continues, the deeper the effects will be, and said he sees no credible path back to how energy markets operated before.

Separately, the US Central Command chief, Admiral Brad Cooper, met Israeli military and intelligence leaders in Tel Aviv, including Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and Mossad director Roman Gofman, to assess regional threats centred on Iran. The Israeli military described the trip as part of routine visits. Bahrain and Kuwait reported repelling Iranian aerial attacks after US strikes on an Iranian island.

auto-8235712b0c52.headline: Pakistan says 22 militants killed in northwest raids it links to India
auto-8235712b0c52.summary:
Pakistani security forces, acting on intelligence, raided militant hideouts near the Afghan border in the northwest, sparking gunbattles that the military said killed 22 militants. The raids took place over 48 hours in South Waziristan, Bannu and Tank districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The military described the fighters as backed by neighboring India, a claim New Delhi had not publicly answered at the time of reporting.

The operation follows an earlier announcement that 74 militants were killed in raids across the northwest and southwestern Balochistan province. Troops are still searching the areas, and President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the forces and pledged to keep fighting militancy.

auto-a0d4288bb098.headline: IEA says Hormuz shipping trust is shattered and Gulf energy routes need rethinking
auto-a0d4288bb098.summary:
The International Energy Agency says confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a dependable route for energy exports has been badly damaged after the Iran war blocked shipping through it. IEA head Fatih Birol said there is no credible path back to the situation before February 2026, though the world could conceivably manage without the strait, albeit with difficulty.

In its World Energy Outlook, the agency estimated that new bypass pipelines would cost about $40bn and add roughly $2 per barrel to Middle Eastern oil. Gulf states such as Saudi Arabia and the UAE are expanding routes around the chokepoint, while Iraq has resumed exports through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey. The agency warned those bypass routes remain vulnerable to attack.

auto-e6e917b74142.headline: Macron urges allies to speed air defence to Ukraine and revisit its NATO bid
auto-e6e917b74142.summary:
At a Berlin summit of Ukraine's supporters, French President Emmanuel Macron called on allies to speed up delivery of air defence systems, especially anti-missile systems and interceptors, to Kyiv. He also said Ukraine's NATO membership should be reconsidered given Russia's maximalist position. The meeting, co-hosted with Germany and the UK, came hours after a Trump, Putin and Xi summit in China. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said new peace talks should take place soon, with Europe seeking a seat at the table.

US envoy Jared Kushner said Trump supported European involvement and was open to a NATO-style security guarantee for Ukraine. Ukrainian President Zelensky said real guarantees would mean US or European forces and bases on Ukrainian soil.

auto-518942cd6e6a.headline: Iran says drones hit US-linked targets at Kuwait air base
auto-518942cd6e6a.summary: Iran's army said its combat drones struck US Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms at the Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait. Iranian state media carried the statement, which described the base as a key logistics and transit hub for US forces in the region. Kuwait's military said its air defences were countering hostile drone attacks. Separately, the IRGC spokesman said the broadcaster Iran International was among Iran's military targets, renewing an earlier threat against the outlet and its journalists. auto-34e700538d34.headline: Trump's cyber director Sean Cairncross removed after a run of US tech outages
auto-34e700538d34.summary:
Sean Cairncross, who led cybersecurity policy for the federal government as White House national cyber director, has been removed from the post, a source close to the White House said. Kirsten Davies, the Defense Department's chief information officer, will temporarily take over the role. Axios reported that chief of staff Stephen Miller pushed for the change, saying Cairncross lacked strong cyber credentials; this could not be independently confirmed.

The move follows a week of technology failures affecting US air travel, banking, email services and a brief disruption to an National Security Agency network. Intelligence officials said the outages were maintenance-related rather than a coordinated or state-sponsored attack. The successor will need Senate confirmation, and the Senate becomes Democrat-controlled in January.

impact_points: The United States faces a leadership change in federal cyber policy just as critical systems were disrupted.

auto-850cfdab1562.headline: Putin says Russia invited Europeans to Moscow to define their Ukraine talks stance
auto-850cfdab1562.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow has invited European representatives to Moscow through diplomatic channels to clarify what Europe would contribute to talks on ending the war in Ukraine. He spoke after trilateral talks with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, where he said the Americans had pressed for Europe's involvement. In Berlin, European leaders said they were ready for negotiations with Russia, but only after a peace agreement with Ukraine, while Ukraine's Zelensky said Putin had rejected every proposal so far.

Separately, Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita reported that Russian intelligence planned a mass-casualty sabotage attack on Polish territory near Kaliningrad to blame on Ukraine, which Warsaw says it foiled. Polish officials did not confirm the plot's details, and the claims could not be independently verified.

auto-8683f754eff1.summary:

Xi called the talks groundbreaking, and the leaders pledged to pursue United Nations reform, limit the International Criminal Court's role, avoid nuclear war and boost refined petroleum supplies. The joint statement did not mention Russia's war in Ukraine or the US-led war in Iran, and nuclear arms talks were limited to 'dialogue' with no firm commitments to cut stockpiles.

auto-84a33478ed4c.headline: European allies gather in Berlin to back Ukraine and press for a seat in talks

The meeting followed a three-way summit in Shenzhen, China, between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, which German Chancellor Friedrich Merz dismissed as a photo op. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff also joined the Berlin talks, and Kushner said Russia had grown comfortable with Article 5-style security guarantees for Ukraine, though Moscow has not commented.

auto-212539edf147.headline: Trump nominee declines to call Jan. 6 an attack at Senate hearing
auto-212539edf147.summary: Michael LoSapio, nominated by President Trump to head the US agency responsible for election security, faced questioning at his Senate confirmation hearing. auto-69ca4248344d.headline: UK and Australian sanctions on West Bank settlement firms and figures draw Israeli response
auto-69ca4248344d.summary: The United Kingdom has sanctioned eight Israeli construction and property firms tied to West Bank settlements, and an Israeli regional council head says two banks have already frozen one firm's foreign trade accounts. auto-692b03676373.headline: EU states clear signing of Indonesia trade and investment pacts
auto-692b03676373.summary: EU member governments have authorised the signing of a trade agreement and an investment protection pact with Indonesia, both concluded in September 2025. The Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement aims to remove import duties on more than 90 percent of goods, with the EU expecting about 600 million euros in annual customs savings. Indonesia's 50 percent duty on EU cars is to be phased out over five years. The deals were also presented as a hedge against new U.S. tariffs, and both sides want them applied quickly, since Indonesia leaves the EU's preference scheme on January 1, 2027. auto-e8b4833cbe6a.summary: Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv killed three people and wounded about 15, city officials said on Friday. auto-4ca814dcd226.headline: Pentagon puts US cost of Iran conflict at $48.3 billion
auto-4ca814dcd226.summary: A Pentagon official told lawmakers that the American military campaign against Iran has cost an estimated $48.3 billion. auto-269c52dddb19.headline: US reinforces Gulf naval presence as Iran standoff drags on

A third US aircraft carrier group, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, has arrived in the Middle East, adding to Washington's forces around Iran. The US says it prefers economic pressure, including a naval blockade of Iranian ports and a land blockade called Task Force Iron Gate, over renewed large-scale strikes. auto-de5b2af44edf.headline: Iraq deploys forces to militia town of Jurf al-Sakhar under negotiated arrangement
auto-de5b2af44edf.summary:
Iraqi security forces moved into Jurf al-Sakhar, a town south of Baghdad long controlled by the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah militia, on Friday, state media said. Under the arrangement, Kataib fighters were expected to relocate to other areas, and nine officials have been dismissed in the probe. Kataib has denied the smuggling accusations.

auto-7243b505fc00.headline: Burnham and EU leaders meet in Brussels to advance post-Brexit reset
auto-7243b505fc00.summary:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is in Brussels for a summit with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa, seeking to repair economic damage from Brexit. Agreements under discussion include easing food and agricultural border checks, linking carbon emissions trading systems, and a youth mobility scheme for up to 100,000 young people from each side. Talks reportedly went down to the wire over university fees and regulatory input, with a compromise on fees still to be settled.

auto-82f7eb45457a.headline: US weighs reported Iranian dirty-bomb plot in Washington; Tehran rejects claims
auto-82f7eb45457a.summary:

President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Washington was taking the possibility seriously and investigating the information. Iran's Foreign Ministry called the allegations baseless and denied them.

Experts interviewed by Iran International judged an attack unlikely, citing operational hurdles and the risk of US retaliation. The White House said there were no credible threats to the homeland at the time, and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin called the planning aspirational.

actors.why: Accused of plotting attack; denies claims, faces possible US retaliation
Officials investigating reported threat to senior officials in Washington

impact_points: Iran faces heightened US scrutiny and possible retaliation if the reported plot is substantiated.
The United States, including its senior officials in Washington, is treating the reported threat as a security concern under investigation.

auto-aa342eae5673.headline: Pakistani minister in New Delhi for SCO forum, first such visit since 2025 clashes
auto-aa342eae5673.summary: Pakistan's climate change minister, Musadik Malik, arrived in New Delhi to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum, the first visit to India by a Pakistani federal minister since the four-day conflict of May 2025. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was due to open the forum, and Malik is expected to speak there. No bilateral meeting has been announced, and both governments describe the trip as routine SCO business. India's position is that its Pakistan policy, shaped after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack, has not changed.

actors.why: Minister attends SCO forum, keeping influence and channels open before hosting the summit
Hosts forum and keeps its Pakistan policy, with no bilateral talks planned
SCO partner whose regional forum continues with both India and Pakistan participating

impact_points: Pakistan gains a chance to keep its SCO role ahead of hosting the 2027 summit in Islamabad.
India and Pakistan keep limited contact through a multilateral forum, with no sign yet of bilateral progress.

auto-f2ea5eec2dc7.headline: El Salvador's roughly 2,500 troops in Haiti: origins, mandate and early results
auto-f2ea5eec2dc7.summary:
El Salvador has deployed about 2,500 soldiers to Haiti since October, starting with a mission to rescue four missing Salvadoran aviation technicians who vanished after an attack near Port-au-Prince. The operation has since widened into a broader offensive against gangs that reportedly control most of the capital region, alongside Haitian forces, the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force and private contractors.

President Nayib Bukele said on Wednesday his forces destroyed the mansion of gang leader Jeff Larose, posting video of helicopter strikes. It was unclear whether Larose was killed or present. Thousands of Haitians have rallied in support, though critics note the troops largely operate outside UN monitoring and raise human rights concerns.

actors.why: Gangs control most of the capital; foreign troops now striking their leaders, though civilian risks grow
Bukele gains public visibility and regional influence, but faces criticism over the deployment
Relevant as a bystander to regional security efforts, with limited direct impact in these reports

impact_points: Haiti gains a foreign military push against gangs, but faces questions over civilian risk and control of retaken areas.
El Salvador's president extends his regional security profile, while Bukele's rule draws criticism over human rights abuses.

auto-b1d006924fc1.headline: Ukrainian strikes damage Crimean Bridge, straining Russia's supply route to Crimea
auto-b1d006924fc1.summary:
Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea three times in a week, the latest overnight on Wednesday into Thursday, hitting the rail section. On Tuesday, a missile and drone attack destroyed a roughly 200-metre stretch of the road deck and collapsed an arch into the Kerch Strait, halting car traffic for the foreseeable future. Russian officials said rail services resumed later on Thursday and that nobody was hurt, while Kyiv says the strikes cut the flow of supplies to Russian forces.

Moscow's Kremlin spokesman said the bridge would be rebuilt, and President Putin vowed a response he said would be far more painful. The attacks came as Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump held talks in Shenzhen, China.

actors.why: Road bridge unusable, rail disrupted, supply lines strained, and Putin has vowed retaliation
Strikes cut Russian supply routes to occupied south, which Kyiv says saves lives
Hosted the Shenzhen summit where the attacks were timed to coincide with talks
Trump attended the Shenzhen summit overshadowed by the attacks on Russia's bridge

impact_points: Russia faces logistical strain as the bridge's road section is unusable and rail traffic is limited.
Russian farmers and shippers may struggle to move grain through the Kerch Strait, possibly raising global grain prices.

auto-fd884ea9af95.headline: Russian strike hits Ukrainian rail network as Kyiv commuter service resumes
auto-fd884ea9af95.summary:
Ukrainian state railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia says Kyiv's circular commuter service is resuming despite a large-scale Russian missile and drone attack that damaged rail infrastructure and delayed several trains. Repair crews are working on damaged sections, and staff are evacuating passengers whenever a threat arises. Commuter trains in Kyiv and the surrounding oblast continue to run under safety measures, and delay information is posted on the operator's website.

Separately, Reuters sources say Ukrainian drone strikes have cut Russian refinery crude processing by about 45% since late October, with 15 of 35 major plants disrupted. Russia's energy ministry did not comment. In Kursk, a Ukrainian drone attack reportedly injured 11 people on November 19.

actors.why: Rail infrastructure damaged by Russian strike; service continues under safety measures
Refinery output cut nearly in half by drone strikes, causing domestic fuel shortages

impact_points: Ukraine faces disrupted rail service and repair costs after the Russian strike damaged tracks and delayed trains.
Russia's fuel supply is strained, with domestic shortages in some regions and a possible knock-on effect on global fuel markets.

auto-a42ced7c98ee.headline: Ukrainian strike halts rail services on Crimean Bridge for third time in a week
auto-a42ced7c98ee.summary:
Rail traffic on the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea was suspended after an overnight strike on its railway section, the third attack on the crossing in recent days. Russia's transport ministry said train services were halted temporarily, and Crimea's Moscow-appointed head Sergei Aksyonov said repairs were underway. Ukraine's Defence Ministry said Neptune missiles hit near an arch and on the tracks, while Ukraine's General Staff only hinted at the strike. Earlier in the week a road section had been destroyed, leaving road traffic impossible.

The bridge is a key supply route for Russian forces in southern Ukraine and a symbol of Russia's annexation of Crimea. Local residents reported that the second arch appeared undamaged, and the extent of the damage was still being assessed.

actors.why: Key supply route for forces in the south is damaged and rail traffic halted
Strike on a symbolic target disrupts Russian logistics for its war effort
Bloc watches the escalating strikes on a Russian supply route and the wider war

impact_points: Russia faces disrupted fuel and ammunition supplies to its forces in southern Ukraine via the bridge.
Crimea is cut off from its main land link, with both road and rail traffic currently halted.

auto-2dde3a55a17f.headline: EU proposes €45 billion loan for Ukraine in 2027
auto-2dde3a55a17f.summary:
The European Commission has proposed a €45 billion loan for Ukraine in 2027, aimed at covering about two-thirds of a projected €70 billion funding gap. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Ukraine would only repay once Russia compensates it for war damage. The loan would be split between roughly €25 billion for military needs and €20 billion for civilian budget support, and still requires approval from all EU member states.

Several EU members, including Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria, have said they will not take part, and Germany has warned it could block the EU budget unless all countries join. Meanwhile, European leaders are preparing to meet in Berlin, as US envoys seek a European role in peace talks with Russia.

actors.why: Gains a large funding lifeline to fill its 2027 financing gap and defend itself.
Faces a loan designed to be repaid from its reparations, adding pressure on Moscow.
Must agree the loan among 27 states, with some members resisting and funding gaps remaining.
Is the largest EU payer and presses for unanimity, pressing other members to join.
Has ruled itself out of the loan, standing apart from the EU consensus.
Backs European participation in talks, but European funding shifts burden toward Europe.

impact_points: Ukraine faces a potential cash crisis and must rely on EU and allied funding to sustain its defence and services.
Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria are opting out, while Germany threatens to block the EU's seven-year budget over the dispute.

auto-9e041dd7b060.headline: Iran prepares tanker convoy from Kharg Island as US blockade tightens
auto-9e041dd7b060.summary: Iran has gathered more than 14 oil tankers at Kharg Island, its main crude export terminal, and plans to send them in convoy toward the Sea of Oman in the coming days, satellite and ship-tracking data indicate. Ship-to-ship transfers near the island have reportedly been carried out with tracking systems switched off. The US military has warned that vessels receiving cargo at sea from Iranian-loaded ships may be stopped, boarded or seized, and President Trump has said he will not decide on renewed strikes on Iran until next year. Iranian figures have threatened strikes on Gulf oil facilities if tankers are attacked; these threats are unverified.

actors.why: Crude exports stalled under blockade, financial strain, but attempting to restore flows
Blockade enforcement continues while strike decisions are deferred to next year
Oil facilities threatened by Iranian warnings amid escalation risk
Oil facilities named in Iranian threats of retaliation if tankers are attacked
Iranian tankers reportedly heading toward China, sustaining Asian crude supply

impact_points: Iran faces mounting financial pressure as crude loadings at Kharg Island have stalled under the US blockade.
Gulf states including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain could face risk to their oil facilities if the standoff escalates.

auto-7fa4cd559c11.headline: Italian workers and students march nationwide over pay and living costs
auto-7fa4cd559c11.summary:
Workers and students across Italy joined a nationwide strike on Friday, marching in dozens of cities to press for higher wages, cheaper living costs and stronger social protections. Organisers said demonstrations were planned in more than 45 Italian cities. The walkout was expected to disrupt schools, hospitals and local transport.

The action was timed to coincide with an International Day of Student Mobilisation, linking the labour protest with student demonstrations. The reporting is based on a video from Rome and the planned scope of the marches, and does not give final participation figures.

actors.why: Nationwide strike disrupts services and pressures government over wages and costs

impact_points: Italy faces disruption to schools, hospitals and local transport while the government confronts pressure over wages and living costs.
Italian workers and students are pressing for higher pay and stronger social protections, a demand that the government must answer.

auto-ca88e6c74ab4.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold Shenzhen summit with symbolic declaration but no arms deal
auto-ca88e6c74ab4.summary:
Leaders of China, Russia and the United States met for about 90 minutes in Shenzhen, China, at an unprecedented trilateral summit held alongside an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gathering. The three signed a symbolic joint declaration stating that nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and pledged to discuss reducing nuclear risks, but set no timeline and announced no arms control talks, which Washington had sought.

Reports describe Russian President Vladimir Putin receiving a cooler welcome than Trump and Xi, with seating arrangements and a late arrival drawing commentary that he was sidelined. The declaration did not mention Russia's war in Ukraine or the US conflict with Iran, and analysts disagreed on whether Putin gained or lost ground.

actors.why: Hosted summit and gained prominence as Xi was seen as the central figure.
Putin was seen as sidelined and snubbed, though some analysts saw him gaining credibility.
Trump secured a symbolic photo opportunity but no arms control deal despite pushing for one.
Prime Minister Takaichi received no welcome ceremony, highlighting the summit's focus on the big powers.
Trump expressed interest in meeting Kim Jong Un, while Russia-North Korea ties drew Chinese irritation.

impact_points: Russia's Putin faces questions over his standing, though one analyst argued he gained credibility from the meeting.
Smaller nations and US allies worry their interests could be overlooked by the major powers' dealings.

auto-94455d6cb569.headline: Ukraine's European allies gather in Berlin as US envoys join talks
auto-94455d6cb569.summary:
Leaders of the Coalition of the Willing, a group of countries backing Ukraine, met in Berlin on November 19 to show a united front and press for a European role in any peace talks. The gathering came shortly after a three-way meeting in Shenzhen, China, between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe must be involved in any negotiations, while Kushner said Russia had grown comfortable with NATO Article 5-style guarantees for Ukraine, though Moscow has not commented.

Putin separately vowed retaliation after Ukrainian aerial attacks damaged the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia, and proposed that European officials travel to Moscow. Ukrainian President Zelensky urged pressure on Russia and new European sanctions.

actors.why: Seeks firmer allied backing and pressure on Russia; war continues
Kerch Bridge damaged; Putin vows retaliation and faces supply strain
Co-hosts summit and pushes for a European seat at talks
Co-hosts summit; Macron urges air defence and reopening NATO accession
Co-hosts summit and pushes for a unified European negotiating position
Envoys join Berlin talks, though European sidelining draws criticism

impact_points: Ukraine and European states seek a seat at any peace talks after feeling sidelined by Washington.
Russia faces possible retaliation and logistical strain after damage to the Kerch Bridge, its key supply route to Crimea.

auto-95ca05f49aeb.headline: EU releases record €7.9 billion tranche to Ukraine as it proposes new loan
auto-95ca05f49aeb.summary:
The European Commission has paid out €7.9 billion, its largest single tranche yet under the Ukraine Facility, to help Kyiv meet its financing needs and keep state institutions running during the war. Officials tied the payment to Ukrainian reforms in areas including the judiciary, anti-corruption work and energy, and said Kyiv had mobilised about €948 million in public investment.

Separately, the EU proposed a further €45 billion loan to cover much of Ukraine's projected 2027 funding gap of about €70 billion. EU leaders will discuss the plan at a summit next week, though some member states want to be excluded from financing it.

actors.why: Receives record funds for budget needs, tied to reform progress
Faces a bigger Western financial commitment to Ukraine, though its frozen assets remain untouched
Continues to block use of frozen Russian central bank assets held in Belgium
Seeks exemption from financing the new loan, resisting EU-wide cost sharing
Chancellor Merz insists all 27 members must settle financing before budget deal

impact_points: Ukraine receives urgent budget support to fund state operations while Russia's invasion continues.
Several EU states, including Hungary and Slovakia, resist sharing the cost, complicating the loan and wider budget talks.

auto-f2828db0a282.headline: Houthis warn of strikes on Saudi Red Sea ports and airspace
auto-f2828db0a282.summary:
Yemen's Houthi movement has threatened to attack Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports if the Saudi-led coalition follows through on a warning to bomb the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah. Military spokesman Yahya Saree urged workers, residents and shipping companies to leave the facilities immediately, and said Saudi airspace is unsafe, with the exception of the skies over Mecca and Medina.

The threats came after the coalition told civilians to evacuate Hodeidah port. Cross-border fighting between the coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, and the Houthis has intensified during the wider US-Israeli war on Iran.

actors.why: Threatened ports and airspace could be struck amid escalating cross-border fighting
Houthis threaten escalation but face coalition strikes on Hodeidah port
Houthis are Iran-aligned, and the front opens amid the US-Israeli war on Iran

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces possible strikes on Jeddah and other Red Sea ports, plus disruption to its airspace.
Shipping companies and airlines face safety risks and may need to move vessels or reroute flights.

auto-482a1c4917b2.headline: Italian workers and students strike nationwide over pay and living costs
auto-482a1c4917b2.summary: Workers and students in Italy were set to stage a nationwide strike on Friday, with schools, hospitals and local transport expected to be disrupted. Demonstrations were planned in more than 45 cities, timed to coincide with an International Day of Student Mobilisation. Protesters are calling for higher wages, lower living costs and stronger social protections. The action is a domestic labour and student protest with no reported international dimension.

actors.why: Nationwide strike disrupts services and pressures government on wages and costs

impact_points: Italy's public services, including schools, hospitals and local transport, face disruption from the strike action.
Italian workers and students are pressing the government for higher pay and stronger social protections.

auto-fe535de4143b.headline: Russian cruise missile enters Polish airspace during allied drills, Warsaw says
auto-fe535de4143b.summary: Poland says a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile was among three objects that entered its airspace early Friday, falling in rural southeastern areas near the Ukrainian border. Nobody was hurt and no damage was reported. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incursion did not look accidental, and noted it coincided with a Western-led exercise involving 11 countries in the region. Russia has not commented. Russia's attacks on Ukraine that day killed at least eight people, according to the reports. Nato's secretary general condemned the violations and Nato jets were scrambled.

Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges and Lviv killed civilians during the same day
Allied Coalition of the Willing drills and Nato response put European security in focus

impact_points: Poland faces a second airspace violation by Russian munitions this year, prompting it to seek additional Nato support.
Nato and its coalition partners face pressure to respond, as the incident occurred during preparations for a possible peace deal in Ukraine.

auto-47975d4014ab.headline: Putin invites Europeans to Moscow; Kremlin rejects Kallas role in talks
auto-47975d4014ab.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow has invited European representatives to Moscow to set out their position on ending the war in Ukraine, and that the Kremlin would then decide how dialogue should continue. He said the United States had pressed Russia to accept European participation. On Friday, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said that the presence of EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas in any future talks would cause them to collapse. Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said a possible visit by British, German and French representatives was being prepared.

European governments had previously named national security advisers from Germany, France, Britain, Italy, Poland and the EU to represent Europe. The Kremlin had said that European involvement in US-mediated talks had not been agreed.

Ukraine's future depends on talks where European participation is disputed
EU seeks a seat at talks, but Moscow rejects its foreign policy chief
Washington pushes for European participation, with Kremlin not yet agreeing

impact_points: Ukraine and European states face uncertainty over whether they will have a seat in peace negotiations.
Russia gains a possible channel to shape talks, while the EU's role and Kallas's position remain contested.

auto-6e05d6ab268b.headline: EU and UK urge Iran to halt Hormuz attacks and hybrid operations in Europe
auto-6e05d6ab268b.summary:
The European Union and Britain issued a joint statement after a Brussels summit condemning Iranian attacks on neighbouring states and on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. They demanded Tehran end its destabilising activity and what they called hybrid attacks on European soil, and reaffirmed that Iran must never obtain a nuclear weapon. Leaders also signed a pledge rejecting any tolls or fees for passage through the strait and agreed closer cooperation against cyber and hybrid threats.

The statement follows Iran-linked incidents in Europe, including a French probe into a cyber attack on supermarket refrigeration systems and convictions in Britain for spying on Iran International journalists. A US official separately told the Jerusalem Post that Iran has increasingly used anti-ship cruise missiles against vessels, while oil traffic through the strait remained high.

Coordinated stance against Iran and expanded cooperation on hybrid and cyber threats

Backed by the statement after Houthi attacks on Saudi territory and Red Sea shipping
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and shipping drew condemnation tied to Iranian allies

Gulf neighbours and shipping firms gain stronger Western backing for free navigation and against Iranian transit fees.

auto-9fca38365c9b.headline: Russian drone flights over Kyiv surge, with far longer routes and more intrusions
auto-9fca38365c9b.summary: Ukrainian investigative outlet Texty reported that Russian drones flew more than 19,000 kilometres over Kyiv between August and October, over four times the distance recorded in the same period of 2025. More than 630 drones were detected over the capital in that window, twice the 2025 figure. Analysts attribute the rise to Russia's growing use of faster, jet-powered Shahed drones, which are harder to intercept. Ukraine says it has ordered over 1,000 new interceptors and is developing faster models.

Long-range drone campaign against Ukrainian cities is intensifying and penetrating defences

impact_points: Ukraine, and Kyiv in particular, faces more drone penetration and longer flight paths over the capital.
Ukraine's defence innovation effort is racing to build faster interceptors and adapt electronic warfare against jet-powered drones.

auto-01a2053bdd88.headline: Arab and Islamic states back UK and Australian sanctions over West Bank settlements
auto-01a2053bdd88.summary:
Foreign ministers from roughly fifteen Arab and Islamic countries have welcomed sanctions imposed by Britain and Australia over Israeli settlement activity in the occupied West Bank. Britain targeted eight Israeli construction firms with asset freezes and director disqualifications, while Australia sanctioned three individuals and four organisations, including settler leader Daniella Weiss, over settlement expansion and settler violence.

In a joint statement, the ministers condemned Israel's settlement policies, especially the E1 project east of East Jerusalem, and called on other states to follow. They also urged full implementation of the US-backed plan to end the Gaza conflict and reaffirmed support for a two-state solution.

Gains diplomatic support against settlements and for a two-state solution

Joins regional statement backing sanctions and Palestinian statehood

auto-c47e5a72bc65.headline: Paris requests Security Council session after deadly Russian strikes on Kyiv
auto-c47e5a72bc65.summary:
France has asked for an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council after a fresh round of Russian missile strikes on Kyiv. Ukrainian officials said eight people were killed overnight, and the Austrian and Dutch embassies in the capital were damaged, though no diplomatic staff were hurt. France's foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, condemned the attacks as crimes and said Russia would have to answer for them.

The Dutch government summoned Russia's ambassador in response to the damage to its embassy. In a separate development, Poland reported that Russian objects, likely missiles and a drone, entered its airspace and fell on its territory, a claim Moscow has not immediately addressed.

actors.why: Eight killed in Kyiv strikes; civilians and capital under renewed attack
Faces UN Security Council scrutiny and condemnation over strikes and embassy damage
