Austria, the Netherlands and Poland are drawn into the crisis through damaged embassies and an airspace violation, raising pressure on NATO's eastern flank.

auto-349f8a493761.headline: Ukrainian strikes on Crimean Bridge disrupt Russian rail and road links
auto-349f8a493761.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Crimean Bridge, linking Russia with occupied Crimea, on November 19, 2026, with Neptune missiles, days after a strike collapsed a road section. Ukraine's Defense Ministry said rail traffic was halted and called the bridge a supply route for Russian troops in southern Ukraine. Russia's transport ministry confirmed the suspension, and occupation authorities announced passenger ferries across the Kerch Strait starting November 20. Putin said Russia would not negotiate a ceasefire after the strikes and promised a painful response.

actors.why: Bridge damage halts rail, forces ferries, and delays ceasefire talks
Strikes disrupt Russian supply lines, though Putin threatens retaliation

impact_points: Russia faces disrupted supply routes to occupied southern Ukraine, with repairs estimated to take a year or more.
Ukraine gains leverage by cutting a key logistics route, while Russia's ceasefire prospects appear to have collapsed.

auto-1416865b0ab4.headline: Washington warns Singapore and Malaysia to police Iran sanctions evasion
auto-1416865b0ab4.summary:
US Treasury officials met regulators and security bodies in Singapore and Malaysia this week, warning of risks if they fail to comply with American sanctions on Iran. Washington asked both countries, along with local banks and law firms, to watch for Iranian front companies, especially in maritime transport, aviation and procurement.

Officials said the US will target any lifeline supporting Iran and will not negotiate over it. They pointed to an Iranian airline that has flown to Malaysia, which Reuters linked to a Tehran-Kuala Lumpur route. Singapore said it is committed to preventing abuse of its corporate vehicles.

actors.why: Sanctions pressure is disrupting its oil revenue and overseas business links
Pressing allies to enforce sanctions and tighten Iran-linked network scrutiny
Must strengthen vigilance over shipping and finance under US pressure
Faces scrutiny over ship-to-ship oil transfers and Iranian airline flights

impact_points: Malaysia and Singapore face pressure to tighten oversight of shipping, aviation and financial firms.
Iran faces mounting economic strain as US efforts target its overseas business links and revenue.

auto-04d29b5c555f.headline: US Senate backs bill to fast-track energy project reviews
auto-04d29b5c555f.summary:
The US Senate voted 62-33 to approve a bipartisan bill aimed at shortening federal reviews for power plants, transmission lines and other energy infrastructure. Fifteen Democrats, including minority leader Chuck Schumer, joined Republicans in support, while two Republicans voted against. The measure would also require large AI data centres to pay more toward upgrading power grids.

President Donald Trump urged passage and said he would sign the bill if the House approves it. Environmental groups such as the Sierra Club warned it would weaken environmental protections and favour fossil fuel projects, while industry groups on both renewable and oil and gas sides backed it.

actors.why: Bill would speed energy approvals and ease electricity demand pressure, though critics say it weakens protections.

impact_points: The United States faces a bill that shortens energy permitting, aiming to lower electricity costs as demand grows.
Environmental groups and some Democrats warn of weaker protections and more fossil fuel development, while the House still must act.

auto-56b0e44ef25e.headline: Estonia closes all road crossings with Russia after arson attempt
auto-56b0e44ef25e.summary: Estonia has approved closing all five road border crossings with Russia from 1 December, following an attempted arson at a defence firm near Tallinn. Authorities blame Russian military intelligence and say Russian security services authorised two attacks on Estonian defence companies this year; Moscow denies involvement. The government says the closure could last at least six months and may be reviewed then. Rail services will continue. Russia's Foreign Ministry condemned the move and promised political and diplomatic responses.

actors.why: Closes road crossings for security, but gains a stronger response to hybrid attacks.
Loses road border access and faces accusations, with Moscow vowing a response.
Eight people from Latvia detained over the arson attempt, linking it to its territory.
Border closure reflects wider EU concern over Russian hybrid warfare on its eastern flank.

impact_points: Estonia faces tighter border controls and lost cross-border traffic, though it frames the step as a security measure.
Russia loses road access to a NATO and EU neighbour and has vowed diplomatic countermeasures, while Latvia's detention of eight suspects links the case to neighbouring territory.

auto-4b240450d24f.headline: US and Venezuela agree to restore military cooperation under interim government
auto-4b240450d24f.summary:
The United States and Venezuela have signed an agreement to re-establish military ties, less than a year after US forces seized former president Nicolás Maduro in a raid on Caracas. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth signed the deal with Venezuela's interim government, led by Delcy Rodríguez, during a visit to the capital. Hegseth said the deal includes intelligence sharing and joint training, though few specifics have been published. Rodríguez said the cooperation would help confront shared threats.

Hegseth also visited neighbouring Colombia, where President Abelardo de la Espriella is a close ally of the Trump administration. Critics argue the US has exerted heavy influence over Venezuela's government, while the broader boat-strike campaign has killed an estimated 240 people.

actors.why: Restores military ties and US backing for its interim government, though under heavy US influence
Expands military influence in Venezuela and the wider region against cartels
Closer alignment with US counter-cartel operations and a promised military aircraft delivery

impact_points: Venezuela's interim government gains a security partner and Washington's backing, while facing criticism of US influence over its affairs.
Colombia is drawn further into US-led counter-cartel efforts, with possible joint operations against armed groups under discussion.

auto-1f4a97a6946b.headline: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi weapons smuggling sites at Hodeidah port
auto-1f4a97a6946b.summary: A Saudi-led coalition carried out air strikes on Tuesday against the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah in Yemen, which it said was being used to smuggle weapons. The coalition described the operation as a special mission to neutralise threats to civilians in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. Al Masirah TV, which is linked to the Houthis, showed smoke rising from a sponge factory in Hodeidah after the reported strikes. Civilians had earlier been urged to leave the port area before the attacks.

actors.why: Hodeidah port hit by air strikes; civilians urged to evacuate, Houthi supply line targeted
Coalition led by Riyadh frames strikes as protecting kingdom from threats

impact_points: Yemen's Houthi movement faces military pressure as its Hodeidah port, a key entry point, is struck.
Saudi Arabia is positioning the strikes as protection against threats from Yemen, raising regional security tensions.

auto-45efe2e8bd7b.headline: Tanker set alight near Hormuz after projectile hit, Iran cites mine
auto-45efe2e8bd7b.summary:
A tanker caught fire after being hit by an unidentified projectile while sailing through the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Friday. The incident happened about 8 nautical miles north of the Omani town of Khasab, and no casualties or environmental damage were reported.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said shortly afterwards that an oil tanker had caught fire after striking a mine near Khasab, according to Iranian state media. Shipping through the strait has been disrupted since Iran moved to close the waterway after the US-Israeli conflict with Iran began on February 28.

actors.why: Attack occurred near Omani town of Khasab; coastal security and shipping at risk
Revolutionary Guards blamed a mine; Iran's closure of the strait is under pressure
Conflict with Iran continues to disrupt strait shipping and regional security

impact_points: Oman and its Musandam Peninsula sit beside the attack site, with shipping through the strait already disrupted.
Global oil markets face added supply risk, since the strait normally carries nearly a fifth of world crude.

auto-9be7fd327727.headline: US Army delays detonation of degraded lead azide in Iowa after public alarm
auto-9be7fd327727.summary:
The US Army has pushed back its plan to blow up about five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, now moving the detonation to Monday. The chemical, a sensitive bomb-making compound, was found deteriorating earlier this year and the army says detonation is the safest disposal route. Residents and state officials have voiced alarm that the blast could send a plume of lead particles drifting north, prompting school closures, evacuation advisories and a lawsuit by environmental groups seeking emergency court action.

Iowa's governor, Kim Reynolds, pressed for the delay and spoke with the acting army secretary, while the governor-elect criticised poor communication. The Environmental Protection Agency approved an emergency permit requiring public notice and dust tracking.

actors.why: Army must dispose of unstable chemical but faces public backlash and delays

impact_points: Middletown residents and nearby communities face possible lead dust drift, window damage and school closures.
The US Army faces public trust and communication criticism over how it handled the disposal plan.

auto-4045402abbe7.headline: UNICEF reports record child casualties in Ukraine this year amid Russian strikes
auto-4045402abbe7.summary:
UNICEF says at least 1,144 children were killed or injured in Ukraine between January and October 2026, the highest verified figure in the three years of the war. The agency, citing UN human rights monitors, counts 114 children killed and 1,030 injured, with child casualties in October up sharply from a year earlier.

The figures were released as a large overnight Russian missile and drone attack killed at least nine people and damaged bridges and utilities in Kyiv. Separately, Russian strikes hit the Odesa district, killing four and injuring at least 13, according to regional officials.

actors.why: Child casualties rising sharply; energy and civilian infrastructure repeatedly struck.
Long-range strikes on cities and civilian sites draw international criticism.

impact_points: Ukraine faces a sharp rise in child deaths and injuries, with attacks on energy and schools intensifying.
Children and families across Ukraine, including far from the front, face lasting physical and psychological harm.

auto-6bc69d9935b7.headline: Overnight Russian strikes hit Kyiv bridges and kill several across Ukraine
auto-6bc69d9935b7.summary:
Russia carried out a large overnight air attack on Ukraine, with missiles and drones striking Kyiv and other regions. Kyiv's mayor said three bridges over the Dnipro River were damaged, disrupting traffic in the capital, and citywide power outages were reported. Ukrainian officials put the death toll at eight, including six in Kyiv, with dozens wounded. The attack followed a Ukrainian strike on the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea, which Moscow's leader Vladimir Putin vowed to answer.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles, targeting civilian energy and transport infrastructure. Russia's defence ministry said it hit military-industrial sites and bridges used to move weapons. Diplomatic efforts toward a ceasefire showed little progress, with Moscow rejecting any form of Ukrainian NATO membership.

actors.why: Mass strikes killed eight, damaged Kyiv bridges, and cut power across regions.
Retaliatory strike rejects a ceasefire, but Kerch Bridge damage and Ukrainian drone attacks cost Moscow.
European states back Ukraine and are considered for negotiations, though the attack deepens security concerns.
US-led ceasefire mediation made little progress, with envoy comments suggesting openness to security guarantees.

impact_points: Ukraine faces heavy civilian casualties and damage to bridges, power generation and transport across several regions.
Russia faces retaliation pressure after the Kerch Bridge attack, while its rejection of Ukrainian NATO ties stalls talks with the US, Europe and Kyiv.

auto-475d440fc582.headline: Israeli tank raid into central Gaza ends; Palestinians return to Nuseirat
auto-475d440fc582.summary: Israeli forces carried out a tank raid across the ceasefire boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza, targeting what the military called Hamas infrastructure near the Nuseirat refugee camp. It was the first such ground operation past the yellow line since the October 2025 ceasefire, and it displaced thousands. Israel's military later said the operation had been completed and the Salah al-Din road reopened. Palestinian officials reported further deaths and injuries from shelling and strikes, and the UN-backed Board of Peace warned the truce was at risk.

actors.why: Civilians displaced and killed; Hamas says the raid violated the ceasefire.
Tank raid achieved its tunnel-dismantling aim but drew international criticism over the truce.
Backs the Board of Peace overseeing the ceasefire, which is now at risk of collapse.

impact_points: Palestinians in central Gaza were displaced again, with many losing shelter and property during the raid.
The fragile October 2025 ceasefire is under strain, with Israel, Hamas and the Board of Peace trading accusations.

auto-1b96fd7a32ae.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin pledge more fuel supply, but analysts doubt it
auto-1b96fd7a32ae.summary:
At a three-way summit in Shenzhen, China, the leaders of the United States, China and Russia said they plan to raise output and supply of refined petroleum products. The pledge came as wars involving Iran and Ukraine disrupt global energy markets. Analysts questioned how it would work, noting that US refineries already run near full capacity, Russian refining has been hit by Ukrainian drone strikes, and China's crude imports have been disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz conflict.

The joint statement also reaffirmed that nuclear war must never be fought but set no arms control talks. Ukraine's president Zelenskyy said China and the US could pressure Moscow into ending the war through sanctions.

actors.why: Pledged fuel supply boost but has little spare refining capacity
Pledged fuel supply boost while crude imports are disrupted by Hormuz conflict
Joined pledge but refining is hit hard by Ukrainian drone strikes
Continued Russian war and Zelenskyy calls for outside pressure on Moscow
Heavily dependent on crude imports affected by Hormuz blockades

impact_points: Ukraine faces ongoing pressure from Russian strikes, and Zelenskyy urges China and the US to press Moscow.
Consumers in fuel-importing countries such as India and China may see little relief, as analysts doubt supply will rise.

auto-0bae2053ebb0.headline: Moscow rejects quasi-NATO guarantees for Ukraine as US floats Article 5-style protection
auto-0bae2053ebb0.summary:
US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington is open to security guarantees for post-war Ukraine modelled on NATO's Article 5 mutual defence clause, and claimed Russia is comfortable with the idea. He spoke at a meeting in Berlin of around 40 European allies of Ukraine, days after a first-ever summit in China involving Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Kushner said any guarantee would need to serve American interests and form part of a wider security package.

Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov rejected any form of quasi-membership of NATO for Kyiv, while French President Emmanuel Macron called for Ukraine's NATO membership to be reconsidered. The claim about Russia's comfort could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Offered possible Article 5-style guarantees, but the deal remains uncertain and unagreed
Rejects quasi-NATO membership for Kyiv, calling it totally unacceptable
Pushing a security plan while seeking a deal with Russia and Europe
Largely sidelined from US-Russia talks, pressing for a role at the table

impact_points: Ukraine would gain possible Article 5-style protection, but Russia has rejected any quasi-NATO arrangement for Kyiv.
European allies, sidelined from US-Russia talks, are pressing to be at the table, while Moscow warns against any NATO-linked role.

auto-d72f5e515bea.headline: Iraq's government moves to take control of militia-held Jurf al-Sakhar
auto-d72f5e515bea.summary: Iraq's government under Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered army, federal police and Popular Mobilization Units to secure Jurf al-Sakhar, a area south of Baghdad controlled by the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah. The move follows a government report alleging the group smuggled hundreds of millions of dollars of state oil from nearby pipelines since 2021, which the group denies. Kataib Hezbollah has rejected an order to withdraw, with a commander vowing its fighters would leave only "over our dead bodies." Reuters reported late Thursday that a compromise had been reached on the deployment, though its terms were unclear.

actors.why: Government seeks to reassert state authority and secure oil sites, but risks confrontation.
Iran-backed militia faces losing control of its stronghold; Tehran is mediating.
Pressure on Iraq to disarm Iran-aligned groups aligns with US interests.

impact_points: Iraq's government is testing whether it can reassert authority over Iran-backed armed groups inside its borders.
Iran, which backs Kataib Hezbollah, faces a setback to its influence in Iraq, though it has sent a commander to mediate.

auto-6efc918adf31.headline: Estonia to shut road crossings with Russia; Moscow vows response
auto-6efc918adf31.summary:
Estonia's government has approved a preliminary six-month closure of its road border crossings with Russia, starting December 1, citing security concerns. Officials say the move will limit Russian intelligence recruitment, influence operations, sabotage and sanctions evasion, after Tallinn accused Russian security services of an attempted arson attack on a defence company, which the Kremlin denies.

Moscow's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova called the plan an attempt to build a new Iron Curtain and said Russia would take political and diplomatic steps if it goes ahead. Rail freight remains open, subject to customs checks.

actors.why: Border closure is a security measure, but cuts road access for residents and travellers.
Loses road crossings and faces a pledged diplomatic response to the closure.
Its own Russia crossings have been shut since 2023, so the move reinforces existing policy.
Maintains open crossings with Russia while neighbouring Estonia closes its own.
Keeps its Russia crossings open; indirectly affected by the regional border policy shift.

impact_points: Estonia gains tighter control over cross-border movement, but border communities and travellers lose easy road access.
Russia faces diplomatic pushback and fewer crossing routes, with Moscow promising a response to the closure.

auto-7fc91c968022.headline: Ukraine's General Staff reports Russian losses topping 1.63 million troops
auto-7fc91c968022.summary: Ukraine's General Staff says Russian forces suffered about 1,970 to 2,150 casualties in the past day, depending on the report, bringing the cumulative total since February 2022 to roughly 1.63 million. The figure covers killed and wounded personnel and also includes large amounts of lost equipment, such as thousands of tanks and armoured vehicles. Ukraine's own losses are not disclosed by its military, while Western think-tank estimates suggest Russian casualties significantly exceed Ukrainian ones. The Ukrainian figures could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Reports large cumulative casualties and equipment losses, a heavy strategic and manpower cost
Continues to absorb heavy fighting and casualties, though reported Russian losses favour its position

impact_points: Russia faces mounting personnel and equipment losses, with October 2026 reported as its deadliest month for combat casualties.
Ukraine receives a claimed battlefield advantage in attrition, though its own losses remain undisclosed and unverified.

auto-e934ead5ca52.headline: Somalia expels UAE envoy and recalls its own ambassador amid worsening rift
auto-e934ead5ca52.summary: Somalia has ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador to leave within 72 hours and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi. Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud accused the Emirates of violating Somalia's sovereignty in what he called an open invasion, without specifying the actions involved. The UAE condemned Mogadishu's approach as escalatory and hostile, saying Somalia was trying to pull it into internal power struggles. The UAE closed its embassy in Mogadishu in January 2026, and the dispute follows Somalia's earlier cancellation of agreements with Abu Dhabi, including port and security deals.

actors.why: Diplomatic rupture and loss of Emirati military and port ties
Expelled envoy and loses influence in Somalia, though it denounces Mogadishu

impact_points: Somalia faces a deepening diplomatic rupture with the UAE, which has funded and trained its military and backed ports.
UAE-linked regional administrations in Somalia and the Emirates' Horn of Africa influence could be strained by the escalating dispute.

auto-6f9524a642b5.headline: Senator blocks Trump's cybersecurity nominee after he denies January 6 attack
auto-6f9524a642b5.summary: Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who is leaving office after clashing with Donald Trump, has reportedly placed a hold on the nomination of Michael LoSapio to lead the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency. At his Senate hearing, LoSapio said he did not believe the January 6, 2021 Capitol assault was an attack, after first saying he did not know. The agency he would lead helps protect US election infrastructure. The hold means the nomination will not be included in a package of nominees due for a vote next month, before Republicans lose their Senate majority.

actors.why: Key cybersecurity agency leadership is delayed amid a dispute over the nominee's January 6 remarks.

impact_points: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency faces a delayed leadership appointment, leaving its election-security role without a confirmed director.
Trump's nominee and his administration face pressure over their stance on the January 6 attack before the Senate majority changes.

auto-b8c1b2f44792.headline: California subpoenas Nvidia over possible chip diversion to China and investor disclosures
auto-b8c1b2f44792.summary: California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, has issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia, examining whether its advanced semiconductor chips reached China despite US export restrictions and whether the company misled investors. The probe follows the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang after reports of multiple affairs, including one with a woman linked to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which has bought nearly $5bn of Nvidia hardware and is being examined over possible chip diversion to China. Megaspeed says it operates legally. Nvidia's shares have fallen about a fifth since Huang's admission, and Huang is due to testify before congressional committees on 1 December.

actors.why: Export controls on advanced chips to China are being tested by the state probe
Alleged access to advanced chips and confidential information raises its strategic gains
Megaspeed, based there, is under investigation for possible chip diversion

impact_points: Nvidia faces a state investigation into export compliance and investor disclosures, with its share value down about a fifth.
Rival AMD fell nearly 8% after short-seller-linked reports questioned its China ties, which AMD disputes.

auto-899e0517af63.headline: Japan uneasy over possible regular US-China-Russia summits in Shenzhen
auto-899e0517af63.summary: Japan is worried that a first-ever trilateral summit between the United States, China and Russia in Shenzhen could become a recurring event. Officials in Tokyo said they were relieved nothing major was decided, while Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spoke by phone with President Donald Trump to reaffirm close ties. Separately, Takaichi met Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit for about 30 minutes, agreeing to keep communicating. Tokyo raised the detention of a Japanese journalist in Russia and the seizure of Japan Tobacco assets there.

actors.why: Worried about sidelining and a Russian seizure of Japanese assets
Trump's engagement in the trilateral format is a major factor; Japan-US ties on the ICC differ
Hosted the trilateral summit and gains prominence as a power broker
Gained prominence through the summit, though relations with Japan remain strained

impact_points: Japan fears the three major powers may meet regularly, sidelining its role in global affairs.
Japan Tobacco faces a projected 724 billion yen loss after Russia seized some of its subsidiaries.

auto-56d302d00016.headline: Vance avoids saying whether he would have approved Iran strikes
auto-56d302d00016.summary:
US Vice President JD Vance declined to say whether he would have authorised the February strikes on Iran aimed at preventing a nuclear weapon, saying the call belonged to President Trump. Trump urged him to affirm the attacks were necessary and that he would repeat them. Vance had earlier blamed the war for Republican midterm losses and called for the US to exit the conflict. Separately, reports said Trump was weighing a renewed Israeli-backed air campaign against Iran, with Israeli and American officials citing Iranian chemical and biological weapons concerns, which could not be independently verified.

Trump has reportedly told Vance to drop negotiations with Tehran in favour of economic pressure. Iran is the central party, while Israel is pressing for further strikes.

actors.why: Faces possible renewed strikes and economic pressure over its nuclear and weapons programmes
Divided internally over Iran strikes, political costs and renewed military options
Pressing for a new air campaign against Iran, backed by its intelligence warnings

impact_points: Iran faces renewed US and Israeli military pressure and the possibility of another air campaign.
Israel is pushing Washington for a swift strike, shaping how the US weighs its options.

auto-71d07ec4218b.headline: US warns Singapore and Malaysia to police Iran sanctions evasion
auto-71d07ec4218b.summary:
US Treasury officials met regulators and national security bodies in Singapore and Malaysia this week, warning of risks if they fail to comply with US sanctions on Iran. Washington asked both countries, along with local banks and law firms, to watch for Iranian front companies, especially in maritime transport, aviation and procurement.

Officials said the US will target any lifeline keeping Iran's business going and will not negotiate over it. They also flagged an Iranian airline that has flown to Kuala Lumpur, which Reuters linked to a scheduled service. Singapore said it is committed to preventing abuse of its corporate vehicles, and Malaysia did not respond to requests for comment.

actors.why: Pressed by US to police front companies and banks; faces compliance pressure
Warned over sanctions risks; asked to tighten scrutiny of Iranian flights and tankers
Sanctions pressure deepens as revenue falls and its air links are targeted
Advancing its sanctions campaign against Iran through allied financial hubs

impact_points: Singapore and Malaysia face pressure to tighten oversight of banks, shipping and aviation firms.
Iran faces tighter sanctions pressure on its overseas trade and revenue as its economy contracts sharply.

auto-d8bfb638af53.headline: US and China hold annual maritime military safety talks in Shanghai
auto-d8bfb638af53.summary: The United States and China held their yearly maritime military safety consultations in Shanghai, a working-level channel meant to reduce the risk of accidents between their navies and air forces at sea. The meeting took place alongside high-level contacts between the two countries' leaders, including a trilateral summit in Shenzhen that also involved Russia. The reporting available does not give details of specific agreements reached at the Shanghai working group.

actors.why: Hosts talks that help manage military risk with Washington
Keeps a crisis-prevention channel open with a major rival at sea
Watches US-China military contacts while holding its own summit ties

impact_points: China and the United States gain a channel to manage the risk of unplanned military encounters at sea.
Russia and other regional navies are indirectly affected by the signals of military stability between Washington and Beijing.

auto-722d1c4ef062.headline: US floats NATO-style guarantees for Ukraine as Russia pushes back
auto-722d1c4ef062.summary:
US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington is open to security guarantees for post-war Ukraine modelled on NATO's Article 5 mutual defence clause, and claimed Russia is comfortable with the idea. He spoke at a meeting in Berlin of around 40 Ukrainian allies, a day after a first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen involving Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, which produced a four-point declaration on peace.

Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov rejected any form of 'quasi membership' of NATO for Kyiv, and Moscow has long warned that Ukrainian NATO membership would bring a harsh response. Analysts noted the US has not clearly defined its commitment, and the claimed Russian acceptance could not be independently confirmed.

actors.why: Seeks security guarantees, but the plan remains uncertain and unagreed
Publicly rejects quasi-NATO membership for Ukraine, opposing the proposal
Pitches a new plan while stating it must serve America's interests
Sidelined in US-Russia talks, angered, and pushing for a larger role
Hosted the trilateral summit and joint declaration with the US and Russia

impact_points: Ukraine would gain potential security backing for after the war, if Washington and Moscow agree.
Russia has rejected quasi-NATO membership for Kyiv, so the proposal faces firm resistance from Moscow.

auto-09e73f0bcf53.headline: Houthi missile hits Riyadh tower as Saudi-led coalition intercepts attacks
auto-09e73f0bcf53.summary: Saudi Arabia says a Houthi attack damaged the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh's financial district, causing material damage but no injuries. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted missiles fired toward the capital and the south, including four ballistic missiles, and destroyed a launchpad. Saudi aircraft also reportedly struck Sanaa, a claim made by the Houthi-run Saba agency. The strike is part of a wider Houthi campaign against Saudi airports, oil facilities and offices, and fighting has displaced more than 330,000 people in Yemen.

actors.why: Tower damaged in Riyadh and repeated missile attacks on cities and oil sites
Renewed fighting has displaced over 330,000 people and caused heavy casualties
Houthis, whom Iran backs, are escalating attacks on Saudi targets

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces damage to its sovereign wealth fund headquarters and renewed attacks on its cities and infrastructure.
Yemen's civilians face rising displacement and casualties as the 2022 truce collapses and fighting intensifies.

auto-0ee2e6f45e54.headline: Israeli tank raid in central Gaza ends; Palestinian militias accused of support
auto-0ee2e6f45e54.summary:
Israel's military said it had completed a ground operation in central Gaza that began Wednesday, targeting what it described as a tunnel crossing beneath the Yellow Line. The incursion, the first major Israeli ground move beyond the line since the October 2025 ceasefire, prompted roughly 6,000 Palestinians to flee, according to Gaza's government media office. Residents returned Thursday to find the Salah al-Din road scarred by track marks and earthen barriers, and at least one person was reported killed in nearby strikes.

Palestinian sources and analysts alleged that Israeli-backed local armed groups took part in the operation, intimidating families into leaving their homes. These claims could not be independently verified, and Hamas called the raid a blatant ceasefire violation.

actors.why: Families displaced again, roads damaged, and deaths reported during the incursion.
Military claims it destroyed a tunnel threat, though it faces ceasefire violation accusations.
US-brokered ceasefire is strained, with the truce overseer blaming both sides.

impact_points: Palestine and displaced Gazans face renewed displacement, damaged shelters and continued deadly strikes near the Yellow Line.
Israel gains a temporary tunnel strike, but faces accusations of violating the truce and of backing armed militias.

auto-0fd3cedb47ec.headline: Trump defends Russia and China ties, criticises Iran's negotiating approach
auto-0fd3cedb47ec.summary:
US President Donald Trump defended his close relationships with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin after a summit in Asia, calling critics of the ties foolish. He described Putin as a source of strength for America and said the Russian leader wanted an end to the war in Ukraine through diplomacy, though he blamed hostility between Putin and Ukrainian President Zelenskyy for stalling a deal.

On Iran, Trump said Tehran had not offered acceptable terms for a deal and accused its government of dishonesty. He also said reports of an Iranian plot involving a radioactive dirty bomb would bring a severe response, while Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected the allegations as baseless.

actors.why: Faces US accusations, sanctions and threats of severe retaliation over alleged plots
Leader defends ties with rivals but offers little concrete progress on Iran or Ukraine
Trump praises Putin and says his ties strengthen America, boosting Moscow's standing
Xi meeting seen as a boost to Beijing's push for a rebalancing of global power
Peace in Ukraine remains stalled, with no security guarantees yet discussed

impact_points: Iran faces continued US pressure, including sanctions and a naval blockade, with no agreed deal in sight.
Russia and China gain political standing from the summit, while Ukraine faces stalled peace efforts.

auto-906c65e42e84.headline: Ukraine strikes Crimean Bridge again as Russia weighs retaliation
auto-906c65e42e84.summary:
Ukraine attacked the bridge linking annexed Crimea to Russia on Thursday, the third strike on the transport link in a week, according to a Russia-appointed official. Railway traffic was halted, and Russia's transport ministry said no one was wounded. Earlier strikes on Tuesday had destroyed a road arch and blocked the shipping channel, and officials have offered no firm repair timeline.

Russian President Vladimir Putin reportedly threatened retaliatory strikes and said a partial ceasefire idea was dropped after the bridge attacks. Ukrainian officials say the bridge is used for military purposes, and Ukraine's president argued that Crimea is Ukrainian territory.

actors.why: Bridge damaged, supply route disrupted, Putin threatens retaliation
Strikes on a key military-use transport link to Crimea
Putin's China meeting coincided with the strike, affecting regional diplomacy

impact_points: Russia faces disrupted supply routes to Crimea and a damaged symbol of Putin's rule, with no clear repair timeline.
Ukraine gains leverage as the bridge strikes continue, while Putin has threatened stronger retaliation.

auto-18c6bf478a05.headline: UN talks on autonomous weapons end with pledge for further rules
auto-18c6bf478a05.summary: Negotiations at the UN Convention on Conventional Weapons in Geneva on lethal autonomous weapons, often called killer robots, ran into a deadline after five days of talks. Russia in particular slowed progress, while states including the United States and Russia resisted being bound by strict rules. Most of the 128 member states favour a legally binding agreement, though the Red Cross proposed one year of negotiations and Washington proposed five years. A later report from Reuters says the talks ended with a pledge to develop new rules within two years, with Russia, the United States and Israel opposing firmer commitments, and that it remained unclear whether future measures would be legally binding.

actors.why: Russia slowed talks and opposed observers, keeping its freedom to develop such weapons.
Washington resisted binding rules and proposed a five-year negotiation timeline.
Israel opposed firm rules, aligning with major arms producers against binding limits.
France pushed a hybrid approach combining binding and non-binding measures.
Such systems have reportedly been tested or deployed in the war in Ukraine.

impact_points: Russia is blocking faster progress on binding rules, drawing criticism from rights groups and most states.
The United States and Israel also resist binding limits, leaving states that want firm rules without a clear path.

auto-589171948ccf.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen, issue vague peace declaration
auto-589171948ccf.summary: Leaders of the United States, China and Russia met in person for the first time on November 19 in Shenzhen, China, and issued a joint declaration. It reaffirmed that nuclear war must never be fought and pledged UN reform, more fuel supplies and protection for state officials' immunity in international courts. The document did not mention Ukraine or the US conflict with Iran, and it set no timeline for nuclear talks. Commentators widely rejected comparisons to the 1945 Yalta conference, calling the results modest. Analysts said the meeting gave Putin publicity and China a leading role, while Trump drew criticism from US lawmakers.

actors.why: Gains prominence as a central broker in great-power negotiations and reinforced its role.
Gained publicity and escaped pariah status, though the declaration constrains some positions.
Trump secured few tangible results and faced criticism from US allies and Democrats.
Excluded from the declaration, with its war unresolved and its future decided elsewhere.
Japan was among US allies left uneasy by Trump's closeness to Xi and Putin.

impact_points: Ukraine is left out of the declaration, with its war with Russia unaddressed despite its European backers meeting in Berlin.
Smaller states worry their interests could be ignored as the great powers negotiate among themselves over the international order.

auto-1b0e403c2714.headline: World Court's Myanmar genocide ruling could shape South Africa's case against Israel
auto-1b0e403c2714.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, finding that the 2017 killings, razing of homes, sexual violence and forced exodus of over 700,000 people amounted to state-sponsored genocide. Legal experts say the judgment may strengthen South Africa's genocide case against Israel over the Gaza war, since it holds that genocidal intent can coexist with a military objective. Israel and Myanmar both describe their operations as legitimate responses to insurgencies. Israel's own case is not expected to be argued until 2029, and Israel rejects the allegations.

actors.why: Ruling lowers the proof threshold and may weaken Israel's defence against genocide charges
Judgment strengthens South Africa's case against Israel and offers more arguments
Court found state-sponsored genocide and ordered reparations and refugee return
Gambia won major legal victories in the case it brought on behalf of Muslim-majority states
Gaza civilians are at the centre of the case; the ruling may advance accountability efforts

impact_points: Israel faces a lower bar for proving genocidal intent, which could weaken its defence before the court.
South Africa gains broader grounds to argue its genocide case, with Myanmar's ruling used as a precedent.

auto-a044337e3864.headline: US cost of Iran war put at $48.3bn, excluding base repairs
auto-a044337e3864.summary: A Pentagon official told US lawmakers that the war against Iran has cost an estimated $48.3 billion. The total covers munitions, replacement of equipment and day-to-day operating expenses. It does not include the cost of repairing US military installations in the Middle East that were damaged after fighting began in February, so the final bill is likely higher. The figure was presented to Congress as lawmakers press for more detail on the damage to bases.

actors.why: Bears a $48.3bn cost, excluding base repairs, and faces congressional scrutiny
Is the target of the US campaign and has suffered military losses

impact_points: The United States faces a large, growing financial burden from the Iran conflict, with base repair costs still uncounted.
Iran is directly affected as the target of the campaign, with its territory and military at the centre of the fighting.

auto-eed2a9a4a655.headline: Iran claims it downed another US MQ-9 drone over Hormuz
auto-eed2a9a4a655.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps said its aerospace forces shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of Saturday, using a newly deployed air defence system. The IRGC described it as the 58th MQ-9 downed by Iranian forces. Iranian officials said they monitor military and aerial activity in the strategic waterway and will respond firmly to violations of their airspace. The claim could not be independently verified. The MQ-9 Reaper is a medium-altitude drone used by the US military for surveillance and strikes. The report places the incident within the wider US-Israeli conflict with Iran that began in late February.

actors.why: Claims a new air defence system downed a US drone over its strait
Loses another MQ-9 surveillance drone during the wider conflict
Is named as a co-belligerent in the wider war with Iran
Borders the Strait of Hormuz and faces heightened regional military risk

impact_points: The United States loses another surveillance drone, if Iran's claim is confirmed, amid the ongoing conflict.
Iran signals a tougher stance on Hormuz airspace, raising tensions for shipping and regional states nearby.

auto-f084cd9f83a6.headline: Trump praises Putin talks on Ukraine but defers security guarantees
auto-f084cd9f83a6.summary:
US President Donald Trump said he and Russian President Vladimir Putin had productive talks on Ukraine during the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, and that he expects a diplomatic path to end the war. He said he would not discuss security guarantees for Ukraine until a broader peace deal is reached.

Trump's comments came after a Kushner-led round of Ukraine talks in Berlin, where guarantees modelled on NATO's Article 5 were reportedly floated. Russia's deputy foreign minister rejected any form of quasi-membership for Kyiv. Trump described the differing accounts as negotiating posturing, and Russia launched a major missile and drone attack on Ukraine shortly after the leaders issued their declaration, killing eight people.

actors.why: Civilians hit by a large strike; guarantees deferred until a broader deal
Direct talks with Trump; rejects quasi-membership for Kyiv
Trump pursues a diplomatic deal but holds back on guarantees
Hosted the APEC summit and the leaders' meetings in Shenzhen

impact_points: Ukraine faces continued strikes and a stalled debate over security guarantees while a settlement is pursued.
Russia gains diplomatic momentum from direct talks with Trump, but faces Moscow's firm rejection of Western-style guarantees for Kyiv.

auto-b05480e642e5.headline: US pushes Ukraine and Russia toward a deal before Congress changes hands
auto-b05480e642e5.summary:
US negotiators have reportedly told European and Ukrainian officials they want a Russia-Ukraine peace agreement by early January 2027, before Democrats take control of Congress. The Financial Times, citing unnamed sources, reported that a European official feared Kyiv would have to make substantial concessions. Ukrainian officials reportedly worried Zelensky could be pressed into terms set by Moscow.

The push followed a trilateral summit in China involving Trump, Xi Jinping and Putin, where Trump said Putin wanted an end to the war. Putin said Ukraine and its European allies must accept compromises, and a joint declaration from the meeting made no mention of Ukraine.

actors.why: Faces pressure to make major concessions on territory and security under a rushed timeline
Gains from a US push for quick talks and pressure on Kyiv to concede
Pursues a rapid deal before a Democratic-led Congress could increase Ukraine aid
Sidelined from early talks and wants a ceasefire before wider European security discussions
Hosted the trilateral summit that shaped the diplomatic push

impact_points: Ukraine faces pressure to accept concessions, including territory in Donbas, before a possible deal.
European countries seek a formal role and a ceasefire, while Russia says any final deal needs their input.

auto-dac4d433cb1b.headline: Fire at Hartha power station near Basra kills four in Iraq
auto-dac4d433cb1b.summary: A fire at the Hartha power station, north of Basra in southern Iraq, killed at least four people and injured around 30 on Saturday, November 21, 2026, and officials said the toll could rise. Civil defence teams brought the blaze under control, but it spread to nearby homes and halted operations at the plant. The station has an installed capacity of 800 megawatts but was running at about 400 megawatts before the fire. No official cause or damage assessment had been released, and the reporting notes Iraq's power grid has long suffered from underinvestment and poor maintenance.

actors.why: Deaths and injuries, a halted power plant and strained grid

impact_points: Iraq loses part of its power supply at Hartha, worsening chronic electricity shortages in the south.
Residents of Basra and neighbouring homes face casualties, property damage and possible further outages.

auto-1d2cc8cafd2b.headline: Crimean Bridge repair timeline unknown after Ukrainian strikes; Putin vows response
auto-1d2cc8cafd2b.summary:
Russia says it cannot yet set a date for repairing the Crimean Bridge, which links occupied Crimea to Russia's Krasnodar Krai across the Kerch Strait. Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed the central road span this week, in one of several strikes that Ukraine said answered Russian attacks on its infrastructure. Russian officials say the steel arch and roadway beam were damaged, with one estimate of about two years for full replacement under wartime conditions. Road traffic is halted and rail service has partly resumed on a single track.

President Vladimir Putin rejected negotiations after the strikes and promised retaliation he said would be more painful, while also saying the bridge would be rebuilt. Ukraine says the bridge was a key supply route for Russian forces in Crimea and southern Ukraine.

actors.why: Bridge closed to road traffic; logistics strained and retaliation promised
Strikes disrupt Russian supply lines, but Putin signals harsher retaliation

impact_points: Russia faces disrupted supply routes to Crimea and southern Ukraine, with traffic diverted onto the R-280 highway.
Ukraine's strikes add pressure on Russian logistics, while Moscow signals escalation rather than talks.

auto-b5b52e3019ef.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold rare three-way talks at APEC in Shenzhen
auto-b5b52e3019ef.summary:
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met for trilateral talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. The closed-door session lasted about 55 minutes. Xi called the gathering historically significant and urged a nuclear-free world, while Putin signalled that Ukraine would dominate his discussion. Analysts expected no major agreements given deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear arms and trade.

Before the trilateral, Trump held separate bilateral meetings with Xi and Putin, calling both a friend. Russia's Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said the Putin-Trump meeting went well and that Putin left in an excellent mood. Smaller countries reportedly worried their interests might be ignored.

actors.why: Putin gains prestige and direct access to Trump, with Ukraine central to talks
Trump engages Xi and Putin directly, though deep disagreements remain unresolved
Xi gains a stability-focused framing and a showcase as host of APEC
Ukraine is the focus of Putin's remarks, with no settlement announced
Europe is portrayed as sidelined by the meeting of the big three powers

impact_points: Russia gains visible high-level engagement with Washington and Beijing, though no concrete deal was expected.
Smaller nations and European partners may feel sidelined by a meeting between the three largest nuclear powers.

auto-944f32b12b7b.headline: Tanker attacks in Hormuz raise pollution fears and push oil prices
auto-944f32b12b7b.summary: Attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have intensified, with reports of several vessels exploding after striking naval mines and at least two seafarers missing. Endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh entered the waters during the blasts to highlight the environmental toll, warning that oil contamination could take decades to clean up after the fighting ends. Brent crude nonetheless edged up on Thursday, trading near $92.58 a barrel, though it had fallen sharply earlier in the month as Middle East exports neared prewar levels. Iran is widely linked to the strikes in the reporting, though attribution could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Accused of the tanker attacks; faces international pressure over the Hormuz campaign
Coast near the strait where a burning tanker was seen; exposed to pollution
Fighting in the war on Iran; oil markets and naval operations affected
Named as a party in the US-Israeli war on Iran
Gulf oil exporter whose shipments depend on safe passage through Hormuz

impact_points: Gulf states and shipping firms face disruption, casualties and rising insurance and transit risks through Hormuz.
Marine ecosystems and coastal communities face long-term oil pollution that could outlast the conflict.

auto-eedd0e631dee.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin hold first trilateral summit; nuclear risk talks yield pledges
auto-eedd0e631dee.summary:
Leaders of China, the United States and Russia met in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit, holding their first trilateral talks. The meeting lasted roughly 80 to 90 minutes behind closed doors. Afterwards the three governments issued a joint declaration pledging to pursue strategic stability, open a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks, and reform the United Nations. It also called for protecting state officials from international courts, a point aimed at the International Criminal Court, which has an arrest warrant out for Putin.

The ambitions were broad, but the concrete steps were limited. Beijing has long insisted that the United States and Russia cut their larger arsenals before it joins arms control talks. Ukraine and the Middle East were also on the agenda. Analysts had expected the summit to offer more symbolism than breakthroughs.

actors.why: Hosted the summit and gained prominence as a peer of the US
Gained a platform with Washington, though Putin faces ICC warrant pressure
Secured nuclear dialogue pledges but achieved few concrete arms control steps
Received a noticeably cool welcome from Chinese hosts at the summit
Kim Jong Un did not meet Trump, leaving North Korea diplomacy stalled

impact_points: China, Russia and the United States gain a formal platform for nuclear risk talks and UN reform.
The International Criminal Court faces pressure from the three powers, as its jurisdiction over state officials is questioned.

auto-e7e1223aed13.headline: Russian strikes in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast leave one dead and another hurt
auto-e7e1223aed13.summary:
Russian forces carried out nearly twenty attacks across Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, according to the regional military administration, killing one person and wounding another. Homes, a car, a farm and infrastructure were damaged in the Dnipro and Nikopol districts, including in the city of Nikopol. In Pavlohrad, a business was hit and a 50-year-old woman was injured; she is receiving outpatient treatment.

The attacks were part of a wider overnight and daytime campaign against Ukraine reported by Ukrainian officials, which also included strikes on Kyiv and Kharkiv. In Kursk, Russia's border region, Ukrainian drones injured 11 people the same day, according to the regional governor.

actors.why: Civilian death, injuries and damage to homes and infrastructure from Russian strikes
Kursk region hit by Ukrainian drones, injuring 11 and damaging buildings

impact_points: Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk Oblast faces property damage, a death and injuries from ongoing Russian strikes.
Russia's Kursk region bears casualties and damage from Ukrainian drone attacks on its city centre.

auto-1f91126fd775.headline: Denmark expels Russian defence attaché over alleged plot against Ukrainian rapper
auto-1f91126fd775.summary:
Denmark is expelling Russia's defence attaché after prosecutors and intelligence services linked a failed plot to kill a Ukrainian-American rapper in Copenhagen to Russian intelligence. Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said the attaché must leave within seven days. Two Danish men, reportedly tied to the criminal gang Loyal to Familia, have been charged and held in custody; both have reportedly pleaded not guilty. The rapper, Kyivstoner, had cancelled a Danish concert after being warned of a threat to his life.

Denmark's intelligence service says the plot was planned and initiated by Russian services. Police have also announced a nationwide crackdown on the gang. Moscow's response was not reported in the coverage provided.

actors.why: Expels Russian attaché; faces a plot on its soil and a gang crackdown
Accused of the plot and expelling its defence attaché from Denmark
Its citizen-rapper was targeted; the case adds to Ukraine-related tensions in Europe
Europe-Russia tensions rise; the case reflects wider security concerns across the bloc

impact_points: Denmark faces further tension with Russia after accusing Moscow of a plot on Danish soil.
Russia loses a defence attaché, a diplomatic setback in its relations with Copenhagen and wider Europe.

auto-570e9419a8f3.headline: China, Russia and US leaders issue joint declaration after Shenzhen summit
auto-570e9419a8f3.summary:
Leaders of China, Russia and the United States met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026, for a first trilateral summit and then released a joint declaration toward peace. The three presidents said they were committed to strategic stability and international security. Their statement pledged to reform the United Nations, which the three permanent Security Council members said should respond more effectively to global challenges.

The declaration also said the three countries would expand production and supply of refined petroleum products and stressed the importance of stable energy flows. It added that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and announced a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation.

actors.why: Hosted the summit and co-signed a declaration backing stability and UN reform
Co-signed declaration on energy supply and nuclear risk dialogue
Joined joint commitments on UN reform, energy flows and nuclear dialogue

impact_points: China, Russia and the United States gain a formal framework for coordinating on UN reform, energy supply and nuclear risk.
Global energy markets and nations dependent on fuel supplies could benefit from the stated commitment to stable energy flows.

auto-598eeef22c7c.headline: UN talks on lethal autonomous weapons end with rules pledge, no binding commitment
auto-598eeef22c7c.summary: After five days of talks in Geneva under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, states agreed to keep working toward rules on lethal autonomous weapons, with new rules targeted within two years. Russia slowed the process, and the United States and Israel also opposed a firm, legally binding outcome. Around 100 countries had backed binding rules on a short timeline, but the final text left open whether any future measures would be binding. Campaigners and the UN secretary-general had pressed for stronger action.

actors.why: Russia slowed talks and resisted binding rules, keeping its options open
Washington opposed binding rules and proposed a five-year timeline, avoiding constraints
Israel opposed binding rules, so no firm restrictions were agreed
Ukraine has reportedly seen such systems used, and rules remain uncertain

impact_points: Russia, the United States and Israel, which resisted binding limits, keep their military AI development options open.
Ukraine, Sudan and the Middle East, where such weapons are reportedly used, face continued uncertainty over future controls.

auto-ec9d9b542f60.headline: Ukraine says Crimean Bridge is a legitimate target after strikes; Putin rules out talks
auto-ec9d9b542f60.summary:
Ukrainian forces struck the Crimean Bridge, linking occupied Crimea to Russia, on the night of November 17, 2026, damaging a section of its roadway. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the bridge is a legitimate target because Russia occupied Crimea, built the crossing and treats it as Russian territory, and that it will not stand during or after the war. He argued Russia uses it to move military equipment. Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would no longer discuss ceasefires covering energy infrastructure and Black Sea shipping, and vowed retaliation.

Reports say Ukraine used Ruta missiles made by a Dutch firm, Destinus, which confirmed its weapons were used. Days later a Russian drone crashed near the Dutch Embassy in Kyiv, slightly damaging the building.

actors.why: Bridge damaged, supply route disrupted, and Putin rejected ceasefire talks
Strike responds to Russian attacks; Moscow now vows retaliation and refuses talks
Dutch-made Ruta missiles used in strike; embassy hit by a Russian drone

impact_points: Russia faces disrupted supply routes to its forces in occupied Ukrainian territories, and a prolonged repair effort.
The Netherlands faces scrutiny over Destinus weapons, and its embassy in Kyiv was hit by debris from a drone.
Ukraine faces Russian retaliation threats and no prospect of an energy ceasefire for now.
Civilians in Ukraine face continued Russian strikes on energy and transport infrastructure.

auto-99357a355ab4.headline: Ocean campaigner swims near Hormuz tanker fires to warn of pollution
auto-99357a355ab4.summary:
Ocean campaigner Lewis Pugh, a UN Patron of the Oceans, swam off Oman's Musandam Peninsula in the Strait of Hormuz, in sight of burning ships and smoke plumes. Two explosions shook the area about 20 minutes into his first swim, and an oil tanker caught fire roughly four kilometres away, so he paused the attempt. The next day he saw another vessel in flames while swimming the waterway again.

Pugh warned that pollution from damaged tankers could harm coral reefs, mangroves and coastal ecosystems for decades. He said the war must end, the strait must reopen and the spill must be cleaned up.

actors.why: Coastal ecosystems and waters near Musandam face pollution from burning, damaged tankers
Regional war and strait disruption tied to Iran's conflict; environmental fallout reported
Gulf shipping through Hormuz disrupted, adding pressure on regional trade

impact_points: Oman faces coastal pollution threats to its reefs, mangroves and wildlife, which could persist for decades.
Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is disrupted, with tankers damaged and the waterway effectively closed.

auto-ca837eb81180.headline: Putin rejects energy and sea truce after Ukraine hits Crimea bridge
auto-ca837eb81180.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow will retaliate for Ukrainian strikes on the bridge linking Russia to Crimea, and that he is dropping any idea of a mutual moratorium on attacks on energy facilities and shipping. Speaking in Shenzhen after meetings with the Chinese and U.S. leaders, he said he had asked his Security Council to consider a possible halt to attacks at sea and on energy sites. The comments followed the third Ukrainian strike on the bridge in a week, which briefly suspended train services. Separately, Ukraine's General Staff said it hit a Russian ammunition depot in occupied Crimea, two command posts in Zaporizhzhia and Donetsk, and a road bridge near Luhansk, while Crimea faces widespread power outages.

actors.why: Bridge strikes and power outages hurt; Putin rejects truce and vows retaliation
Strikes disrupt Russian supply routes and depots, though Moscow vows retaliation
Hosted Putin's talks in Shenzhen, positioning itself as a diplomatic venue
Held talks with Putin in Shenzhen; the truce proposal stalled

impact_points: Russia faces retaliation threats and rejected a truce on energy and shipping attacks, raising escalation risks.
Ukraine continues striking Crimea and supply routes, while occupied Crimea suffers blackouts and disrupted military logistics.

auto-c587510a9e60.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen; Ukraine and Europe sidelined
auto-c587510a9e60.summary:
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, and pledged to increase refined petroleum supplies amid the Iran and Ukraine wars. Putin called the exchange open and candid, saying the leaders covered Ukraine, nuclear risks, maritime security and international institutions. Analysts doubt the energy pledge can work, citing limited US refining spare capacity, Russian refinery damage from Ukrainian drone strikes and disrupted Chinese crude imports.

Ukraine was discussed without Kyiv or European leaders present, drawing criticism from European capitals that rejected a Yalta-style carve-up of the country.

actors.why: Discussed without Kyiv present; faces pressure toward concessions in peace push.
Putin gains a diplomatic platform and says talks opened future agreements.
Trump pushes a peace deal by January and pledges more fuel supply.
Hosted the summit and positions itself as a power broker with Washington and Moscow.
European leaders were excluded and reject the Yalta-style format for Ukraine.

impact_points: Ukraine is left out of talks on its own war, facing possible pressure to make territorial concessions.
European allies, sidelined from the discussions, are pressed by Washington over billions in Ukraine aid.

auto-b24d2012f200.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold Shenzhen summit with few concrete outcomes
auto-b24d2012f200.summary:
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the APEC forum on Thursday, November 19. The three leaders issued a symbolic declaration that nuclear war should never be fought, but announced no arms control talks and no progress on Iran, Ukraine, Taiwan, trade or artificial intelligence. Trump said afterward that the Korean Peninsula and the war in Ukraine had been discussed, without giving details.

Analysts said the meeting highlighted the limits of Trump's personal style of diplomacy, while Xi and Putin gained visibility. European leaders, excluded from the talks, voiced frustration, and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the meeting mainly a photo opportunity.

actors.why: Summit yielded few results and weakened Trump's standing as his term ends
Xi hosted the gathering and gained diplomatic prestige
Putin appeared on par with the top leaders without major concessions
Fears of great-power deals over Ukraine without Kyiv's participation
Merz criticised Europe's exclusion from the Shenzhen talks

impact_points: The United States faces criticism that Trump's summit delivered little despite his claims of success.
Ukraine and European allies worry that great-power talks may shape outcomes without their participation.

auto-6046a4650122.headline: Italian workers and students march nationwide over pay, living costs and defence spending
auto-6046a4650122.summary:
Tens of thousands of workers and students marched in more than 100 Italian cities during a 24-hour general strike. The walkout, called by the CGIL union with grassroots unions such as Cobas, disrupted schools, hospitals and public transport. Protesters in Rome, Milan, Turin, Naples and Palermo demanded higher wages, stronger social protections and less spending on defence.

The action coincided with an international student protest day in over 45 cities and a wider European day of action on living costs, military spending and climate. Demonstrators criticised the government's handling of energy bills, and some called for it to resign. CGIL leader Maurizio Landini called for a sweeping reform of Italy's social and economic model.

actors.why: Nationwide strike disrupts services and pressures government over wages and costs
Coordinated European day of action highlights defence spending and living cost concerns

impact_points: Italy's government faces mounting pressure over energy bills, wages and public spending priorities.
Workers, students and public service users face disruption, while Europe-wide protests highlight shared concerns over defence spending.

auto-5dba848c7832.headline: EU and Indonesia finalise trade and investment pacts, pending parliamentary approval
auto-5dba848c7832.summary: The European Union and Indonesia have approved a trade agreement and a separate investment protection pact after roughly a decade of negotiations. The deals would remove tariffs on about 95 to 98.5 percent of goods traded between the two sides, with roughly 80 percent of cuts taking effect at entry into force and the rest phased in over five years. The European Commission projects EU exports to Indonesia rising nearly 40 percent within 15 years and savings of around 600 million euros a year in duties. The agreements still require signature, European Parliament approval and Indonesian ratification, and could apply from early next year.

actors.why: Gains tariff-free EU market access and investment protections, but faces graduation from EU preferences
Secures lower duties for exporters and diversifies trade amid US tariff volatility

impact_points: Indonesia gains tariff-free access to EU markets and investment protections, though it loses preferential EU tariffs when it graduates from the scheme in 2027.
EU machinery, motor vehicle and small business exporters gain lower duties and new access to Indonesian markets, saving over 600 million euros yearly.

auto-6fee20989866.headline: Mexican forces arrest Sinaloa cartel leader, sparking deadly unrest
auto-6fee20989866.summary:
Mexican military and security forces arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro', in Guasave, Sinaloa, on the night of 20 November. Meza Flores, who leads a cartel also called the Guasave Cartel and was on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted list, was taken after an exchange of gunfire. Mexican authorities said US intelligence contributed to the operation, though details of the cooperation were not disclosed.

The arrest was followed by shootings, burning vehicles and roadblocks, and residents were urged to stay indoors. Gunfire interrupted a baseball game, and no reliable overall casualty figure was established in early reports.

actors.why: Captured a major cartel leader but faced violent unrest in Guasave
Its FBI most-wanted fugitive was captured, with US intelligence contributing

impact_points: Mexico gains a major security success, though rival cartels may exploit any resulting power vacuum in Sinaloa.
The United States sees its FBI most-wanted fugitive detained, reflecting intelligence cooperation with Mexico against cross-border drug trafficking.

auto-a8df939bf3a1.headline: Ukraine's NATO bid revived as allies meet in Berlin
auto-a8df939bf3a1.summary:
Ukraine's NATO membership is back on the agenda after a Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, co-hosted by France, Germany and the UK, with President Zelenskyy attending. French President Macron urged allies to speed up delivery of air defence systems and to reopen the question of Ukraine's accession, citing Russia's maximalist position. Zelenskyy said membership would offer the clearest guarantees, but that it is too early to decide, as everything depends on how and when the war ends.

The discussions came hours after a trilateral summit in China between Trump, Putin and Xi, and reports say the US is open to a guarantee similar to NATO's mutual defence clause. Zelenskyy said a real guarantee would mean US or European forces and bases on Ukrainian soil. Germany expects new peace talks soon, possibly in the UAE.

Faces stronger Western resolve and talk of Ukraine's NATO accession
Macron leads push to revisit Ukraine's NATO accession and air defence

Open to a NATO-style guarantee but says it must serve American interests

impact_points: Ukraine would gain stronger security guarantees if NATO membership advanced, though timing remains uncertain.
Russia faces a firmer European and Western stance, with allies signalling that its position will not shape Ukraine's future.

auto-806faf36e9ed.headline: Russian missiles and drone fall in Poland during massive strike on Ukraine
auto-806faf36e9ed.summary:
During a large overnight Russian attack on Ukraine on November 20, two missiles and a jet-powered drone came down on Polish territory in the southeast, Poland's defence minister said. One missile is believed to have landed about 50km from the Ukrainian border, close to where European troops were holding a military exercise. No injuries or damage were reported. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the incident an apparent intentional provocation by Moscow, while analysts see it as part of a wider pattern of Russian incursions testing NATO's response.

The episode came as Ukraine faced one of the heaviest bombardments of the war, with Kyiv's bridges and railway stations also hit, and as US envoys pushed new peace talks that Moscow rejected on Ukraine's NATO-style guarantees.

actors.why: Missiles and drone fell on its soil, prompting provocation accusations and air defence activation
Faced a massive strike of hundreds of drones and missiles, killing civilians
Accused of deliberate provocation, but its strikes continue and talks on Ukraine remain stalled
Its coalition exercise in Poland was overshadowed, and its security role for Ukraine is being debated

impact_points: Poland faces a direct spillover of the war and must weigh how to respond within NATO.
NATO allies face a test of Article 5 limits as Russia probes their airspace and defences.

auto-03cfc80fa947.headline: Somalia orders UAE envoy out and recalls its own ambassador from Abu Dhabi
auto-03cfc80fa947.summary:
Somalia has told the United Arab Emirati ambassador to leave within 72 hours and has pulled its own envoy back from Abu Dhabi. Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud announced the move at a news conference in Mogadishu, describing an "open invasion" against Somalia's sovereignty and unity and warning of measures against anyone cooperating with the UAE. The UAE foreign ministry did not immediately respond, while a senior Emirati adviser condemned the remarks.

The move follows accusations from President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud that the UAE has built military bases outside national security structures, funded armed groups and opponents of the central government, and interfered in internal affairs. Ties have been strained for years over the UAE's support for Somaliland, and worsened in January when Somalia annulled agreements with the UAE on ports, security and defence.

actors.why: Expels UAE envoy and recalls its ambassador, deepening diplomatic isolation and tensions
Ambassador expelled and publicly condemned, facing a major diplomatic setback with Mogadishu

impact_points: Somalia faces a sharp diplomatic rupture with the UAE, losing a key foreign partner while escalating accusations of interference.
The UAE faces expulsion of its ambassador and public condemnation, deepening a dispute that already involves Somaliland and cancelled port and security deals.

auto-551e96a7b4e2.headline: Trump's Asia trip ends without a Kim meeting as Pyongyang stays silent
auto-551e96a7b4e2.summary:
US President Donald Trump repeatedly sought a meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his Asia tour this week, but Kim did not respond and no encounter took place. Kim was instead shown in state media visiting a ski resort, a sacred mountain and a naval university. Trump left Asia after a trilateral summit with the leaders of China and Russia, saying he was too busy and that a meeting would happen at some point.

Analysts doubt that real contacts preceded the offer. They note that Pyongyang is unlikely to engage unless Washington moves toward recognising it as a nuclear state, while the US still demands denuclearisation. North Korea's growing support from Russia and China reduces its need to talk with Washington, though experts say a future meeting remains possible.

actors.why: Trump's outreach to Kim failed, leaving denuclearisation talks stalled
Kim avoided engagement, keeping sanctions and isolation but gaining leverage
Closer ties with Pyongyang and a trilateral summit with Trump strengthen its position
Military and economic support to Pyongyang deepens ties tied to the Ukraine war
Seoul backs denuclearisation and faces a stalled peace track with the North
Tokyo joins Washington and Seoul in demanding complete denuclearisation

impact_points: The United States faces a stalled diplomatic push, as Trump's overture to Kim produced no meeting or response.
North Korea gains room to rely on Russia and China, reducing its incentive to negotiate with Washington on its nuclear programme.

auto-92f04b4eb84d.headline: US Central Command rejects Iranian claim of striking F-16 over Gulf
auto-92f04b4eb84d.summary:
US Central Command has rejected an Iranian claim that its air defences fired a missile at a US F-16 over the Gulf, damaging the jet and forcing an emergency landing. Iranian state media had reported the strike on Friday evening, saying the aircraft aborted its mission and landed at a nearby airport. CENTCOM said Iran did not attack an F-16 at all and that all US fighter jets in the region were safe and accounted for.

Iran has made similar claims during the conflict about shooting down or damaging US aircraft, and Washington has denied each one. The wider war began in February when the United States and Israel attacked Iran and has since spread across the Middle East, killing thousands and disrupting shipping and energy prices.

actors.why: Denies claimed hit; fighters safe, but facing an Iranian propaganda narrative
Claims air defences hit a US jet; claim unverified and publicly disputed
Co-attacker of Iran in the war that has spread regionally

Iran is using its claims of downing or damaging US aircraft as a public narrative, though Washington disputes each one.

auto-58cd31ad06e0.headline: Former Italian police chief found dead while under investigation over 1992 bombing
auto-58cd31ad06e0.summary: A former senior Italian police official, who had been under investigation over the 1992 bombing that killed a prominent anti-mafia judge, was found dead, apparently by suicide. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni publicly expressed shock at the death. The man had been facing an inquiry into the attack, which is one of the most notorious mafia killings in Italy's recent history. The case remains a sensitive part of the country's efforts to confront organised crime.

actors.why: Domestic judicial and political fallout from the death of a suspect in a mafia case

impact_points: Italy's government faces renewed scrutiny over how it handles long-running investigations into mafia-linked crimes.
Families of the bombing victims and wider public trust in the justice process may be affected by the loss of a suspect before trial.

auto-9384b958e84b.headline: Tehran's top diplomat says Beijing and Moscow back Iran's nuclear doctrine
auto-9384b958e84b.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said China and Russia oppose changing Tehran's nuclear doctrine, in an interview published Saturday by the state-run Iran Daily. He described the question as serious and divisive at home, with supporters and opponents of a shift. Some hardliners argue a change could open the way to a nuclear weapon as a deterrent. Araghchi said the official position has not changed. Iran has restricted the IAEA from inspecting its nuclear sites, and the UN watchdog recently urged incremental steps to restore access. Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father after a February US-Israeli strike, has not issued a decree altering the fatwa.

Beijing is aligned with Tehran in opposing a doctrine change
Moscow is aligned with Tehran in opposing a doctrine change
Iran's nuclear stance remains a concern after wars with Israel
Iranian nuclear facilities were attacked and the nuclear dispute remains unresolved

impact_points: Iran faces domestic pressure over its nuclear doctrine while seeking backing from Beijing and Moscow.
China and Russia, Iran's strategic partners, are shown opposing any shift away from the current nuclear stance.

auto-6ff79d7df86d.headline: Russian missile strikes hit Kyiv bridges and power, killing eight across Ukraine
auto-6ff79d7df86d.summary:
Russia launched a large overnight barrage on Ukraine, with Kyiv's Dnipro River bridges and power infrastructure among the targets. Ukrainian officials said eight people were killed, including six in Kyiv and two in Lviv, and dozens were wounded. Moscow framed the attack as retaliation for Ukraine's strikes on the Kerch Strait bridge linking Russia with Crimea, and Russia's Defence Ministry said it targeted bridges used to move military equipment.

Poland said three objects, likely two missiles and a drone, entered its airspace during the attack, which Warsaw called a Russian provocation. The strikes came as US-led ceasefire mediation made little visible progress.

actors.why: Deadly strikes damaged bridges, power plants and civilian sites across Ukraine
Strikes retaliated for Kerch bridge damage but ceasefire talks stall
Missiles or drone entered Polish airspace during the attack
US-led mediation efforts show little progress after the attacks
Austrian embassy in Kyiv was damaged, though staff were unhurt

impact_points: Ukraine faces deaths, damaged bridges and power outages across Kyiv and about ten regions.
Poland faces airspace incursions that its defence minister described as a deliberate Russian provocation.

auto-0f33cd1783a6.headline: Explosion in Riyadh follows Houthi strike on city's tallest tower
auto-0f33cd1783a6.summary:
A loud blast was heard in Riyadh late on Friday, shortly after Saudi civil defence issued a danger alert and then said the threat had passed. The cause was not immediately clear. It came a day after a Houthi attack damaged the Public Investment Fund tower, the capital's tallest building, which houses Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund. Saudi-led coalition forces said they had dealt with a missile threat, and Yemen's Houthis have escalated strikes on Saudi airports, energy sites and offices in recent weeks.

The Saudi-led coalition has responded with strikes on Houthi-held areas of Yemen, where fighting resumed after a long ceasefire. The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed in the latest round.

actors.why: Capital's tallest tower damaged and repeated missile attacks on infrastructure
Renewed war, Saudi airstrikes and over 1,600 killed nationwide

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces repeated missile and drone attacks on its capital, airports, energy assets and financial district.
Yemen faces renewed fighting, Saudi airstrikes and a growing humanitarian toll as Houthi forces advance toward Aden.
